articleTitle: Experimental Harmonic Evaluation for Induction Motor Drive with Active LC Low-Pass-Filter via IRM-ILQ Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Inverters used for induction motors often operate in pulse width modulation (PWM) mode, and the output voltage of PWM inverters contains many harmonic components due to switching. Harmonics in the inverter output voltage can cause electromagnetic interference problems, torque ripples, and noise. Additionally, since motors are inherently wideband loads, LC filters with resonance phenomena cause serious instability. It is very difficult to achieve stable control with good transient response by conventional PI control as a simple-input-simple-output system, because AC motor drive systems with LC filters have multidimensional dynamics. Therefore, it is essential to introduce multivariable control based on modern control theory that can deal with multi-input-multi-output systems. The control method has been proposed, in which an actively controlled LC low-pass filter (LC-LPF) can significantly reduce harmonic distortion of motor voltages due to the PWM modulation and can control the torque and flux of motor at high response and with high accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been indicated by simulation and experiments by applying it to the control of an induction motor and a synchronous motor. In this research, the effectiveness of the LC- LPF is shown through harmonic analysis of the phase voltage.

articleTitle: Harmonics Analysis and Evaluation for Active LC-LPF Attached PMSM Drive by IRM-ILQ Control Through Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper describes analysis and evaluation of harmonics reduction for Active LC Low Pass Filter (LC-LPF) attached Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SPMSM) drive operated by IRM-ILQ (Inverse Reference Model - Inverse Linear Quadratic) current control. Harmonics due to high-speed switching of inverter should be reduced since it brings not only low efficiency motor drive such as torque ripple, also cause electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems. Those problems will be solved by appending LC-LPF though, LC resonant phenomena against inverter's carrier frequency and motor's operating frequency should be considered. The IRM-ILQ control is classified into modern control methods and simultaneously transacts multiple variables. Owing to it, stable motor drive can be realized even though LC-LPF is attached. In experiments, degrees of the harmonics reduction by Active LC-LPF are evaluated via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and confirmed 2 % of voltage distortion on average in rated speed region.

articleTitle: A Proposal of Speed Sensorless Control Based on IRM-ILQ Control for SPMSM Drive with Active LC Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Generally, a position detector has been used to drive the Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SPMSM), because the current and voltage must be controlled according to the magnetic pole position of the rotor. However, using a position detector causes problems such as more expensive and lower reliability due to position detector failure. Therefore, the speed sensor-less control, which estimates the magnetic pole position from voltage and current without using a position detector, is required. Harmonic components in the output voltage waveform of the PWM inverter used to drive the SPMSM can cause problems such as Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). Harmonic components can be suppressed by using an LC filter. In addition, IRM-ILQ control, which combines modern control theory's Inverse Linear Quadratic (ILQ) control and Inverse Reference Model (IRM), can achieve stable and robust SPMSM drive despite with LC filter. In this paper, robustness of speed sensorless control based on IRM-ILQ current control for SPMSM with active LC filter is described. In simulation, the proposed method allows stable control even when there are parameter errors.

articleTitle: A Proposal of Optimal Current Control for Three-Phase Grid-Connected Inverter with LCL-Filter via IRM-ILQ Method
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel grid-connected inverter with LCL filters applied to IRM-ILQ (Inverse Reference Model - Inverse Linear Quadratic) control strategy. The IRM, which is feed-forward control, allows for realizing the fast response to current control without delay. The ILQ control gives an analytical solution for optimal control, and response speed in the closed-loop system is controlled. The IRM-ILQ control method simultaneously provides target tracking and error convergence, basically the IRM-ILQ control is the two-degree of freedom control. Owing to it, it can suppress surge current less than 58.6% during momentary power failure and make power factor keep unity even when command current value changes. The proposed grid-connected inverter is confirmed current tracking and an impressive adaptability to varying amplitude and phase of current by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Development of High-Quality High-efficiency High-Reliability 6.6kV 12MVA Multiple Power Compensator
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In order to curb climate change and advance towards a sustainable society, there is a shift from fossil fuels such as coal and oil to renewable energy sources like solar power and wind power. However, most renewable energies are challenging to obtain stably, and incidents such as grid voltage drops are common. Furthermore, power grid supply accidents are inevitable due to natural disasters like lightning, heavy wind or snow. It has been reported that critical facilities have suffered from momentary drops or outages of the power grid. For instance, even momentary power failure of about 10 milliseconds can cause significant damage to production lines in the semiconductor manufacturing industry, where precision processing is conducted [1]. In response to this situation, we have developed a Multiple Power Compensator (MPC) with high quality, high efficiency, and high reliability. The MPC can safeguard the power supplies of various vital facilities essential to our daily lives, including data centers, airlines, traffic control systems, factories, etc., from power failures such as momentary drops or blackouts at the power grid transmission distribution systems. This paper presents the techniques for achieving high-quality, high-efficiency and high-reliability of the MPC and presents the test results.

articleTitle: Fuel Cell-Battery Power Management System for eVTOL Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A power management system (PMS) for hybrid energy storages using a fuel cell and battery is proposed for the propulsion of an electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) drone. The concept and structure of the proposed PMS are first presented. The power electronic converters for the proposed PMS and their control methods for efficiently using the fuel cell and battery storages for the eVTOL drone are discussed. The experimental and simulation results for the converters and PMS are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed PMS.

articleTitle: Assessment of Reliability Indicators of Power Supply Systems with Two-Transformer Substations During Technical and Economic Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The proposed article is devoted to the assessment of reliability parameters of in-plant power supply systems with 10/0.4 kV double-transformer substations. The paper studies the reliability of the power supply system for the following variants of two-transformer substation schemes: without redundancy; with redundancy when installing a sectional switch; with double redundancy: when installing a sectional switch and a redundant jumper at 0.4 kV. The graphical dependences of operating time to failure of power supply schemes with two-transformer substations on different rated capacity of shop transformers for three variants have been obtained: without redundancy; with redundancy; with double redundancy. The optimum condition is the use of a smaller number of transformer substations, and, accordingly, transformers, while maintaining the value of load factor 0.8. When comparing the graphs, it was found that the longest MTBF is achieved with double redundancy, and the shortest - with no redundancy. The results of the research can be recommended for use in the process of designing systems of in-plant power supply to assess and improve the reliability and efficiency of equipment operation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Controlled Parallel DC-DC Converter for Edge Server
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a parallel dc-dc converter with adaptive control for edge servers, which is developed by a project of the Ministry of the Environment of Japan aimed for achieving carbon neutrality. A prototype of a 2 kW full bridge converter using GaN FETs has up to 96.8% power efficiency. Also, adaptive control is used for 8 kW four-parallel dc-dc converters to realize high power efficiency in the whole load range. As a simulation result of the adaptive controlled parallel dc-dc converter, it is shown that the power loss can be reduced by up to 56%.

articleTitle: Control of a Simple High-Frequency Isolated Single-Phase AC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new simple circuit structure and a control theory of high-frequency isolated single-phase AC-DC converter. In the proposed circuit, AC power source charges the capacitor by half-bridge circuit. Therefore, the number of switching elements can be decreased. Furthermore, total power factor of transformer can be improved by using the LC resonance, then the size of transformer can be smaller. The control theory of the proposed circuit is confirmed by experiments.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Accuracy for Partial Shading Detection in Series-Parallel Configuration of Photovoltaic Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Photovoltaic Generation Systems (PVGSs) are frequently impacted by Partial Shading (PS) conditions, which can significantly reduce their power output. The maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) methods can enhance PVGS performance. MPPT's effectiveness can be improved considerably with PS Detection (PSD) results, which help select the most suitable MPPT strategy. Most PSD methods investigate a PVGS with the series configuration; however, PVGSs are usually arranged in series-parallel, total-cross-tied, series-parallel with total-cross-tied configurations, etc. The applicability of existing PSD methods in different PVGS configurations requires in-depth explorations. Therefore, this paper investigates the efficiency and accuracy of a PSD in the series-parallel configuration of PVGSs. The PSD method proposed in this paper estimates the solar irradiance and temperature of a PVGS based on two measured voltage and current sets. A PS Factor (PSF) is then used to detect whether a PS occurs. This paper uses a series-parallel PVGS composed of 5x5 PV panels to verify the proposed PSD method. Different PS patterns, including column, row, diagonal, and corner, are examined for the PVGS. Experimental results show that for both two-row and corner PS patterns, the proposed method can efficiently and accurately detect whether a PS occurs in 3s with a tracking time interval of 1s. Simulation results show that the PSD accuracies of single-row and diagonal PSs reach 100%, corner PS reach 99.8%, and single-column PSs reach 89.74% under solar irradiance variations.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of the Simulation Scheme Estimating the Freewheeling Transistor Surge Voltage During the Switching-Side One Turn-on Transient in a Half-Bridge Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The simulation scheme is experimentally validated to estimate the freewheeling device surge voltage when the switching device is turned on in a half-bridge circuit. The simulation scheme was previously proposed by the authors, where the freewheeling device is equivalent to a capacitance, switching device operates as a variable voltage source, and there is a stray inductance. This approach is characterized by taking into account the voltage dependence of the capacitance and the transient resistance of the switching device. The comparison of simulated and measured surge voltage showed that it was well estimated by considering the effects of both the capacitance and the resistance of the devices, and therefore this fact supports the validity of our proposed simulation scheme.

articleTitle: Optimising Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging Systems Using Neural Networks to Enable Free-Position Parking
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper explores wireless power transfer (WPT) systems for public electric vehicle charging, focusing on optimising the transmitter design to enhance interoperability across various receiver coil geometries and alignment conditions. Due to the complex non-linear relationships inherent to WPT systems, traditional optimisation methods are computationally expensive. Therefore, this study proposes an approach using artificial neural networks (ANNs) trained on finite element method (FEM) data to develop a surrogate model of the WPT system. This model is integrated into a blackbox optimisation solver, enabling faster identification of improved transmitter designs. The proposed method achieves computational speeds 6,000 times faster than traditional FEM simulations, with post-validation on the final solutions verifying prediction errors below 0.6%. The results demonstrate a significant acceleration in the optimisation process, establishing this method as an effective framework for developing practical WPT systems for public charging applications.

articleTitle: Wind-Lens Effect in Micro Wind Power Plant Installed in Airflow Duct
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wind power generation using duct airflow has been considered as an energy-harvesting source to power wireless sensor terminals. According to previous studies, wind power generation in ducts connected to a diffuser is stable, and use of a diffuser increases the power output. Thus, in this study, we analyzed the wind-lens effect in micro wind power plants installed in an airflow duct to use duct airflow as an energy source. Experimental findings of the study showed that the output power increased when a diffuser was connected to the exhaust port of the duct. Without a diffuser, the output power was proportional to the cube of the air velocity, and the application of a diffuser resulted in a higher output power. When the diffuser was connected, the output power characteristics were evaluated with respect to the position of the rotor inside the duct. Experimental results showed that the rotor maximized output power when it was placed inside the duct. Thus, the diffuser was found as an effective method for increasing the output power in duct-based micro wind power generation.

articleTitle: PV Power Generation System Recently Installed on Railway Station Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper describes the photovoltaic (PV) power generation system in railway stations of East Japan Railway Company (JR East). The specifications and configurations regarding newly constructed Takanawa Gateway station and renovated Shimbashi and Sendagaya station are reported. The amount of power generation is also introduced for Takanawa Gateway station.

articleTitle: Current Status of Medium-Term and Long-Term Wind Power Forecasting in the Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wind energy integration into the existing energy generation systems is an important issue. Wind energy is variable and intermittent over various time scales as it depends on weather conditions. Therefore, wind power forecasting is critical for load tracking, pre-dispatching, maintenance scheduling and energy trading. In order to perform these tasks, numerous wind power forecasting studies have been conducted in the literature. In this paper, the current status of medium-term and long-term wind power forecasting is reviewed considering different criteria. Many guiding results have been achieved from the literature. Particularly, it is noteworthy that novel hybrid forecasting models have been created by combining the strengths of individual forecasting models in the current literature.

articleTitle: Digitally Controlled Peak Current Mode DC-DC Converter for Plasma Thruster in Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Remote sensing using satellites is essential to realize carbon neutrality. The Hall thruster, a type of plasma thruster, is a strong candidate as a propulsion system for various satellites. Hall thrusters require an anode power supply to discharge and accelerate ions. The anode power supply also requires a wide output range. This paper proposes a DC-DC converter with digital peak current mode control. Simulation results show good steady-state characteristics in the 100 to 200 V output range from 2 to 7.5 A. Simulations reveal that the proposed converter has acceptable load regulation over the output range and offers better stability than conventional methods. The experimental results for the peak current detection agree with the prediction by considering the offset of the threshold voltage and the parasitic capacitance of the circuit. Thus, the converter is suitable for a wide range of anode power supplies used in Hall thruster systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Virtual Power Plant Generation Forecasting in Japan Using Fuzzy Decision Support and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Models
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Recursive prediction technique used in bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks often struggles with long-term prediction accuracy. This study introduces a fuzzy decision support system (FDSS) that improves long-term forecasts by combining K-means clustering and fuzzy membership values. The FDSS classifies daily peak power generation of a virtual power plant into five weather types-rainy, overcast, partly cloudy, cloudy, and sunny- and generates FDSS test data for the BiLSTM model. The results indicate that the proposed model achieves a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE) of 49% for 38-hour ahead predictions, outperforming the BiLSTM and LSTM models with a sMAPE of 62% and 64%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Material Choice of High Frequency Transformers for Solid State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The Solid-State Transformer (SST) is gaining attention as a next-generation transformer, serving as a potential replacement for traditional pole-mounted transformers. The selection of magnetic materials aimed at miniaturization and loss reduction is a critical issue. In this paper, the properties of several candidate materials are measured to identify those suitable for the SST core, followed by the design based on the proposed model specifications. Finite element analysis is employed to calculate the volume and losses for each material, and the trade-offs are evaluated to determine the optimal magnetic material. Furthermore, a prototype transformer is designed using the selected material, and its performance is evaluated.

articleTitle: Steady State Characteristics of Push-Pull Converter with Asymmetric Operation for Wide Input Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, the push-pull converter with asymmetrical operation is investigated for applying wide input voltage range. A switch is driven by asymmetrical gate waveforms in the investigated operation, and the primary side of the push-pull converter is configured two conversion circuits. Therefore, two different conversion ratios can be obtained by different numbers of turns in each circuit, and this method enables to handle the wide input voltage range. The operation principle and steady state characteristics are analytically and experimentally examined in this paper. As a result, the operating principle of the converter with asymmetrical operation has been analytically clarified, and it has been experimentally confirmed. Moreover, the operation limit of this converter has also been analytically and experimentally confirmed. The output voltage can be regulated 48V for all input voltage range of 100 to 400V, and the maximum efficiency is achieved 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in low input voltage range.

articleTitle: A Study on the Compensation Calculation Model for Utilizing Residential Storage Batteries to Alleviate Grid Congestion
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study focuses on a compensation calculation model for utilizing residential storage batteries to alleviate grid congestion caused by increased renewable energy generation, particularly solar power. Currently, residential storage batteries are mainly used to reduce electricity bills. The model calculates the marginal kW compensation, considering opportunity loss of reducing the electricity bills and the shortfall in the kWh compensation due to the difference in the forecast and confirmed notifications. Simulations based on past consumption, generation data, and market prices are conducted to evaluate the marginal kW compensation. The results show the potential for economically utilizing residential storage batteries to alleviate grid congestion.

articleTitle: From Data to Energy Management: Evaluating and Analysis of Univariate and Multivariate AI Models for Photovoltaic Systems in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Protecting our environment necessitates a significant shift towards renewable energy sources. Among these, photovoltaic (PV) energy is one of the most widely used. However, the dependence of this energy on sunlight presents challenges in predicting energy production. So, it is crucial to have methods that allow us to predict the PV energy production of our PV systems. This will enable us to better manage this energy, anticipate energy needs, and optimize the energy supply for Buildings-Integrated PV (BIPV). The data generated by PV systems are time series data (TSD), and tools like Artificial Intelligence (AI) are widely used to predict this type of data. The objective of this study is to explore the performance of various AI models applied to TSD analysis, using both univariate and multivariate approaches. We will then examine their integration into Smart Grids (SG), specifically within a PV system connected to the electrical grid of a BIPV house in Switzerland. The goal is to determine which of these two approaches offers the best efficiency in terms of energy prediction and management within SG. We worked with four machine learning and deep learning models: XGBoost, Random Forest, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a hybrid model (CNN-LSTM) combining LSTM with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Our proposed SG consists of a PV system connected to the grid and a battery for energy storage. In our future work, we will develop this SG by automating energy management system based on the energy predictions made by our AI model.

articleTitle: Cell balance Control Method for on-board Chargers with Multi-level configurations for PFC and LLC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a method for improving the efficiency and reducing the noise of LLC converters as a feature of LLC converters. And in DCM mode, the rectifier circuit can operate in ZCS mode, so no recovery current flows. However, when applied to a wide range of voltages, such as in an automotive charger, the reactive current may increase. In addition, when the output voltage is low, DCM operation is not possible and recovery current flows, causing a decrease in efficiency. To solve these problems, we present a method that uses multi-level conversion technology to solve these problems. Since this is an in-vehicle charger application, it is configured as an AC-DC converter. We show a control method to balance the load with a PFC converter based on the variation of resonant circuit parameters.

articleTitle: Grid Voltage Control of Energy Storage System Using Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Distributed power sources such as the photovoltaic and the wind power generation are susceptible to weather conditions and their output is unstable, but stable output can be obtained by combining distributed power sources with energy storage devices. Energy storage device requires high-speed control of the power converter in response to fluctuation of generation systems and load for power leveling. This study proposes a DC grid voltage control of the energy storage system with the dual active bridge (DAB) converter to cope with steep fluctuations in the grid. The proposed control is based on the digital deadbeat control method to improve the response of the grid voltage and the output current control method. The operation of the proposed control scheme is verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Switching Instants Optimization for MHz CrM Totem-Pole PFC without Real-Time Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of ZVS-on instants and reduce the calculation burden for digital implementation, a new soft switching control technique without parameter dependent calculations of ZVS-on instants for MHz Totem-Pole PFC is proposed. For traditional soft switching control of Totem-Pole PFC, the calculations heavily depend upon the inductance value and parameters of power devices which are affected by the operation voltage and current conditions. Because of these facts, the accuracy of switching time instants, especially, ZVS-on instants, becomes one of the major concerns. Moreover, the calculation burden is another concern for digital implementation using MCU, especially, for the applications with MHz switching frequency. Simulation and experimental results are presented for confirmation. The specifications include: input voltage = 230 V, output voltage = 400 V and output power = 1.5 kW. The maximum efficiency is 98.6% and ZVS-on can be achieved even the switching frequency is up to mega Hz. The calculation time for conventional method is reduced from 16.69 µs to 3.83 µs using proposed technique. These results fully support the effectiveness of the proposed soft switching control technique.

articleTitle: Variable Off-Time Control for Mixed Conduction Mode Boost PFC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel peak-current-mode based variable off-time control for the boost PFC converter to achieve low input current THD and high power factor across a wide range of loads. The proposed control scheme makes the boost PFC converter operate in part continuous conduction mode (CCM) and part critical conduction mode (CRM) at heavy loads. It adaptively transfers to the full CRM at light loads. The proposed control scheme has the advantage of being simple, and it can be easily implemented in ICs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can maintain low input current THD and high power factor at light loads.

articleTitle: A High-Frequency Flying-capacitor Linear Amplifier for Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems emit leakage magnetic fields due to their operating principle. Thus, reducing electromagnetic field (EMF) harmonics is essential to meet standards such as CISPR. The WPT system with a flying capacitor linear amplifier (FCLA) has been proposed to reduce the EMF. However., the high-frequency operation of the FCLA has not yet been realized. This paper proposes a gate driver unit (GDU) that enables the high-frequency operation of the FCLA with low voltage distortion by feedforward compensation of the gate-source voltage. Experimental results show that the WPT system with a 2-series FCLA prototype reduces odd harmonic components of primary current by up to 16.5 dB compared to the conventional WPT system with a square-wave output inverter.

articleTitle: Impact of Demand-Solar Irradiance Correlation on the Optimal Sizing of ESS for PV Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Photovoltaic generation is highly sensitive to weather changes, resulting in significant diurnal variations. In addition to diurnal variations, energy demand is also influenced by the climate of the demand region. These factors can lead to reduced system stability and profitability, making the integration of Energy Storage System (ESS) with PV farms even more critical. In this context, it is essential to consider the impact of the correlation between solar irradiance and demand on the optimization of ESS capacity and scheduling. This article analyzes the impact of the correlation between irradiance and demand on ESS planning in PV systems, considering three distinct climate scenarios. For this purpose, correlation coefficients are calculated, and the ESS's size and schedule are optimized in each scenario. The optimization focuses on maximizing annual profits by determining the optimal ESS size and daily schedule. The Pearson correlation coefficient is used for correlation analysis, while the Gurobi Optimizer is employed for ESS optimization. In conclusion, the optimal ESS size was derived differently across scenarios with varying correlations, suggesting that considering the solar irradiance-demand correlation in the installation region when integrating ESS with a PV system could enhance cost efficiency.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Analysis of Branch Prediction for a Processor Tightly Coupled With Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As a preliminary study toward the development of a new processor architecture that achieves high energy efficiency by more closely linking the processor and power supply, this paper implements RISC-V processors with different branch prediction configurations on an FPGA and experimentally evaluates the relationship between branch prediction and energy efficiency. Energy efficiency was quantified by measuring the current during program execution using an oscilloscope. As a result, it was confirmed that the processor with branch prediction reduced the energy consumption by a maximum of approximately 59.4 % compared to the processor without prediction.

articleTitle: Using Vector Space Decomposition for Inter-Turn Short Circuit Modeling and Classification in a Nine- Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces a simplified analytical modeling approach for internal short circuits in permanent magnet synchronous machines. A nine-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine is used as a demonstrator. Based on the fault studied at varying operational conditions, four assumptions are derived from modeling inter-turn short circuits in the machine at hand. A simplified analytical model of the fault based on these assumptions is then derived. The values used for the parametrization of the fault model are ultimately used to conduct a preliminary fault classification. The classification includes the number of shorted turns, the short circuit resistance, and the compromised coil in a phase. The proposed analytical model shows results with good accuracy compared to the finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Voltage Control of Parallel Inverters for Photovoltaic Without Parallel Operation Signal Line
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new disturbance observer-based voltage control of parallel inverters for photovoltaic without parallel operation signal line. Each inverter has no information about the load-sharing ratio and the other inverters connected in parallel at its output. Each inverter compensates the load current to be shared using each disturbance observer and achieves a rapid response through its output voltage control. The inverter compensates for the effects caused by errors in the output voltage sensor gains by allowing a small circulating current to flow. The proposed parallel inverters apply to improve the output voltage waveform on condition of the adjustment control-gain and the rectifier circuit at light load. The proposed method allows a simple capacity increase by connecting only the output terminals. The experimental results in this paper confirms that the validity and the fine voltage response of proposed method without parallel operation signal line.

articleTitle: Self-Excited Synchronous Machines Used for Small Wind Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper discusses the suitability of two self-excited generator variants to be used in small wind power applications. Commonly, self-excited generators are separately excited, from an external dc source. Here, the proposed solutions are excited from the main field source of the machine, i.e., the permanent magnet (PMs). Through rotor's rotation, an induced electromotive force is produced, which is later rectified and partially injected into a supplementary field winding. Thus, no external source is needed to produce electricity. In the paper, the topologies of two self-excited generators are detailed, while the losses (i.e., the iron loss within stator and rotor core) are computed through finite element method (FEM). The performances and the air-gap field variation capability are carefully evaluated for both variants. Thus, through simulations, based on FEM, we will check which variant is best suited for the given application.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Fixed-Time Super Twisting Control for Quadrotors with Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a sliding mode control (SMC) approach with a fixed-time super-twisting reaching law (FxSTRL) for quadrotor systems subjected to uncertainties and disturbances. The proposed SMC scheme utilizes a super-twisting reaching law to ensure convergence to the sliding surface within a fixed time independently of initial conditions, enhancing the robustness and transient performance of the control system. The proposed control rule effectively eliminates the chattering issue associated with SMC and exhibits robust control performance in the presence of actuator faults. The proposed method underwent comprehensive simulation evaluations to assess its trajectory-tracking performance under various conditions, including both the presence and absence of actuator faults. The simulations compared the proposed method's performance against existing control approaches, namely classical SMC. In conclusion, the proposed FxSTRL-based sliding mode controller offers a novel robust control strategy that effectively handles actuator faults, and reduces chattering.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy-Powered BLDC Motor-Based Appliances Based on Supercapacitor-Assisted Converters for DC Homes
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Today solar or wind energy resources are coupled with the AC grid supply in the household using inverters and battery banks. However, the maximum power point tracking-based battery chargers and inverters have significant losses in the renewable-to-AC grid link. By using supercapacitor modules with extra low-frequency power converters, we can increase the end-to-end efficiency of whiteware such as refrigerators, washing machines, dryers, and heat pumps. Given that the modern inverter-driven whiteware carries brush-less DC motors driven by an inverter supplied by an internal DC bus derived from the line frequency AC supply, these systems can be easily powered by a direct DC source for the reduction of losses associated with the renewable energy link in a household. In addition, this could also reduce the converter losses within the white-good. The paper presents the theoretical and experimental details on how commercial whiteware can be easily modified to operate from a DC rail with a supercapacitor module used for the dual purpose of power conversion and energy buffering based on an example of a refrigerator.

articleTitle: Galvanic Isolation Switch Activation Mechanism for Hybrid DC Circuit Breakers Using Very High Current Capability of Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Direct Current Circuit Breakers (DCCBs) are an essential requirement in DC circuits due to the rise of DC microgrids and the growing demand for DC-based renewable energy sources and appliances. Basically there are three types of DCCBs (i) mechanical, (ii) solid-state and (iii) hybrid where solid-state and hybrid DCCBs are constructed based on semiconductor switches. Galvanic isolation is an important factor for circuit breakers in the open state, ensuring safety and facilitating maintenance. In mechanical DCCBs, galvanic isolation can be easily achieved after the fault current is cleared, thanks to the intrinsic property of a mechanical switch. However, for the other two types, additional galvanic isolation is necessary to meet the required safety standards and prevent leakage current, as semiconductor switches do not provide galvanic isolation. This paper proposes a novel technique to activate a galvanic isolation (mechanical) switch after a fault is extinguished, utilizing the high current delivery capability of supercapacitors due to their very low equivalent series resistance. Proper synchronization between fault current extinguishing and galvanic isolation is achieved by using a supercapacitor and simple passive components.

articleTitle: Imbalance and ICA Monitoring for Multiple Battery-Electrolyser Cells in Series
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper investigates imbalance and the application of Incremental Capacity Analysis (ICA) in monitoring lead-acid battery-electrolysers. These are single devices which function as both batteries and electrolysers. The study examines whether traditional monitoring and balancing strategies used in lithium-ion batteries are applicable to battery-electrolysers in series configurations. Findings suggest that cell balancing may not be necessary for systems with low levels of degradation as cell voltages align and electrolysis helps to balance cells further. ICA is employed to generate Incremental Capacity (IC) curves, which are reportedly used to detect subtle changes in battery behavior indicative of degradation. The proportional change method is applied to estimate state of health (SOH), yielding estimations within 7.9% of the actual measured SOH, indicating the potential of ICA as a tool for monitoring health in battery-electrolysers. However, the ICA only works when the battery-electrolyser is functioning as a battery. These findings suggest that, although cell monitoring and active balancing may not be required for minor degradation, the hardware could be useful for long term ICA tracking of degradation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells in Agricultural Areas: Technical and Economic Benefits
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This article analyzes the technical and economic feasibility of implementing Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) in agricultural and rural areas of the coastal region of Ecuador. Challenges in terms of costs, hydrogen storage, and infrastructure are explored. An economic analysis includes highlighting cost components and potential sources of revenue. The findings indicate that while PEMFC technology advancements are urgently needed to overcome existing barriers and maximize return on investment (ROI), immediate action is required to ensure the timely implementation of these advancements.

articleTitle: Development of an Efficient Charging Control System for Pico-Hydro Power Generation Utilizing Multiple Impact Water Wheel (MIWW) with MPPT Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced charging control system for a Multiple Impact Water Wheel (MIWW) used in pico-hydropower generation. The control system maximizes energy conversion efficiency by employing a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, which dynamically adjusts the system's operation based on real-time voltage and current measurements. Unlike traditional methods that rely on monitoring rotational speed, this approach simplifies the system by eliminating the need for speed sensors, thereby reducing costs and enhancing reliability. The control system is structured into four main operational phases: the water turbine acceleration phase, optimal control (MPPT) phase, drooping characteristic suppression phase, and overvoltage protection phase. Each phase is designed to optimize distinct aspects of system performance, ensuring stable and efficient power generation under varying water flow conditions. Experimental validation was conducted by subjecting the system to three different water pressure levels (0.036 MPa, 0.048 MPa, and 0.042 MPa). The results demonstrate that the system successfully maintained stable voltage and current, even during rapid fluctuations in water pressure, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed MPPT algorithm. By addressing the challenges of droop characteristics and overvoltage conditions, the control system ensures the reliability and efficiency of pico-hydropower systems. This research contributes to the development of cost-effective, efficient, and sustainable energy solutions, especially in regions lacking conventional power infrastructure.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power Quality and Losses in Single-Phase H-Bridge Inverters: A Comparative Study of IGBT and GaN Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of a single-phase H-bridge inverter using Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) devices, comparing power quality and efficiency. The primary focus of the study is to evaluate the total harmonic distortion (THD) of voltage and current waveforms and to analyze power losses across different operating frequencies with different values of the output filter inductor. Simulations were carried out using both device technologies to assess their behavior at various switching frequencies. The results indicate that GaN-based inverters exhibit superior performance in terms of lower THD and reduced switching losses, especially at higher operating frequencies, compared to IGBT-based inverters. The findings of this study highlight the trade-offs between power quality, efficiency, and operating frequency, providing insights into the suitability of IGBT and GaN devices for different inverter applications.

articleTitle: Estimated Energy Balance for Shuttle Service of Nursing Home-Collaborated Hospital Assuming EVs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents estimates of the energy balance between power demand, photovoltaic (PV) power generation, and utility power in the case of operating electric vehicle (EV) shuttle services in nursing homes collaborating with hospitals. Reducing power demand is crucial for lowering C02 emissions and mitigating global warming. In particular, hospitals have a high power demand because, hospitals provide medical services to patients around the clock. As a result, the government requires hospitals to save energy by adopting renewable energy sources. The number of hospitals and nursing homes installing PV systems is increasing. Hospitals can reduce their power demand by using PV to charge EV s. Therefore, the number of hospitals and nursing homes installing EV s powered by PV is expected to expand. However, there are few studies on the specific energy-saving effects and energy balance estimates of EV s due to the lack of information on the initial investment and operating costs. Actual driving data and demand data are required to estimate the energy balance. This study estimates the energy balance of using electric vehicles (EVs) for shuttle services in nursing homes collaborating with hospitals. The results show that the installation of EV s powered by PV systems can reduce power demand by 10 %, especially during the first 6 months.

articleTitle: Roles of PV+Storage at Community Centers in Achieving a Level of Distribution Network Resilience After Extreme Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this study, a Time-Sharing Resilience Strategy (TSRS) is implemented to enhance the resilience of a power distribution network in Orlando during outages caused by severe weather events. The strategy involves integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) at a community center (CC), and strategically placing reclosers within the radial network to ensure fair power distribution. The TSRS adjusts service duration based on solar irradiance over a two-day period. Case studies confirm the effectiveness of this strategy in enhancing grid resilience, particularly through the positive impact of PV integration. This framework offers practical guidance for utilities and community planners aiming to enhance power system resilience against rising extreme weather events.

articleTitle: A Study on Locate Method of Series Arc Fault Point in Photovoltaic Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As photovoltaic (PV) systems expand rapidly, safety concerns, particularly related to arc faults, have emerged. Current methods for detecting arc discharges in PV systems measure conducted noise but lack the ability to accurately locate faults, limiting their effectiveness in preventing incidents like fires. This study introduces a novel approach to both detect and locate arc faults by analyzing conducted noise during arc events. By focusing on specific frequency ranges, called “Target bands,” we demonstrate that “Target band 1” consistently detects arc events, while “Target band 2” shows attenuation with increasing distance, allowing for location estimation. The method offers potential for enhancing PV system safety by providing early detection and accurate localization of arc faults, contributing to the prevention of fire risks and improving overall system reliability.

articleTitle: Fluctuation Mitigation Control of Wind Farm with Battery Energy Storage System and Wind Turbines' Curtailment Function
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As variable renewable energy sources such as wind turbines have been integrated into power grids, their intermittency raises concerns about the stable operation of the grids. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is a promising tool to mitigate intermittency; however, its mitigation performance highly depends on a control strategy. This paper proposes a novel variable limiter control scheme for the hybrid system of a wind farm and BESS to increase mitigation capability and extend the lifespan of the BESS. The control scheme is based on the concept of an allowable range of the wind farm's output. The range is determined to mitigate the fluctuation in the target frequency range and intentionally leave out the faster components. The scheme also incorporates the wind turbines' curtailment functionality to prevent rapid increases in their output and achieve higher mitigation performance. The performance of the proposed control was analyzed in simulation using one-year wind farm data. The simulation demonstrated that the proposed scheme also reduces the charge and discharge operation of BESS to about 50% of that in conventional low-pass filter control, which contributes to the elongation of BESS's lifespan.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy for Smart Homes Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In residential multi-energy systems, energy management strategies enable the coordinated and cascade utilization of diverse energy sources, which reduces energy costs for households. However, energy management algorithms suffer from the problems of model uncertainty, parameter uncertainty, temporal coupling and multi-energy coupling. To address these problems, this paper proposes an energy management algorithm for a residential multi-energy system based on the deep reinforcement learning. The proposed algorithm simultaneously considers multi-energy time-shifting and cascade utilization to minimize energy costs and maintain indoor temperatures. In the proposed algorithm, an adaptive additional reward method is introduced to define the priority of different energy sources, which facilitates the exploration of the action space to achieve unconstrained energy cascade utilization. Meanwhile, the adaptive additional reward method exploits the additional reward selectively to avoid suboptimal results. Comparatives simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves 10.32%/12.58% and 3.14%/9.75% lower daily energy costs in the low-temperature day and the high-temperature day. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm has superior performance in energy cascade utilization.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Power System of a Clinic Integrating Diesel Generator and Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The increasing number of dialysis patients in Japan highlights the importance of securing reliable power for hospitals and clinics during blackouts. To improve the resilience of clinic power grids, a system combining a diesel generator (DG), and electric vehicles (EVs) is considered. This power supply system requires power optimization to sustain electricity for the clinic as long as possible. This paper proposes an optimization method for power system of a clinic integrating the DG and EVs during blackouts. Since optimizing the power supply from the DG and EVs involves both linear and nonlinear programming problems, the optimization method consists of two steps. In the first step, power distribution between the DG and EVs is optimized using linear programming. In the second step, the power distribution among seven EVs is optimized using nonlinear programming. The proposed method is simulated for both winter and summer power demand. The results show that the proposed method can supply power to the clinic without load suppression throughout the entire day during blackouts. This ensures that the clinic remains comfortable and continues to provide artificial dialysis services to patients. After operating throughout the entire day, the remaining fuel of the DG is 17.3 L in winter and 98.9 L in summer.

articleTitle: Suitability of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator with Magnetic Gear for Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In wind power applications, the main mechanical energy flow comprises the turbine, the transmission and the generator, each component adding volume and inertia to the system, while the overall efficiency is affected at each level. But if we could decrease the number of components, it means that we could practically obtain increased efficiency for our wind generator. For that, we are proposing a generator with magnetic gear, which integrates the transmission and the generator. By means of electromagnetic analysis, as well as experiments, we are investigating the suitability of such a solution for wind power applications.

articleTitle: Core Loss Measurement Method for Magnetic Materials using Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, a method for measuring magnetic core loss at high frequency using a boost converter is proposed. Generally, magnetic core loss can be estimated through the loss based on the data provided by the core manufacturer's datasheets or loss analysis using Ansys Maxwell. However, these methods have the limitation of not accurately reflecting real operating conditions, making it difficult to trust. Since it measures under real operating conditions, the proposed method provides higher reliability compared to existing methods for estimating magnetic materials loss. The proposed loss measurement method was experimentally verified through a CRM (Critical Conduction Mode) boost converter.

articleTitle: A Smart Buoy-integrated Antenna for Monitoring Tidal Power Turbines

Simulated and measured results show that the bandwidth of 10dB-return loss satisfies the 920MHz band of the specified low power base station. articleTitle: LVRT Performance Improvement of a PV Power Plant for Asymmetric Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Low-voltage ride through (LVRT) is amongst the important attributes suggested by various grid codes for operation of photo-voltaic (PV) inverters. Asymmetric grid faults can hinder performance during LVRT due to their nature to introduce oscillations at the double grid frequency in active power and thus in DC-link voltage. This paper proposes a method for reducing the double grid frequency components from the inverter's i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> and i<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> currents in the presence of asymmetric faults resulting in reduced charging power fluctuations and eliminating DC overvoltage. Stable DC link voltage ensures steady power flow between PV panels and AC grid. The reduced oscillation will enhance reliability and life of capacitor.

articleTitle: Estimating the Switching Lifetime of GaN HEMT Under Soft-Switching Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: GaN power semiconductors are promising power devices for power applications (switching power supplies, inverters, etc.), but they have different materials and structures from Si devices (Si), so it is important to have a reliability qualification process suitable for GaN HEMT power devices. Especially, a characteristic unique to GaN devices is the increase of dynamic on-resistance (dRds(on)) due to the current collapse phenomenon caused by electron traps. Currently, a lot of research is being conducted into how this affects reliability in hard switching operations. In this paper, we will focus on soft-switching operation and propose a high-resolution measurement method for dRds(on). Also accelerated testing is conducted under high voltage and high current conditions to calculate the lifetime. Additionally, using simulation, the method is applied to power applications involving soft-switching operation.

articleTitle: Challenge to Build Sustainable Goto Islands
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper examines the historical context and current renewable energy initiatives in Goto City, Japan, a remote region with distinct geographical and economic challenges. It discusses the evolution of energy systems from traditional maritime practices to modern electric vehicle (EV) integration and intelligent transport systems (ITS). The findings highlight Goto's potential as a model for sustainable energy utilization, particularly in marine renewable energy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Renewable Energy Utilization: Performance Analysis of Hydrogen-Natural Gas Blending with KSM Static Mixer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Renewable energy and hydrogen energy are closely related, and utilizing renewable energy to produce hydrogen and then transporting and storing the hydrogen can effectively address the uneven geographical distribution of renewable energy. Utilizing in-service natural gas pipelines for the delivery of hydrogen generated from renewable energy sources is a current research hotspot. The flow characteristics of natural gas and hydrogen in the KSM static mixer were analyzed using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method, and the accuracy of the numerical model in this paper was verified. Based on the research results, effective measures to improve the static mixer have been proposed. The findings provide a theoretical foundation for advancing hydrogen blending in natural gas transportation.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based HVAC System Operation Under Limited Data Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The optimal operation of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems has been extensively studied to improve energy efficiency in building operation. With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources into power systems, this research has gained additional importance, particularly in addressing the uncertainties in power generation and utilizing HVAC systems as demand response resources. Traditional optimization approaches rely on precise parameters from physics-based models or full datasets that include all environmental factors influencing indoor temperature variations. However, it remains a significant challenge to acquire such detailed datasets and accurate model parameters. In this paper, a reinforcement learning-based strategy is proposed to operate the HVAC system under limited data acquisition. The proposed strategy does not require exact modeling parameters or a full dataset. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy by comparing it to conventional strategies in terms of operating cost, thermal comfort, and practical data acquisition.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of The Control Algorithms for The Capacitor Charging Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Capacitor Charging Power Supplies (CCPS) are essential components in systems that necessitate rapid and precise energy storage and discharge, such as pulsed power applications, laser systems, and advanced medical imaging technologies. This paper investigates the design methodologies, operational dynamics, and performance metrics of CCPS, with an emphasis on their efficiency, charging kinetics, and voltage regulation precision. Also, the study focuses on the control methods of the CCPS. The performances of the conventional (non-optimal), hysteresis current-mode constant on-time, constant off-time and discontinuous conduction mode comparator control methods are analyzed. The optimizations are mentioned with the comparative results for CCPS.

articleTitle: Effect of Surface Texturing on Sliding of Adhered Snow and Ice
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In cold regions, the accumulation of snow and ice on equipment used for renewable energy generation can significantly reduce power efficiency. Common de-icing strategies include heating the material surface to melt and slide the adhered snow and ice. However, these methods often require considerable energy. To address this, passive de-icing techniques, such as hydrophobic coatings, have been explored, but they are often susceptible to degradation. This study investigates an alternative approach using surface texturing to influence thermal conductivity and wettability, thereby enhancing snow and ice removal. Glass, polycarbonate, and acrylic were selected as test materials. Both flat and textured surfaces were prepared using a combination of masking and mechanical removal processes. The sliding behavior of snow and ice was evaluated by adhering columns of snow or ice to the material surfaces at -10°C, then gradually increasing the temperature until sliding occurred. Contact angles and sliding angles were also measured to assess wettability and adhesion strength. Results showed that for glass, the ice sliding temperature was higher on textured surfaces than on flat surfaces. For polycarbonate and acrylic, no significant difference in sliding temperature was observed. The findings suggest that surface wettability plays a crucial role in ice sliding due to water film formation, while for snow, texturing on acrylic may reduce adhesion. These results provide insights into optimizing surface texturing for efficient snow and ice removal in renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Heating System for Lithium-Ion Batteries in Low Temperature Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Batteries are crucial for energy storage applications, but their performance is significantly impacted by extreme environments, such as the low temperatures in deep-sea conditions. While batteries generate some heat during discharge, the temperature increase is insufficient to bring them to room temperature. Low temperatures hinder electrochemical reactions and raise internal impedance, leading to diminished capacity and overall performance. To mitigate these effects, this paper proposes a heating circuit based on a synchronous boost converter to preheat the battery in low-temperature environments. By warming the battery to room temperature prior to operation, internal resistance is reduced, ensuring optimal performance during charge and discharge cycles. The feasibility of this approach is first verified through simulations, followed by hardware implementation of the heating system. The setup is tested in a temperature-controlled chamber to simulate low-temperature conditions. In the experiment, the battery's charge and discharge processes successfully generate the required heating effect, with two key metrics evaluated: the rate of temperature rise and the energy consumed per degree Kelvin (1K) of temperature increase.

articleTitle: Database Construction and its Method of Building Materials for Coexistence Study of Beam Type Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Aiming to realize a simulation technique that can precisely predict the strength of the electromagnetic leakage field generated outdoors by Beam Type Wireless Power Transmission equipment located in a building. Therefore, A database of radio wave characteristics of building components was constructed. Then, the results of the simulation based on the database showed good agreement with the measurement results. It was confirmed that the good quality of the constructed database.

articleTitle: Analyzing of Electrospray Modes for Catalyst Layer Formation in Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The performance of polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells depends on the catalyst layer where the chemical reaction occurs. Electrospray deposition (ESD) is known to be able to form catalyst layers with excellent properties. In this study, we investigated the relationship between the spray mode and the properties of the catalyst layer when forming a catalyst layer by ESD. The spray modes were classified into three types based on image analysis: pulsation mode, cone-jet mode, and multi-jet mode. In addition, the proportion of each mode in the spray time was calculated. The mode transition occurred by increasing the voltage applied to the needle, but in the process of transitioning from pulsation mode to cone-jet mode, there was a voltage range in which each mode was mixed. On the other hand, there was almost no mixing of cone-jet and multi-jet. The deposited particle size was the largest in pulsation mode, and the variation was also large. The particle size in cone-jet mode and multi-jet mode was about the same. If pulsation mode is included during spraying, the charge transfer resistance increases. Therefore, from the viewpoint of power generation characteristics, it is better to form the catalyst layer in cone-jet mode or multi-jet mode and not mix pulsation mode as much as possible.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Method for Applying Digital LDOs to Current Measurement of CPUs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As CPUs continue to evolve and become more powerful, the issue of escalating power consumption has come to the forefront. To address this, we are exploring a power-coordinated processor that can effectively distribute power to each module within the CPU and regulate each power supply based on execution instructions to curb power consumption. However, to bring this concept to life, we need a method to accurately measure the current consumption of each module and create a current consumption model. This paper presents a novel approach for the installation of current measurement circuits in each module, a crucial step towards realizing a power-coordinated processor.

articleTitle: An Optimized Dimming Technique for High-Brightness LEDs Based on Variable Voltage Commands
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dimming technique for high-brightness LED drivers that improves luminous efficiency and reduces power consumption while maintaining simplicity. Traditional dimming methods, such as analog modulation (AM) and pulse-width modulation (PWM), are examined for their strengths and limitations. AM dimming offers better efficiency but struggles with nonlinearity and a limited dimming range, while PWM dimming provides precise control but is less efficient at high peak currents. To overcome these challenges, the authors propose a variable voltage command dimming method that adjusts the reference voltage in the LED driver's constant current regulator to achieve N-stage dimming. The method is optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to fine-tune the voltage levels, enhancing overall luminous efficiency. The proposed system incorporates a buck converter for voltage regulation and a linear current control circuit to maintain constant brightness, resulting in a significant improvement in both power consumption and brightness. Experimental results show that the method reduces power consumption by 24.4% and increases luminous output by 15.3% compared to traditional PWM dimming. This new dimming technique provides a cost-effective and energy-efficient solution for LED lighting systems while retaining ease of control, making it highly suitable for practical applications.

articleTitle: An Experimental Approach to DC Voltage Stabilization in a Hybrid Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents the results of experimental studies on the effects of DC voltage stabilization in a hybrid microgrid, using a prototype microgrid experimental system developed by Tohoku Gakuin University, Japan, and implemented at its Itsutsubashi campus. The developed microgrid system is designed to facilitate the use of renewable energy sources. Therefore, PV and wind power are assumed to be the primary power sources in this system. In addition, this proposed microgrid is intended to supply power simultaneously to DC loads (such as EV chargers, LEDs, or other DC-driven electrical equipment) and AC loads (such as those powered by conventional AC motors). However, with this system configuration, the major challenge arises from the fluctuation and uncertainty of power generation by renewable energy sources, which leads to voltage fluctuations and instability in the DC bus where these renewable power generators are integrated. Therefore, two types of energy storage devices with different cost, response, and cycle-life characteristics are introduced into this system for the purposes of power balancing and voltage stabilization: secondary battery and EDLC (Electrical Double-layer Capacitor), respectively. The experimental studies presented in this paper address one of the most critical issues for the stable operation of the developed hybrid microgrid system, which is related to DC voltage stability enhanced by the coordinated control of the two types of energy storage devices. This paper discusses the system configuration of the developed hybrid microgrid system and the coordinated control systems for DC voltage stabilization, and presents some of the experimental results to illustrate the proper controls for voltage stability in the system.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Hybrid Power System Using Marine Predator Algorithm Tuned Cascaded Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)

Renewable energy combined with a thermal generator makes a multi-area power system. As renewable sources are not stable, that's why they are attached to conventional sources to complete the load demand. articleTitle: Enhancing Power Efficiency by Integrating Processor Performance Metrics with Power Supply Phase Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The processor is the most power-consuming device in a computer, yet it often operates under light load conditions for extended periods. During these times, the processor's power supply also experiences a light load, which significantly decreases its efficiency. Therefore, maintaining high efficiency across a wide range of conditions, including light load, is crucial. Previously, an adaptive power efficiency control method was proposed that links real-time power control to the processor's logical data processing workload, optimizing the configuration to achieve the highest possible power efficiency. While this method has shown the potential to improve CPU power efficiency in some programs, processor power fluctuations vary depending on the computing system, and the characteristics of power load differ according to the program being executed. In this study, the processor power supply efficiency improvement under more fluctuating power loads was experimentally verified by applying the proposed method during the execution of various types of programs. The results confirmed that the proposed method can enhance power efficiency and reduce power loss.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Potential of Vehicle-Grid Integration (VGI) in Japan: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In response to Japan's growing energy security concerns and its commitment to a low-carbon transition., Vehicle-Grid Integration (VGI) technology has emerged as a promising solution. VGI can enhance the stability of renewable energy sources and improve grid resilience., particularly in the face of natural disasters like earthquakes. This study explores the potential for VGI application in Japan., using a methodological framework based on simulation., supported by literature review and survey interviews. Our findings reveal significant regional imbalances in VGI adoption., with smaller-scale systems facing uncertainties in revenue generation due to unpredictable user behavior., while larger systems exhibit more stable economic outcomes. Furthermore., technical., economic., and social challenges persist., including the need for a comprehensive economic analysis framework that addresses these uncertainties. Validation of theoretical models using real-world data is essential to accurately assess the feasibility and future development of VGI in Japan. The study highlights critical challenges and provides insights into the pathways necessary to advance VGI technology as a key contributor to Japan's energy transition.

articleTitle: Startup-based Induction Motor Fault Detection and Diagnosis Using Feature Extraction of the S-Transform Image
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Recently, it has been verified that conventional methods for detecting rotor electrical faults in induction motors can be challenging. This is because various fault scenarios can obscure the fault signatures, resulting in false negative alarms, or numerous benign conditions that produce signatures resembling those of actual faults, leading to false positive alarms. Thus, in pursuit of dependable fault detection, a trend has emerged involving the examination of the stator current during motor start-up. To enhance reliability, this paper proposes a novel method based on this concept. The proposed method is based on the use of the S-Transform. By applying the S-Transform to start-up currents, characteristic patterns emerge that can diagnose the induction motor faults. Simulation and experimental results are showcased for both a normal motor and a motor experiencing a fault to demonstrate the efficacy of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Load Nonlinear Feedforward Compensation for Dual-Output LLC Resonant Converter Based on Bang-Bang Charge Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In certain applications, such as TV displays or monitors, the need for two power supplies is common. To achieve high efficiency and power density, LLC resonant converters are often the preferred choice. Consequently, dual-output LLC resonant converters are widely used. However, sharing a resonant tank to minimize component usage and enhance power density can lead to mutual interference between the two output voltages. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel dual-output load nonlinear feedforward control strategy based on bang-bang charge control (BBCC) to reduce mutual interference between the two output voltages. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Development of Sinusoidal Converter and Inverter with Active LC Filter by Optimal Voltage Control Based on IRM-ILQ Control Method
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper describes a development of Sinusoidal Converter and Inverter with Active LC Filter, which are difficult to control optimally by classical control such as PI control due to complex and multivariable system. An IRM-ILQ control combining Inverse Linear Quadratic (ILQ) method based on modern control theory and Inverse Reference Model (IRM), is proposed. It can realize optimally coordinated transient responses of all state variables and outputs. Moreover, output voltages have robustness, few harmonics and distortions. Experimental results and verifications are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Unlocking Energy Stability: An Approach to Managing Load Shedding in eThekwini Municipality by Leveraging the Potential of Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: While maintaining the delicate balance between grid stability and economic productivity, load shedding remains a crucial yet contentious aspect of South Africa's energy landscape. South Africa has been load-shedding since 2007; however, the country experienced the highest amount of load shedding in 2022, where 11 529 GWh was shed. The National Energy Regulator of South Africa (NERSA) has adopted edition 3 of the National Rationalised Specification (NRS) 048, part 9, designed to facilitate the controlled reduction of up to 80% of the base load by rotating across 16 predefined load-shedding stages. While load shedding is beneficial to maintain network stability under grid constraints, it negatively impacts productivity and the economy. This research paper investigated the role of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in mitigating 360 random load-shedding events per annum, each lasting two hours, and has shown the immense potential of BESS.
