With an initial investment of R 250 000 000, ten, 4 MWh, Lithium-Ion BESS maintained the continuity of supply during load shedding; however, the cost to do so translated to R 12.61 kWh, which is R 10.92 kWh more when compared to the grid price of electricity. However, this cost is significantly lower than the estimated Cost of Unserved Energy (COUE), which is R 29.05 GVA/kWh, where GVA represents the gross value added to the economy. Comparatively, the BESS system proves to be a more feasible option, offering optimism for a more stable energy supply in the future. These findings highlight the potential of BESS in managing load shedding and provides valuable insights into its cost and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Novel Model of Reverse Transfer Capacitance for Gate Driver Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A switch mode power supply is demanded for miniaturization. High frequency switching can make miniaturized easy, but it causes to increase switching loss and surge voltage. To reduce both at that same time, the active gate drive is payed attention. The accurate estimation of switching loss and surge voltage is needed for gate drive optimization, and the device physics is included with conventional circuit analysis. However, the voltage dependency of reverse transfer capacitance is decided by internal parameters of switching device. Therefore, it cannot be used for circuit design since the internal parameters are unknown. A novel model which can be used by circuit designers is needed. In this paper, a novel reverse transfer capacitance model which can be used by circuit designers was investigated. As a result, all device parameters are estimated and the investigated model was constructed. Moreover, the validity of investigated model is experimentally examined.

articleTitle: Calcination condition dependence of the passivation properties of sol-gel deposited alumina thin films on silicon substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this research, we evaluated the surface passivation quality of the alumina films for silicon solar cells prepared by sol-gel process. Alumina have been paid much attention around silicon solar cells research area because the alumina has high negative fixed charge that causes good field effect passivation. We have evaluated minority carrier lifetime of sol-gel deposited alumina passivation films on silicon substrates. At the sample preparation process, we modified the sample preparation conditions such as calcined temperature, ambient atmosphere in the calcination process with or without introducing the water vapor, and introducing the thermally oxidized SiO2 interlayer between the alumina and the silicon substrates. The obtained results indicate that the prepared samples with SiO2 interlayer can enhance the minority carrier lifetime. Also, introduction of the water vapor in the calcination process enhances the minority carrier lifetime.

articleTitle: Design of Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge DC-DC Converter for Micro EV
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to indicate design guidelines of Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge (PSFB) converters for Micro EVs by comparing voltage oscillation suppression methods. The PSFB converters has the disadvantage of voltage oscillation caused by the resonant inductor and parasitic capacitor of synchronous rectifier MOSFETs. This voltage oscillation can damage switches or cause noise to deteriorate EMI performance. In order to solve the voltage oscillation problem, various research have been carried out. As a simple method, either clamp diodes or snubber circuits, or both are used. Voltage oscillation can be suppressed by forming the path avoiding the resonance inductors causing oscillation using the clamp diodes. On the other hand, the snubber circuits eliminate voltage oscillation by losses. The experimental results show the difference of voltage oscillation suppression effect and efficiency in each method and clarify the direction of voltage oscillation suppression design specific to PSFB converters for miniaturization.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Power Transistor Faults in Multilevel T - Type Based Nine Switch Inverter Using Center of Mass Indexes
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Nine-switch voltage source inverters (NSVSI) are DC-AC converters that utilize a reduced number of switches, making them advantageous for dual or six-phase motors. To enhance the quality of the output voltage and provide fault-tolerant capability, NSVSI topologies, like the T-Type-based NSVSI, have been modified to operate as multilevel converters. However, to ensure fault-tolerant capability, a fault diagnosis algorithm for power transistors must be developed. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel fault detection and diagnosis algorithm to identify faulty transistors in a multilevel T-Type-based NSVSI. This method is based on the development of specific indices derived from the center of mass of the output currents. The proposed technique offers a fast and reliable solution, demonstrating robustness under various load conditions. The effectiveness of this method will be validated through a series of simulation tests.

articleTitle: Integration of Solar PV with Existing Grid System to Test a Ni-Cd Battery Set for Railway Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to highlight the drawbacks in the adopted approach of conducting capacity test during the maintenance schedule of Ni-Cd battery set used to supply DC power to the control power systems present in electric locomotives in railways. The core purpose is to introduce renewable energy sources during the charging cycle and also make utilization of the energy wastage during the discharging cycle. Rather than wasting that energy, we could utilize it to meet a railway station's DC load need or export it to the grid to earn revenue. In order to charge the battery set using the suggested model, a PV panel is used during the day and a single-phase grid is used used during the night. Instead of using a resistive load during the discharging process, the battery set is discharged using grid and DC loads. A state flow control logic is intended to function in accordance with the adopted approach for testing a battery set, thereby eliminating the present manual process. When compared to the approach employed in Indian Railways, the suggested approach can save roughly 1702.169 MWh of energy over the course of a battery's codal life.

articleTitle: Design of Solar Tracking Solarux Fresnel CSP System and Manufacturing Small Scale Model of the System by 3D Printer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Within the scope of this project, the design and production of a small-scale model of the Concentrated Solar Power technology will be reviewed. Solar Tracking Solarux Fresnel CSP System is designed to increase the efficiency of the overall system and shorten the payback period of investment. Design and optimization of the system is done via Solidworks and it is manufactured via 3D printing technology, which enables fast and easy and low-cost production for parts with complex geometry. Parts of the system were analyzed for actual dimensions and 1:10 scale dimensions, and it was ensured to verify whether the designs met the desired mechanical and thermal properties. Small scale model of the system is manufactured by using PLA filament on a 3D printer, as it enables to low-cost and fast production.

articleTitle: North Atlantic Offshore Wind Characteristics Modeling and Comparison with Field Measurements and Industry Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wind characteristics are critical to offshore wind resource development. The power output from a wind turbine is very sensitive to the wind speed (proportional to the cube of the wind speed). Wind speed measurement is often limited to surface area close to Lidar buoys or meteorological stations and up to 200m due to the range of remote sensing devices. On the other hand, wind fields from ground level and up to 20000m above ground level can be simulated using Weather Research & Forecasting (WRF) model. In this study, WRF simulations are performed for the North Atlantic offshore waters to obtain wind speed time and spatial properties. Statistics of wind speeds for selected sites are derived and validated with field measurements. Wind vertical profiles are compared with ISO and IEC standards, and a power law profile is further derived to find the best fit. It is also demonstrated that the WRF model is reliable to forecast wind data, optimize prediction and improve reliability for coastal and offshore energy development. The wind modeling and characterizing can be extended to global regions to identify prospects with the most renewable energy potentials.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study on Periodic Rotation in a Rotating Pendulum Wave Energy Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The present study investigates the motion of a rotating pendulum wave power generation system equipped with a mechanical pendulum. The motion of the floating body in response to incident waves under various conditions is calculated, and the resulting motion of the pendulum mounted on the floating body is analysed numerically. As a result, it was found that the pendulum performs steady periodic rotation in incident waves under certain conditions, suggesting the possibility of power generation using a mechanical pendulum.

Author Keywords: rotating pendulum wave power generation system

articleTitle: Design Consideration ofMMC-based AC-DC Converter with 3.3 kV SiC-MOSFETs for SSTs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a design consideration of each part in modular multilevel converters (MMCs) using 3.3 kV SiC-MOSFET as AC-DC converters in solid-state transformers (SSTs). In such high-voltage applications, the grid-connected inductor requires an insulation voltage of 20 kV or more, and their size tends to be large. In this study, it was confirmed that the inductor volume can be reduced by 48% by using series connection of five inductors with 10 mH and rated voltage of 4 kV compared with an inductor with 50 mH and rated voltage of 20 kV. In addition, the volume of high-voltage DC capacitors is also concerned in such SSTs. As the result of a product survey for capacitors, it is clarified that when the required capacitance is larger than 11 μF, the size can be minimized by connecting several low-voltage electrolytic capacitors in series. On the other hand, when the required capacitance is smaller than 11 μF, the volume can be minimized by using film capacitors. These selection criteria are useful for the design of high-voltage MMC-based AC-DC converters.

articleTitle: Analysis and Efficiency Improvement of Quasi-Resonant Flyback Converter with Adaptive Valley Detection and Variable Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: QR-Flyback converters exhibit poor efficiency performance under high input voltage and light load conditions. This paper investigates the control of Pulse Frequency Modulation (PFM) and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) in quasi-resonant flyback converters across varying input voltages <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{in})$</tex>, output voltages <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{o})$</tex>, and load conditions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{o})$</tex>. An adaptive frequency control method is proposed, enabling the QR-Flyback converter to operate at an appropriate frequency, thereby improving efficiency. Additionally, this paper presents an adaptive valley detection scheme for QR-Flyback converters, applicable to wide input/output voltage ranges and various load conditions. The proposed control architecture is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis on Subsynchronous Oscillation of a Multi-Loop Grid Forming Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The grid forming converter (GFM) is considered a key technology to solve the issues of inverter- based resource (IBR)-rich grids. Many previous studies have discussed the advantages of GFM over grid following inverter (GFL), but there has been insufficient discussion on the drawbacks of GFM. In particular, a few studies have discussed sub-synchronous control oscillation (SSO) induced by GFM. This paper conducts the eigenvalue analysis on the single-loop GFM and the multi-loop GFM to evaluate the risk of SSO occurrence. The results of eigenvalue analysis reveal that the risk of SSO is greater on the multi-loop GFM than the single-loop GFM. Finally, experimental tests in the controller hardware in the loop (CHIL) environment are performed to verify the validity of the elgenvalue analysis.

articleTitle: Smart Systems Employing IoT Devices for Monitoring and Control of Electric Vehicle Residential Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As the number of electric vehicles (EVs) on the road continues to increase, the rise in power demand may pose challenges, especially for the localized grid capacity during peak load events. This paper briefly reviews methods of power monitoring and load shedding such as smart charging and load management systems. An internet-of-things (IoT) power monitoring system is proposed for high-resolution power monitoring and control of J1772 standard level 2 EV charging systems to provide detailed data to enable future studies on EV grid integration. Additionally, a hardware test bench (HTB) including a DC battery emulator, oscilloscope, and commercial EV charger developed for experimental data collection of voltage and current is described. The systems may be applied, for example, to compare the capability of IoT smart systems to monitor EV charging at high resolution as a retrofit solution for previously deployed chargers without energy monitoring and control systems.

articleTitle: Development of an AI-Based Detection System for Cherry Tomato Skin Splitting and Cracking
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, we applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) to develop a sorting system for cherry tomatoes. To detect cracks in cherry tomatoes using You Only Look Once (YOLO), a deep learning-based object detection method, we compared two different labeling techniques for the training data. One technique involved enclosing the entire crack area within a single bounding box, while the other subdivided the crack into smaller boxes. Through comparative experiments, both methods yielded satisfactory results; however, the approach of enclosing the entire crack with a single bounding box demonstrated particularly promising performance.

articleTitle: Comparison between LCL Filter Design Methods For Grid-Connected Cascaded H - Bridge Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison, between two LCL filter design methods, for cascaded h-bridge multilevel inverter applications, is performed. In detail, the first one was already proposed by the authors in a previous work. However, to validate the method broad applicability, it is now characterized for a seven-level cascaded h-bridge. The second method is proposed in literature and it is used as a term of comparison. The filter optimality criterion deals with complying with the IEEE Std 1547–2018 with lowest values of filter parameters, thus allowing for a filter cost and bulk reduction. The comparison is carried out in the Matlab/Simulink environment on a case study, which consists in a phase-shifted driven three-phase seven-level grid-connected cascaded h-bridge multilevel inverter. Results show that the design method proposed by the authors, which consider the phase-shifted pulse width modulation features also in the filter capacitor design procedure, match the previously discussed optimality criterion, with lower values of filter parameters if compared to the literature method, thus allowing for a filter cost and bulk reduction.

articleTitle: Design and Control Strategy of DAB Converter with 3.3 kV SiC-MOSFETs for SSTs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper reports a design of a DAB converter for the SSTs with the use of 3.3 kV SiC-MOSFETs with considering the device parasitic output capacitance. The mechanism of switching losses caused by the parasitic capacitance of the devices are reviewed, and the characteristics of the 3.3 kV SiC-MOSFETs are compared with other devices. A device selection to achieve a balance between the maximum conduction loss and the maximum switching loss is proposed. This paper also reviews the ZVS range extension methods and discusses their applications to the oscillating instantaneous power operations, which can achieve a drastic size reduction of the high-voltage side smoothing capacitors between the AC-DC and DC-DC stages. Experimental demonstration of the device selection and the ZVS range extension method are reported, and their advantages are confirmed.

articleTitle: Development of Bidirectional DC/DC Converter for Energy Storage with Mixed Power Generations
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: We aim to develop an independent power supply system for offshore aquaculture facilities, and are researching a energy storage system that enables stable use of a mix of power generation sources, including solar, wind, and tidal power. This paper presents on the development of a non-isolated two-stage bidirectional DC/DC converter that controls the charging and discharging of batteries for use in offshore independent power sources, and the results of its demonstration. The voltage and current control method that is based on the digital deadbeat con-trol is proposed. The control is able to maintain the DC grid volt-age of the independent power source constant regardless of the fluctuations of the generation power and the load consumption. The characteristics of the control using the 5kW class prototype device are performed in the experiment.

articleTitle: Impact of Key Technological Parameters on Sulfur Production Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The key technological parameters of the sulfur production unit have been identified, and their influence on the sulfur production processes has been investigated. In this process, the released hydrogen can be used as hydrogen energy. Based on the results of the experimental studies, graphs have been constructed showing the effects of the unit's parameters that significantly impact the processes of converting hydrogen sulfide into produced sulfur. By approximating the obtained graphical dependencies, polynomial equations have been derived that describe the established relationships of the key technological parameters of the sulfur production unit on the sulfur production process. The derived equations describing the relationships between the main parameters of the installation and the degree of hydrogen sulfide conversion into sulfur form the basis of mathematical models that enable computer simulation of various operating modes of the installation and the selection of its optimal operating modes. The originality of the obtained results lies in the development of graphical dependencies and mathematical models that describe the influence of input parameters of the studied object on the sulfur production processes.

articleTitle: A Novel Estimation Method for Equivalent Series Resistance of Film Capacitors Considering Frequency Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Capacitors have been widely utilized for power converters in renewable power generation. Their equivalent series resistance (ESR) is a critical parameter for estimating capacitor lifespan and aging. This study proposes a novel ESR estimation method specifically for low-ESR, low-capacitance capacitors such as film capacitors. Simulations and experimental results under various conditions demonstrate that the proposed method more accurately estimates ESR values, compared to the conventional methods. In addition, frequency characteristics of ESR are estimated under actual operating conditions, which has not been considered in previous literatures.

articleTitle: Unbalanced Three-phase Flying-capacitor Converter for Current Ripple Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a changing method for the ratio of a flying-capacitor voltage in a three-phase flying-capacitor converter (FCC), which increases output voltage levels without modifying the circuit configuration of the three-level FCC. A space vector modulation (SVM) scheme provides the degree of freedom to control the flying capacitor voltage, reducing the harmonic components of the output voltage and current at the switching frequency. Experiments with a 7-kW prototype confirm the output current ripple reduction based on the proposed SVM scheme. The reduction of the switching ripple components were confirmed from the FFT analysis results of the waveforms, and the sideband waves of the switching ripple components were reduced by 18% compared to the conventional SVM scheme. Besides, the power losses of the switching devices were analyzed to evaluate the power losses distribution. The results show that the unbalanced FC voltage does not significantly affect the device's thermal state.

articleTitle: Economic Viability of a Battery-electrolyser System for Frequency Response and Hydrogen Production
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper explores the economic viability of using battery-electrolysers, specifically a lead-acid variant, within the UK's dynamic frequency response services. A battery-electrolyser combines the functionalities of a battery and an electrolyser into a single device capable of both storing energy and producing hydrogen. As the UK accelerates its transition to renewable energy sources, long-duration energy storage is needed for maintaining grid stability. The paper begins by outlining the current frequency response services-Dynamic Containment (DC), Dynamic Moderation (DM), and Dynamic Regulation (DR) and the dominance of battery-operated systems in these markets. The paper looks at the possible role of a battery-electrolyser in dynamic services. This paper presents results looking at the profitability of this technology in the UK's ancillary services market under five different scenarios. The findings indicate that while the battery-electrolyser is not economically viable under most scenarios due to high operational electricity consumption costs, a strategy that leverages free grid charging demonstrates profitability with a net present value exceeding £197 million over 10 years based on a 10MW plant. The paper concludes that while current market conditions do not favor the widespread adoption of battery-electrolysers, specific operational strategies may unlock their economic potential, particularly in the context of growing renewable energy capacity.

articleTitle: Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems and Their Optimization for Remote Community Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: There is a growing interest in implementing hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) in remote communities where people are using diesel power. In the HRES, two or more renewable energy sources are combined, allowing the communities to counteract the weaknesses of one renewable energy source with the strengths of another. This study aims to design, simulate and optimize the HRES consisting of photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and a bio-based generator for applications in remote and northern communities in Canada. A methodology is developed to optimize HRESs so that net present cost (NPC) and levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of the energy systems can be minimized. The optimization is performed using a genetic algorithm-based model. A sample remote northern community in Canada is selected for a case study. The HRES being investigated targets to supply an average load demand of 2205 kWh/day and the peak load of 236.06kW for the sample community. Results show that the LCOE for the top optimal HRES configuration is $0.308/kWh, and its NPC is $4.29M. Through the present study, the HRES is shown to be an effective approach to replacing diesel power in remote communities.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar Flat Plate Collector Performance with Pebbles as Thermal Mass in Arid Climate Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This work investigated the performance of a solar flat plate collector (FPSC) with a natural black pebble as a sensible heat storage added to improve its thermal performance. Specifically, the effects on the temperatures of the absorber plate and glass cover are examined at two different flow rates (0.015 kg/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> and 0.030 kg/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>), and the results are compared to a standard flat plate collector without pebbles. Pebble's integration reduces temperature peaks, highlighting the significant effect of thermal mass of pebbles. At flowrate 0.015kg/s, the longer time spent by the fluid enhances convective heat transfer, leading to a notable 10% improvement in immediate heat transfer efficiency. While immediate efficiency decreases at higher flow rate 0.030kg/s, the sustained thermal release from the pebbles compensates for the lower peak temperatures. Particularly, the FPSC with pebbles integration shows an average maximum thermal efficiency 42.3% in flowrate that is 0.015 kg/s and while the conventional flat plate collector without pebbles was 33%. These findings highlight the complex interaction between flow rate, convective heat transfer, and thermal mass, offering valuable insights for optimizing solar flat plate collectors in water heating systems. The study suggests directions for future research, emphasizing the importance of refining collector design and exploring further modifications to enhance practical efficiency and real-world application.

articleTitle: An Active Bidirectional Balancer with Maximum Value Balancing Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The battery pack requires a large number of batteries of the same model, each with its own characteristics such as self-discharge rate, internal resistance, and temperature, which may vary slightly. These differences can lead to uneven capacity or voltage among the batteries, thereby affecting the efficiency of charge and discharge in the battery pack and preventing effective utilization of the battery pack's capacity. To address this issue, a battery balancer is needed to maintain balance among the batteries in the pack. This article presents the implementation of four bidirectional DC-DC converters. The balancing mechanism is triggered when a significant difference in capacity is detected. Depending on the state of the battery, power distribution during discharge helps to prolong the system's operating time, while during the charging process, the charging current is distributed to ensure that each battery is fully charged by the end of the charging cycle. This approach ensures balance is maintained throughout both charge and discharge cycles.

articleTitle: Y-Inversion Based DC-Link-Less Multi-Source Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper is about an innovative multi-source power network concept, which uses Y-inversion techniques, with high-frequency wide-band-gap semiconductor devices, to deliver a DC-link-capacitor-less, still voltage-boost capable, power-dense architecture. The network design is fully modular, enabling very high flexibility in regard of the number and type of input power sources, as well as easy reconfiguration and power scalability. In particular, the solution put forward retains capability of re-charging batteries from other primary sources and is compatible with regenerative type loads, too.

articleTitle: Reductive Conversion of Small Molecules on Transition Metal Complexes
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Global biogeochemical cycles, including carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles, play crucial roles in sustaining life on Earth. Plants and microorganisms with metalloenzymes are essential in catalyzing the transformations within these cycles. This study aims to replicate the functions of reductases using original metal complexes. In the carbon cycle, photocatalytic CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>reduction was achieved using a ruthenium-based photosensitizer, a ruthenium catalyst with CNC pincer and bpy ligands, and BI(OH)H as a sacrificial reagent, producing formic acid with a turnover number of 5634 over 24 hours and 72% selectivity. For the nitrogen cycle, two reduction processes were investigated: the NO reduction cycle and the NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> - reduction cycle. Unusual N-N bond formation between NO ligands on dinuclear ruthenium complexes was discovered, mimicking the NO reductase mechanism. A synthetic nitrite reduction cycle producing NH3 was achieved using a dinuclear ruthenium complex. In the sulfur cycle, the transformation of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>- to S2-, a pivotal point facilitated by sulfite reductases, was studied. A sulfite-bridged dinuclear ruthenium complex underwent stepwise reduction to form SO-bridged and Ss-brldged complexes, ultimately releasing H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S upon protonation. This study demonstrates the capability of the same dinuclear ruthenium complex to facilitate the reductive conversion of NO, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> -, and SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-, replicating the functionality of their respective reductases.

articleTitle: Research on Urban Surplus Energy Calculation and Utilization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A distributed energy society can be achieved by distributing the risk of renewable energy supply and reducing carbon dioxide emissions. This study examines ways to combine surplus urban energy with EV charging to realize a decentralized energy society. A graphic visualization model was created by linking a surplus energy calculation model and GIS for urban surplus energy visualization. Fukuoka City has confirmed surplus energy availability for energy flexibility, peak suppression using storage batteries, and EV charging based on the time of day.

articleTitle: Active Support Control Strategy for Virtual Flux in Offshore Wind Power Flexible Direct-Current Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The integration of large-scale offshore wind power into the grid poses challenges to the frequency and voltage stability of the receiving end of the power system. The limitations of relying solely on active support strategies from onshore converter stations are received significant attention. To address this, a novel model predictive control strategy is proposed, leveraging virtual flux coupling between onshore and offshore converter stations. This strategy establishes a flux relationship for flexible DC voltage control and optimizes energy balance between the wind farm and the power grid. By incorporating a rotating internal electromotive force under virtual flux, the proposed method achieves effective frequency and voltage regulation for source-grid interaction. The effectiveness of this strategy is validated through a hardware-in-the-loop validation platform for Typhoon MYWAY404.

articleTitle: Simplified Equivalent Circuit Model for Battery Energy Storage System Used for Grid Frequency Response
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The impact of installing renewable energy sources (RES) on the grid causes a reduction in grid inertia which leads to system vulnerability to frequency stability. To overcome this problem, battery energy storage system (BESS) is introduced. However, BESS also has several issues such as cost to its size and safety so that battery modeling must be precise and accurate. Accurate and low-complexity battery models are needed to maximize battery contributions on power grids. As an equivalent circuit model (ECM), the Randles circuit is commonly used for such applications. However, as system complexity increases, this model results in slow execution time. A simplified ECM is proposed to address this issue by representing the battery system as a dependent voltage source and a resistor. The proposed model is evaluated through two approaches, accuracy and running time evaluation. The simulation results show that the proposed model keeps accuracy with the accumulated state of charge (SOC) error for one year is 0.011% and accelerates the run time by 99%.

articleTitle: Assessment for Suitable Distributed Energy Resource Utilization to Mitigate Impact on Voltage Under Congestion Management
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In recent years, the operational flexibility of distributed energy resources (DERs) has been explored to alleviate congestion at substations in distribution networks caused by reverse power-flow from photovoltaic (PV) systems. This approach entails absorbing surplus electricity by creating sufficient demand for DERs, which is essential for clearing congestion. In addition, the management of voltage in the distribution network within acceptable range is crucial for grid operators. Thus, for realizing a suitable operation for flexibility of DERs, the grid operators need to select the utilized DERs to mitigate the voltage impact by increasing DER demand. However, the operational impact of DERs on voltage can vary depending on the power-flow conditions in the distribution network. Therefore, the analysis of the relationship between the utilized DER location and impact on voltage considering power-flow condition is required. This study proposes a method for evaluating the operational impact of DERs connected to high-voltage systems by considering various power-flow scenarios from the voltage perspective. Numerical experiments were conducted using a Japanese distribution network model to assess the operational impact of DER locations on voltage under various power-flow conditions and utilized DER candidates.

articleTitle: Extracting an Experimental Formulation for Power Loss Prediction in a Laboratory-Scale Grid-Forming Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The present paper introduces an experimental modeling approach for predicting power losses in grid-forming inverters. The proposed model reduces the need for measurement equipment, making it a practical solution for real-world applications of grid-forming inverters. The extracted model provides power loss predictions that can be utilized for optimizing system performance and operation. Additionally, the proposed model can detect unusual power losses, serving as an early warning system for potential faults or inefficiencies within the inverter. The effectiveness of this model has been validated through data collected from a laboratory-scale grid-forming inverter, demonstrating its performance in various operational scenarios. By simplifying the process of power loss estimation, this model offers a tool for optimization and energy management in microgrids containing grid-forming inverters.

articleTitle: Key Technologies for High-Efficiency and Reliable Solid-State Transformers for DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces key technologies for improved reliability of practical solid-state transformers (SST) to enable massive expansion of renewable energy. SSTs are attractive as compact and high-efficient AC-DC converters because SSTs accept a direct connection from medium voltage AC grid to DC micro grids without line-frequency transformers (LFTs). However, SSTs have low reliability compared with conventional AC-DC converters using LFTs. This paper introduces our contributions to the implementation of SSTs in society as follows: 1) conducted noise reduction by modulation technique, 2) cell-fault tolerant control, 3) packaging technology of power module for enhanced isolation and noise reduction, 4) development of high-frequency transformer with high voltage tolerance and 5) integrated system design for a I-MV A SST towards practical operation.

articleTitle: Adaptation and Implementation of a Building Management System for a Literature Museum
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Building Management Systems (BMS) are computerized control platforms designed to oversee and regulate the electrical and mechanical systems within a building. The primary goal of this paper is to develop a BMS application that can display, control, and monitor systems for a literature museum, regardless of the manufacturer. Additionally, the paper aims to create a gateway for managing various mechanical and electrical systems in the building, including heating, ventilation, air conditioning, lighting, and security.

articleTitle: Research of the PV Power Plant Installed in Electric Railway Power Supply Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: JR East Group is working on various energy measures to reduce CO2 emissions by 50% by 2030 compared to 2013 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. Installing renewable energy is one of the important issues to solve this problem. JR East has been introducing solar power generation as one of its environmental measures. In the case with KEIYO rolling stock depot solar power plant (Keiyo PV Plant), which is installed as the first self-consumption large-scale solar power generation system in JR East, it has been used for 10 years since 2013. Therefore, we report on the power generation results, the generation efficiency and the use of electric power for the past 10 years. In this paper, the authors first introduce about the long-term environmental goal called “Zero Carbon Challenge 2050” in JR East and explain about Keiyo PV Plant and overview of PV systems in Japan and Japanese railway companies in chapter 1 and 2. In chapter 3 and 4, the authors report about analysis of PV power generations and usage of generated electricity by PV plant, and chapter 5 is the summary of the results of this paper.

articleTitle: The Impact of LCL Filter on the Crest Factor in Hybrid Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study investigates the effect of the LCL filter on the crest factor of the load signal for a hybrid system. For this purpose, a hybrid test system has been modeled in the Matlab/Simulink environment. Buck/boost converter, inverter, and LCL filter have been designed. PWM signal has been generated using the incremental conductance (INC) algorithm. The gate-switching signal for the IGBTs has been generated using the PWM signal. The performance of the LCL filter with various parameters has been examined, and the effect of the signal on the load concerning the crest factor has been analyzed. Results showed that increasing inductance caused a deviation from the optimal crest factor and a reduction in peak voltage due to increased inductive reactance. Additionally, it was found that a 60 μF capacitance yielded improved crest factor performance, while higher values (90 μF) introduced significant harmonic distortion. The study indicates that the use of the LCL filter in power converters plays an important role in reducing the ripples in the system and that the LCL filter is effective in reducing the crest factor. The results highlight the significance of implementing an LCL filter to enhance the efficiency and reliability of PV panels in hybrid power systems. This study offers important insights into how LCL filters impact the stability and performance of systems powered by renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Designing of CO2 Adsorbent for a Pressure-Temperature Swing Adsorption Process
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: We propose zeolite/carbon composites for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capture. The development of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption and separation technologies for combustion exhaust gases is desired. One such technology is the pressure-swing adsorption (PSA) method using zeolites. Combining PSA with the heating process (PTSA: pressure-temperature swing adsorption) is expected to improve the recovery efficiency. The temperature swing part requires an external heat source during regeneration, making reducing energy consumption difficult. Against this background, the electric swing adsorption (ESA) method, which uses Joule heat generated by applying a voltage to the adsorbent to regenerate CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, has been considered. The ESA method is expected to have a higher regeneration efficiency than the existing TSA method because it directly heats the adsorbent. Because zeolite, used as a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorbent, is an insulator, it was mixed with a conductive carbon material for use in the ESA. The results suggest that a zeolite mixture with porous carbon can be applied in the ESA method for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capture.

articleTitle: Applications of Image Recognition Using Deep Learning and Its Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, we provide an overview of image recognition using deep learning and introduce its applications. Then, challenges in application and how to deal with them are discussed from a practical point of view. As a case study, image recognition of medical images and cloud images are examined as examples. Based on the similarity between medical images and cloud images, the paper examines the possibility of applying the method that has been successfully used for medical images to cloud images.

articleTitle: Near-Field Antenna Analysis Using Source-Potential Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a near-field antenna analysis using electromagnetic potentials. We introduce the concept of source-potential energy representation and visualize the spatiotemporal distribution of energy densities around a dipole antenna. Our results demonstrate that the source-potential expression enables clear distinction between the conductive energy within the antenna and the radiated energy from the antenna. This visualization provides a novel perspective on energy dynamics in antenna systems, offering insights into the interplay between internal conduction and external radiation processes.

articleTitle: Challenges Toward Commercializing Tidal Power Technology: Outcomes and Prospects from Japan's First Large-Scale Demonstration Project
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive report on the technical evaluation and commercialization potential of Japan's first large-scale demonstration project using a 500 kW-class tidal turbine. Conducted in Naru Strait, Goto City, Nagasaki Prefecture, between 2019 and 2021, the project marked a groundbreaking effort in Japan's tidal power sector. It focused on key aspects such as the stability of the power generation system, predictability, environmental impact, and technical challenges encountered during the installation process. The tidal turbine used for the project was a seabed-mounted model manufactured by SIMEC Atlantis Energy in the United Kingdom. Over the course of approximately 11 months, stable operation was achieved, exceeding expectations regarding its operational performance. In addition, a highly accurate power generation forecasting method was developed, leveraging the natural periodicity of tidal currents, and this provided significant insights into the potential for commercialization. This project laid the foundation for the future commercialization of tidal power in Japan. However, several challenges remain as critical next steps towards commercialization, such as grid integration, greater involvement of domestic and local companies (particularly in the assembly and installation stages), and ensuring the overall economic viability of the business. Since April 2022, the project has entered “Phase 2,” during which efforts to address these technical and economic challenges have been intensified. With these efforts, further progress is expected towards the full-scale commercialization of tidal power generation.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of H-Bridge Modular Cascaded Linear Amplifier Comprising Six Cells with 95.0% Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The negative effects issued by the harmonics and electromagnetic interference (EMI) are further concerned by increasing the demand for power converters with high-speed switching capability for variable renewable energies year by year. A modular cascaded linear amplifier (MCLA) has been proposed as a power converter which does not generate EMI without any output filter by utilizing partial linear operation. An H-bridge MCLA can improve its efficiency by increasing the number of cascaded H-bridge cells and applying unequal DC capacitor voltages. In this study, the operating modes of the MCLA comprising six H-bridge cells with unequal DC capacitor voltages are analyzed to achieve an efficiency of 95% or over. Based on the analysis, an experimental validation was conducted using a laboratory prototype and developed control scheme including capacitor voltage balancing for the prototype. It is verified that the prototype MCLA realizes sinusoidal voltage output and achieves the efficiency of 95.0% with unequal DC capacitor voltage balancing control. Even in a linear amplifier, the efficiency of the prototype MCLA is comparable to that of a general switched-mode converter.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Model Reference Adaptive Control for Hydrogen Engine Generator System Fueled by Sodium Borohydride
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Fuel cells and hydrogen engine generators are devices that generate electricity from hydrogen. Among them, hydrogen engine generators are inexpensive and tougher than fuel cells. Hydrogen sources for these devices include high-pressure hydrogen cylinders and hydrides such as NaBH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. This paper deals with a system that supplies hydrogen obtained by the hydrolysis reaction of NaBH4 to an engine generator. In the hydrogen engine generator system, the output voltage must be kept constant by changing the supply amount of sodium borohydride aqueous solution according to the output power. This paper shows the experimental results of implementing Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC), which acquires and controls the model while the system runs. As a result of the experiment, it is clarified that the output voltage of the hydrogen engine generator can be controlled to a reference value of 100 V, though there are a few vibrations.

articleTitle: A Study on DC Power Distribution Using Transformer with Special Winding Structure in Renewable Energy-Integrated Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The increasing use of distributed power sources, such as photovoltaic (PV) generation and fuel cells, has brought attention to DC power supply systems, which are now being considered for domestic and industrial applications alongside traditional uses in data centers. As DC-powered appliances like refrigerators and LED lighting become more common, transformer-based AC/DC converters, which avoid switching noise and reduce costs, are a promising solution. However, conventional 6-phase transformers used in these systems produce large DC voltage ripple and input current harmonics after rectification, often requiring polyphasing to mitigate these issues. This approach can increase transformer size and cost due to additional secondary windings. To address this, the authors propose a transformer with a special winding structure that minimizes secondary-side wiring complexity in multiphasing configurations. This study investigates the application of these transformers for AC/AC and hybrid AC/DC-AC/AC conversions, demonstrating improved conversion efficiency, reduced ripple, and enhanced power stability. The findings contribute to advancing DC power systems for renewable energy integration and broader applications in future power supply systems..

articleTitle: Analysis of DC Building Flexible Capacity Optimization Configuration Based on PEDF Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper constructs a DC building energy system based on Photovoltaic Energy storage Direct Current Flexible (PEDF) technology, and the corresponding DC building optimal capacity configuration is selected by analyzing the impact of DC building flexible load capacity characteristics on the stability of PEDF micro grid grid connection points. For this purpose, the over limited probability of the grid voltage at the grid on point is utilized as the assessment indicators for the stability of the established PEDF microgrid model for DC buildings first; Then, the impact of DC building flexible load capacity on the stability of PEDF microgrid is determined via the relationship curve between DC building flexible load capacity and the over limited probability of the grid voltage; In order to obtain the optimal flexible load capacity configuration for DC buildings based on the PEDF micro grid, the Polyfit function in MATLAB is used to perform nonlinear fitting on the relationship curve; Finally, the methods proposed in the article are verified by taking actual engineering cases as examples. Theoretical analysis and experimental results indicate that reasonable planning of DC building flexible load capacity not only enhances the on-site consumption capacity of photovoltaic energy, but also effectively improves the stability and safety of the PEDF micro grid.

Author Keywords: Probability of voltage exceeding the limit

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Optimization Strategy for Three-Level DAB Converters Modulated with Five DoFs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The three-level dual-active-bridge (DAB) converter presents several benefits, including enhanced control flexibility and the ability to use power switches with lower voltage ratings compared to traditional two-level DAB converters. To improve transmission efficiency, an optimization approach based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been proposed, leveraging the five degrees of freedom (5- DoFs) control method. This approach applies the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm to minimize power losses and determine optimal control strategies. The trained DDPG agent functions as a predictor, facilitating appropriate control actions under varying operational conditions. The main goal is to maximize efficiency by minimizing power losses. With the proposed strategy, the conversion efficiency is well improved, and the effectiveness is verified by experiment results under various conditions.

articleTitle: Energy Management of DC Microgrid-based Photovoltaic/Battery and Super Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The large use of microgrids, particularly direct current microgrids, is a global trend driven by the increasing integration of renewable energy sources with energy storage systems. DC microgrids offer the distinct advantage of eliminating harmonics and synchronization challenges, making them a focal point for research and engineering attentions. Considering the intermittent nature of primary renewable energy sources, such as photovoltaic and wind energy, the integration of energy storage systems is necessary to improve the reliability, stability, and overall performance of microgrids. This paper proposes an isolated DC microgrid including a photovoltaic array, a hybrid storage system based on a supercapacitor and battery bank, power electronic converters and a variable load. An energy management system to optimize operation of an islanded DC microgrid is presented. The EMS effectively regulates the DC bus voltage and balances power flow within system. To support the EMS, the test condition considers Maximum Power Point Tracking for the photovoltaic array, state of charge management for the battery and supercapacitor banks and converter control strategies to maintain DC bus voltage stability.

articleTitle: Solarux Wireless Mesh Network and Application for Monitoring Photovoltaic Solar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wireless mesh network is a technology that can dynamically self-organize and self-heal, provide flexible integration, rapid installation, easy maintenance, low cost, high scalability, and secure service capabilities. This technology includes mesh routers and mesh clients. They enable integration into networks such as the Internet, IEEE 802.11, IEEE 802.15, IEEE 802.16 and sensor networks through bridging capabilities in gateways and mesh routers. Wireless mesh networks provide wireless services for personal, local, campus and metropolitan area applications. In this paper, a method and an apparatus to deploy a wireless mesh network its and network nodes are described. In particular, a network with network node neighborhoods is described. A node consists of an antenna and a transceiver controller. Nodes are configured for installation with MAC addresses and geographic coordination with the network. In addition, the software architecture for the mesh network is described.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis, and Validation of High-Level Three-Phase dc/ac Converter with Dual Source/Phase Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Power converters like dc/dc converters and dc/ac converters are crucial for the renewable energy system. Multilevel inverters are used in such systems for higher performance. This paper proposes a new three-phase dc/ac power converter with a dual source per phase configuration. The per-phase configuration of the proposed topology consists of ten switches and four capacitors for an 11L waveform. A detailed analysis of the operation of the proposed 3-ph topology has been discussed along with the different modulation techniques. A detailed power loss analysis has been provided in this paper. Finally, different simulation and experimental results have been included in this paper for different operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Case Study for Energy Management in Food Production Facilities Through Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework and state-of-the-art review of energy management, with the primary goal of developing an analytical methodology to enhance energy efficiency in industrial processes as a precursor to energy management. This approach encourages productive sectors to implement best practices and mechanisms for measurement, monitoring, and control, facilitating effective actions to reduce consumption and improve efficiency. The study also develops a numerical analysis method to guide data collection, process analysis, identification of high-consumption stages, and the implementation of control tools. Finally, a case study is presented, demonstrating an estimated reduction in energy consumption and emissions in a food production plant using real data.

articleTitle: Determination on Equivalent Circuits and Parameters from Impedance Characteristics Using Brute Force
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy uses equivalent circuits to analyze electrochemical characteristics. Although there are several researches about automatic determinations on equivalent circuits, limited types of circuits can be determined. In this study, we brought Brute Force, a kind of global optimization methods, to the determinations. The goal of this research is to choose automatically the best equivalent circuits for the given impedance characteristics from all circuits that satisfy the given restrains, available kinds of circuit elements and the maximum number of elements. In order to achieve this goal, we propose a method that optimizes parameters of circuit elements for all the satisfying circuits. The circuits whose impedances are closest to the given impedance can be regarded as the best equivalent circuits. The proposed method can easily determine appropriate equivalent circuits consisting of up to four elements such as resistances, inductances, and capacitances. The proposed method helps us not only to know the equivalent circuits of anything whose impedance characteristics can be measured, but also to find unexpected elements such as parasitic inductances and capacitances. The major remaining problem is to achieve more faster speed and reduce storage requirements for the calculation of the determination.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Frequency Rectifier in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-frequency rectifier with a compensated zero-impedance angle in wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. By designing capacitive and inductive elements across multi-frequencies, the rectifier uses a single T-type topology to form a dual-frequency LCC compensation, ensuring the zero-impedance angle. Experimental results confirm that the rectifier can transmit power at dual frequencies. The WPT systems with the proposed rectifier achieve high efficiencies of 80.8% and 86.6% at 3.39 MHz and 6.78 MHz, respectively. This verifies the effectiveness of the proposed rectifier.

articleTitle: Interleaved Totem-Pole PFC Converter with ZVS Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents an interleaved totem-pole power factor correction (PFC) converter with zero-voltage switching (ZVS) to improve efficiency. The converter features three inductors and two interleaved bridge arms. The operation mode of the interleaved totem-pole PFC circuit is explained to achieve ZVS, along with the control flow diagram and component parameter design. An experimental prototype was built to validate the theoretical analysis of PFC control. This design allows high-frequency MOSFETs to achieve zero-voltage switching. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the converter, a 500W prototype was developed and tested.

articleTitle: Assessing the Factors that Drive Effective Decentralized Mini-Grids Deployment in Rural Ghana – A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Access to affordable electricity supply is crucial to help achieve the seventeen Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. However, there are several unelectrified rural areas in developing countries. These locations are primarily distant from the central grid and best suited for decentralized mini-grids. However, these systems are capital-intensive and require meticulous planning to ensure their sustainability. The situation is exacerbated when they are deployed using intermittent renewable energy resources. Using the Political, Economic, Social, Technical (PESTLE) framework, the authors analyzed the key factors that can drive the sustainable implementation of such systems in developing countries using Ghana as a case study. The results indicated that economic and technical drivers played a significant role in adopting the technology, while social-cultural drivers were the least impactful. The authors made recommendations that can inform policy and decision-makers on the areas that need improvement when planning and implementing future mini-grids in Ghana.

articleTitle: EVs Wireless Charging in Urban Context: a Model for Optimal Transmitter Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: With new stringent regulations introduced by several countries to encourage the decarbonisation of various sectors, Wireless Power Transfer is becoming one of the most interesting technologies in the transportation framework, as it enables to charge without connection and also dynamically. This type of charging also allows the vehicle to be recharged through short stops in different locations in urban areas, such as crossroads, traffic lights and routes subject to traffic congestions. This work implements a wireless charging model based on resonant inductive power transfer for charging electric vehicles in these locations. To avoid magnetic field leakage, coupled circuits are used that operate at resonant frequency to improve power transfer. The model optimises the number of transmitters for transmission and identifies performance trends by defining an ideal structure for an urban context. This will lead to the possibility of charging EVs also in traffic up to 210 Wh in 30 s. The implementation of this algorithm also makes it possible to check compliance with magnetic field limits on a section of road where wireless power transmission is implemented, proposing solution to avoid undesired citizens involvement.

articleTitle: Design Method of a 400 Vdc Direct Coupled PV Battery Systems for High Efficiency Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a PV battery system that directly connects PV panels and storage batteries in practical applications with 400 V DC output of 4 kW or more, and clarifies the operating conditions that exceed the performance of existing PV-battery systems using power conditioners, The key to high efficiency in a system directly connecting PV and storage batteries is to match the voltage of the PV, which fluctuates due to weather, with the voltage of the storage batteries, which fluctuates according to the remaining capacity. This condition was clarified so that the number of PV panels in series could be optimized at the design stage. Experimental results showed that the overall energy efficiency of a PV -battery system with directly connected PV panels and storage batteries with an optimized number of PV panels in series could achieve very high efficiency: 96% on rainy days and almost 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on sunny days.

articleTitle: Loss Analysis of an AC/DC Isolated Converter Module for Solid-State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) are considered as one of the key enablers for the new more efficient and resilient power grid. Thermal management of the system is one of the important challenges in SST design. To achieve better thermal management, determination of the loss values is essential. Therefore, in this study, the loss analysis of a modular Medium Voltage (MV) SST is presented. To obtain the total loss value of the SST, one module is analyzed, and the loss value of the module is investigated. Losses for the active-front-end converter, primary and secondary converters of the isolated DC-DC converter stage and high-frequency transformer are all investigated and calculated. This, total loss of the system is obtained to be used in cooling system design.

articleTitle: Bidirectional DC-DC Converter Based on Degradation Characteristics of GaN FET
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The high reliability and efficiency of a bidirectional dc-dc converter for batteries are crucial for renewable energy systems. The aim of this paper is to present the degradation characteristics of GaN FETs and discuss their effect on the performance of a bidirectional dc-dc converter using GaN GETs. Accelerated degradation testing over 3,000 hours reveals that the GaN FET used in this study shows an increase in on-resistance by up to 67%. Also, the turn-on delay increases up to 26%. When this GaN FET is applied to a DAB converter, a large change in the secondary current can be observed before and after degradation. Therefore, it is clarified that the reliability of the DAB converter can be enhanced by detecting this current change and predicting degradation.

articleTitle: Three-Level Neutral-Point Clamped CLLC Resonant Tank Design for MVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The paper evaluates various solid-state transformer (SST) topologies and selects the Type E architecture with three-stage conversion. This architecture includes medium-voltage DC (MVDC) and low-voltage DC (LVDC) links, using a high-frequency isolation transformer for electrical isolation. The design employs a three-level CLLC resonant converter, with an input voltage of 10 kVDC and an output voltage of 800 VDC, and aplanar litz transformer as the isolation component. The resonant tank design balances gain, resonant current, and switching frequency range by adjusting Q, k, and m values. Simulation results show that the three-level neutral-point clamped CLLC converter can stably output 800 V under different load conditions, proving its suitability for medium- to low-voltage SST applications.

articleTitle: Battery-Electrolyser Low-Pressure Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As renewable energy adoption grows, integrated energy storage solutions are needed. Traditional battery management systems are not designed to account for gas storage, making them unsuitable for hybrid battery-electrolyser energy storage systems. This paper describes the design of a custom low-pressure gasometer designed to regulate the flow of hydrogen from a battery-electrolyser. The gasometer, optimised to work with lead-acid battery-electrolysers, captures and regulates hydrogen produced from surplus renewable energy. Its modular design allows for scalable and adaptable storage solutions. Initial tests confirmed the gasometer's ability to operate within pressure limits, with consistent performance across continuous cycling. The use of 3D printing for the prototype enabled rapid development and customisation. However, the study highlighted the importance of precise construction to ensure uniform performance across gasometer units. Further testing under real-world conditions and the completion of the compressor design is necessary to transition the gasometer from a prototype to a production-ready system, ready for integration into larger-scale hydrogen storage applications.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for Reducing Second Harmonic Current and Enhancing Transient Response in Bidirectional V2X Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a control strategy for reducing second harmonic current (SHC) and enhancing transient response in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems. The developed V2X system includes a bidirectional three-phase DAB converter and a three-phase inverter circuit, capable of operating in both grid-tie and islanded operation modes. For the utilization of PV generation, PV inverter systems can be connected to the AC bus, enabling the charging and discharging of the EV battery in both operation modes. During islanded operation mode, unbalanced loads cause the output power on the AC side to pulsate at twice the AC frequency, leading to significant SHC on the DC side. To address this issue, a novel control strategy is proposed. The proposed control employs two PI controllers for DC bus voltage regulation. The first PI controller uses the moving average of DC bus voltage for feedback control, effectively suppressing SHC. The second PI controller uses the real-time DC voltage signal for feedback control, ensuring a fast transient response. Both PI controllers share the same integrator for coordinated control. Compared to the techniques described in the previous literature, the proposed control strategy can provide excellent SHC suppression and dynamic performance without the addition of extra measurement circuits. Due to the reduction in SHC and the fast response of DC bus voltage control, a smaller DC bus capacitor can be used in the V2X system. The proposed control strategy is validated through simulation and experimental tests. A V2X prototype was built and tested, demonstrating the feasibility and stability of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Development of Light-duty Commercial Vehicle Powered by Fuel Cell (FCEV) in Tokyo R&D
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Tokyo R&D is a company founded in 1981 focusing on the research and development of mobility such as automobiles etc. The company has worked on vehicle electrification since its founding. And our latest initiative is in FCEVs which use compressed hydrogen gas as a method of storing electrical energy. In this issue, we report on our efforts to demonstrate the development of FCEV commercial vehicles.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Convenience Store with Electric Vehicle and Cooling Model Heat Pump
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In recent years, the spread of renewable energy (RES) has been called for in consideration of environmental issues. In addition, consumers are being asked to reduce their power consumption in order to achieve carbon neutrality. Stores such as convenience store (CS) use electricity 24 hours a day, and the amount of power consumption is a barrier to achieving carbon neutrality. In this study, we propose a convenience store that has introduced a cooling-heat pump to reduce power consumption. In addition, we introduce an electric vehicle (EV) and an EV charging station into this model to improve the economic efficiency of the model. The simulation results show that the proposed model is more effective from the economic and environmental standpoints than a conventional CS without the use of equipment.

articleTitle: Field-Oriented Control of a Reduced Order Model of a Nine-Phase PMSM in Healthy and Faulty Case
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In the task of electrification in various fields, the electrical machine is an important component. Current research show a rising interest in multiphase types, because of their advantages like inherent fault tolerance or lower current per phase. In this paper, the reduced order model of a nine-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine is developed and analyzed. The reduced order model is built using a lookup table created by simulation of certain operating points in an FEA model. To reduce calculation time, current and flux values are transformed into dq-coordinates. Two cases are considered: the healthy and an inter-turn short circuit fault case. For both cases the same control topology, a field-oriented control, with the same parameters is used. The healthy case is validated with an analytical model. The faulty case is then analyzed to firstly visualize the impact of the fault in the control scheme and secondly identify attributes, such as certain harmonic components, to detect this fault scenerio. With a reliable detection, a fault-tolerant control can be applied in future papers.

articleTitle: Automated Determination of Equivalent Circuit Models for Electrochemical Systems Using EIS and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this study, we propose a novel approach to estimating equivalent circuit models for electrochemical systems using Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) and unsupervised learning. While EIS is a powerful technique for characterizing aspects such as mass transfer and ion diffusion in electrochemical devices, the identification of equivalent circuit models has traditionally relied heavily on the experience and intuition of model creators due to the complex nature of impedance spectra. Our proposed method examines low-dimensional embeddings that consider the characteristics between different circuits for equivalent circuit estimation. This approach significantly reduces the time and expertise required for modeling electrochemical systems, providing a scalable solution for large-scale analysis. The model's performance has been validated on various datasets, demonstrating its accuracy and potential as a tool for improving the design and diagnosis of electrochemical devices.

articleTitle: Application of Temperature Balancing in Paralleled Power Supply Systems with Current-Sharing Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces temperature measurements of key components to demonstrate that, when switching mode power supplies (SMPS) operate in parallel with the same output power ratio, environmental factors or other specific conditions can lead to temperature differences among the key components of each power supply. If these temperature differences persist over time, they can decrease the overall reliability of the system. However, the proposed circuit architecture and control method effectively reduce or eliminate these temperature differences, achieving nearly uniform thermal loss among all power units and thus realizing temperature balancing. Experimental results confirm the feasibility of this approach. The system-input specification covers the full range of 90 to 264 Vac, with an output specification of 500 W/48 V. The design utilizes an LLC resonant topology and a secondary-side synchronous rectifier (SR), and includes a front-end stage of power factor correction (PFC).

articleTitle: Design and Control of a Two Switch Forward Converter with Supertwisting Sliding Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and control of a two-switch forward converter utilizing a supertwisting sliding mode control (STSMC) strategy. The two-switch forward converter, known for its efficiency in medium-power applications, is equipped with a robust control method to ensure improved stability and dynamic performance under varying operating conditions. The supertwisting sliding mode approach is chosen for its ability to mitigate chattering effects, a common drawback in traditional sliding mode control, while ensuring precise tracking and disturbance rejection. Through comprehensive simulation, the proposed system demonstrates enhanced performance in terms of voltage regulation and improved transient response.
