The results indicate that the integration of STSMC significantly improves the converter's efficiency and robustness, making it suitable for various power conversion applications.

articleTitle: Conducted Emission Voltage Reduction for Multi-Cell SST with Current-Type ACC
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a common mode (CM) noise reduction method for a multi-cell solid-state transformer (SST) using a current-type active common mode noise canceler (ACC). Multi-cell power converters typically have complex noise propagation paths. However, the proposed current-type ACC with Rogowski coil effectively reduces electromagnetic noise in power converters with multiple cells. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through experimental results. The conducted emission voltage of the power converter is reduced by 20.8dBμV when the ACC is connected to the DC voltage part on the primary(high-voltage) side in one cell.

articleTitle: A Study High Voltage PCB Litz Wire Concept for Solid-State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As global warming intensifies, renewable energy is gradually replacing fossil fuels, and energy storage systems have become key components in power systems. To maximize conversion efficiency, integrating energy storage systems into medium-voltage AC (MVAC) networks while minimizing energy conversion steps is essential. Solid-state transformers (SSTs) have emerged as critical components, replacing conventional transformers and addressing issues of bulkiness and low power density. However, insulation challenges remain in SSTs. Traditional epoxy resin-encapsulated Litz wire transformers partially address these issues, but the manufacturing process is complex. Recent research proposes using printed circuit board (PCB) winding transformers, analyzing different insulation materials to improve dielectric strength and reduce partial discharge. This method, validated through finite element analysis, ultimately selects NPG-180BH as the material, providing a more reliable solution for SSTs in medium-voltage renewable energy applications.

articleTitle: Implementing a High-Frequency Digital SMPS with Microcontroller Hardware Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective approach to implementing high-frequency current controllers within a buck circuit, using a general-purpose microcontroller (MCU), the STM32G474RB. By leveraging its built-in filter math accelerator (FMAC), a type II compensator is deployed to achieve a current control frequency of 250kHz. This method reduces system size and cost while maintaining high efficiency, making it a viable alternative to more expensive digital signal processor (DSP) and field-programmable gate array (FPGA) solutions. The proposed design is validated through hardware implementation, showcasing its potential for advancing switch mode power supply (SMPS) performance.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Visualization Simulator for Power Device Behavior in Power Converter Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: It is important to understand details of power semiconductor devices in the design of power converter circuit. However, it is virtually impossible to acquire all academic subjects on electric and electronic circuits, physical properties, and semiconductor physics. Therefore, the authors have attempted to visualize the relationship between theory and device operation by a simulator. This simulator can understand the relationship between circuit design models and semiconductor device.

articleTitle: Constant DC Current Control of Unidirectional High-Frequency Isolated Medium-Voltage AC-DC Modular Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper discusses a constant DC current control of the proposed high-frequency isolated medium-voltage AC-DC converter using a modular matrix converter. The proposed converter is composed of a modular matrix converter, a high-frequency transformer, and a diode-rectifIer-circuit. Since the proposed circuit is directly connected to an input three-phase medium-voltage using the modular matrix converter, the proposed circuit can generate high output power. The authors propose a constant output current control for any output DC voltage of the proposed circuit using the high-frequency voltage generated by the MMxC. The effectiveness of the proposed output DC current control is confirmed by the experiment using 200V prototypes.

articleTitle: Research on Continuous Operation of Active Gate Driver Combining Current Source and Active Gate Resistor
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Active gate drivers (AGDs) improve the trade-off between switching losses and surge voltage by actively operating switching transitions. However, conventional AGDs, which actively change the gate resistance have limitations in achieving sufficiently high-speed drive. Therefore, a new AGD combining a current source and an active gate resistor was proposed. Double-pulse tests confirmed that the new AGD further reduces turn-on losses compared to conventional AGD. In this study, control of the new AGD with feedback of the load current was implemented. A six-pulse test verified the continuous operation of the new AGD and confirmed that the new AGD with the control reduces switching losses more than it without the control.

articleTitle: Household Energy Management under Incentive-based and Price-based DR Considering Electricity Charges
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Demand response (DR), especially incentive-based DR and price-based DR, is attracting attention and researchers have been studying how to control household devices to minimize electricity charges under both DR systems. However, there has been no research that considers electricity usage charges, basic charges, revenue from selling electricity and rewards of incentive-based DR or uses baselines for DR calculated with optimized electricity consumption either. In this paper, we propose a method which solves the above, showing that proposed method can minimize total electricity charges most effectively through comparison with other three methods. Also, it is found that negative DR is not effective when end users have already optimized their power consumption.

articleTitle: Development for Energy-Efficient Railway Utilizing Wayside Energy Storage System Towards Future Sustainable Society
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, a power control method to improve energy saving effect of wayside energy storage system focusing on the power flow control with distant trains is presented. The proposed method controls the filter capacitor voltage of the wayside energy storage system to suppress the fluctuation of train voltage utilizing a feeder circuit model based on the information of trains and substations. The proposed control method is verified utilizing numerical simulation. As a result, the increase of regenerative energy and decrease of substation output energy comparing with the conventional method are confirmed.

articleTitle: Collectivist and Individualist End-User Values in the Digital Energy Community Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Energy community (EC) is an emerging entity in the energy system. EC information system enables energy consumers and prosumers collectively generate, use, share and trade renewable energy, as well as communicate and exchange data and information within the EC and with external stakeholders. End-user values collectivism and individualism are strongly related to the participation in the energy community through the information system. Collectivistic and individualistic value categories were elicited in 96 value-focused interviews with energy consumers and prosumers as potential energy community members. Although these value categories are partly conflicting, they disclose shared goals that may be implemented in the EC information system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Substation Transformer Tap Adjustment Control Using Digital Twin Database
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In distribution networks where it is challenging to directly measure load-side voltage, frequent voltage fluctuations often occur, leading to frequent transformer tap adjustments. These frequent adjustments can shorten transformer lifespan, increase maintenance costs, and compromise the stability of the entire distribution system. This study proposes a machine learning-based method to accurately predict load-side voltage and derive optimal tap adjustments. By doing so, it aims to improve voltage stability and reduce unnecessary tap changes. The distribution network was modeled using the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) as a digital twin, and OpenDSS was used to simulate various load scenarios and generate data. Machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Random Forest, and XGBoost, were trained using this data. Real-time data management was handled by Microsoft SQL Server, ensuring systematic and secure data handling. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost demonstrated the best predictive performance, excelling at handling large datasets and preventing overfitting through regularization. The proposed method is expected to minimize unnecessary tap changes and significantly enhance both voltage stability and the efficiency of power systems.

articleTitle: Impact of Grid Faults on Grid-Following Converter Controller Operation and Phase Instability
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Currently, most Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) connected to power systems use Grid Following Inverter (GFL) models. However, as the penetration of IBRs in power systems increases, concerns about inverter control issues in weak grids are growing. Particularly, when faults occur in weak grids, IBRs produce voltage with uncontrolled phase and magnitude, leading to their disconnection from the grid. This phenomenon is not observed in traditional generator models, highlighting the need for a detailed analysis of the IBRs controller's operation. This paper analysis the relationship between grid strength and inverter controller operation during grid faults. When fault occurs in a weak gird fault current components inject IBRs controller, consequently IBRs output uncontrolled phase voltage. The voltage with uncontrolled phase causes a three-phase imbalance in the output voltage of the inverter. This phenomenon becomes more severe as the system becomes more unstable. As a result, the output of IBRs is stopped, and they are disconnected from the grid. To verify IBRs controller operation during grid faults, PSCAD/EMTDC is used. To this analysis It will help in establishing criteria for the connection of a weak grid.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Converter Test System With a Single DC Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Grid emulators (GE) provide an excellent test platform for grid-coupled inverters (GC), greatly reducing product development time. However, conventional grid emulators require a separate DC power supply to absorb power, leading to a significant increase in cost. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a GE test bench that requires only one DC power supply to drive a single power trend direction, which greatly reduces the test cost.

articleTitle: Sustainable EV System for Next-Generation Reginal Society
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Nagasaki EV & ITS Project, which aims to enhance sustainable transportation in the Nagasaki region through the integration of electric vehicles (EVs) and intelligent transportation systems (ITS). The project is a collaborative effort involving various stakeholders, including the Nagasaki Prefecture, local companies, universities, research institutions, and non-profit organizations, organized under the Nagasaki EV & ITS Consortium. Key initiatives such as community car-sharing programs in Ishinomaki City, Miyagi Prefecture, and the implementation of next-generation energy solutions in Izumi Park Town are explored, highlighting their impact on regional development and recovery efforts following the Great East Japan Earthquake. This paper also acknowledges the significant contributions of various entities, including the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology, and Mitsubishi Estate, as well as the Tohoku Next-Generation Mobility Technology Demonstration Consortium. The findings demonstrate the importance of collaborative approaches in achieving sustainable mobility solutions, paving the way for future advancements in eco-friendly transportation initiatives.

articleTitle: 200kHz 3kW SiC-MOSFET Single-Ended WPT System with a New Switching-Loss Reduction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Recently wireless power transfer (WPT) systems are expected to be put into practical use as a means of battery chargers for vehicles. A miniaturized system is required especially in underwater power supply such as autonomous underwater vehicle chargers. Although higher-frequency operation is an effective measure for miniaturization of WPT systems, increased switching losses hinder this approach. In this paper, it is revealed that the switching losses of the single-ended inverter driven WPT system are analyzed into a resonant-voltage loss and a parasitic-inductance loss, then proposed is a new combination method of a bear-chip mounted Kelvin-drive SiC-MOSFET (Silicon Carbide-Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor) and Lenz power board to reduce the both losses successfully. Newly developed has been a 3kW c single-ended WPT system of high-frequency 200kHz operation with the proposed method. The prototype system has achieved that the 1/5 low switching loss as compared with conventional systems.

articleTitle: Wide-Range Temperature Environment Testing for Power Converters and Their Components between +40°C and -40°C
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Power electronics converters are essential to renewable energy systems and electric vehicles. However, the converter circuits face significant challenges when used in cold environments. These circuits consist of several parts: power devices, passive components, dielectric, magnetic materials, microcontrollers, and gate drivers. The high-temperature parameters of these parts are provided well in the datasheets. However, no details on the low-temperature conditions are provided in the datasheet. Thus, the power electronics converter's behavior is unknown under cold-temperature conditions. This paper proposes a method for achieving stable operation of power electronics circuits in cold regions. The study shows the shortened rise and fall times of the PWM signal generated from the DSP processor and the reduced propagation delay times of the gate driver in cold environments based on the experimental analysis. Furthermore, the efficiency analysis of a 300W buck converter circuit between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> is conducted, and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Load Identification Method of Urban Rail DC Traction Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The load identification of DC traction power supply system (TPSS) provides a new possibility for energy management strategy (EMS) of wayside energy storage system (WESS) for regenerative braking energy recovery in urban rail. In addition, it also provides application opportunities for operators to conduct energy efficiency analysis and power supply scheduling. This study introduces a deep learning-based approach for identifying TPSS load, requiring only minimal ground data to enable the online detection of load power within the power supply section. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and offers significant practical value for engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Synergic AC-DC-DC Energy Storage System Applying Totem Pole Circuitry Scheme with Inrush Current Limiting Based on SiC MOSFET Spirito Effect and PSFB Converter with Non-uniform Air Gap Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A synergic energy storage system operating with PV energy conversion system is implemented by AC-DC-DC converter, including a totem pole bridgeless PFC and phase shift full bridge (PSFB) circuitries. An inherent inrush current limit based on SiC MOSFET Spirito effect to protect power semiconductor devices for reliable operation as well as functioning as a simple current sensing design for critical conduction mode (CRM) control is applied in this PFC converter to achieve light load efficiency improving. For DC-DC conversion circuitry, the core design is to utilize a non-uniform air gap inductor for performing a pre-set two-state inductances to optimize the operation of this PSFB converter to achieve zero voltage switching (ZVS). The experimental results of the presented AC-DC-DC converter are demonstrated applying the system of 220V AC input voltage and 1000W with 12V output charging voltage. The efficiency of this synergic energy storage system can achieve 95.1% at rated output power and 76.5% at 10% load, with 2.3% and 5.91% improving respectively, comparing to conventional energy storage system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Monopolar Fault-Tolerant Operation Capability of Multi-Active-Bridge Converters in Bipolar DC System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Bipolar DC systems present advantages in terms of flexibility and reliability for the integration of renewable power sources and DC loads. In this paper, focusing on the monopolar fault-tolerant operation capability, the six types of multi-active-bridge converter are examined. The reconfiguration schemes for monopolar fault-tolerant operation are proposed to isolate the faulted pole while maintaining power transfer between the normal ports. Based on the RMS currents of switches in different topologies, the monopolar fault-tolerant operation capability of the converters is evaluated and compared. This study could provide a reference for the topology selection of high-reliable bipolar DC-DC converter.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Analysis of Vector Extension for a Processor Tightly Coupled with Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As an initial study toward the development of a processor that achieves high energy efficiency by cooperating with a power supply, this paper implemented a vector extension of the RISC-V architecture on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and evaluated the impact of the extension instructions on energy efficiency. Experiments were conducted to measure the current flowing into the FPGA when a benchmark program was executed, and the results showed an average improvement in energy efficiency of 3.8 times.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Solar Irradiance Using ARIMA
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Solar irradiance data is a crucial issue for solar thermal and photovoltaic systems. In this instance, a basic step in solar energy applications is the estimation of solar irradiance. The integration of solar irradiance at a high penetration rate into the electrical grid may pose a danger to grid stability due to weather changes. As a result, forecasting the solar irradiance parameter is necessary to guarantee the grid's security and quality. In this study, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model is used to forecast the solar irradiance time series. In addition, the temperature, the relative humidity, and the wind speed are also predicted using the same model.

articleTitle: Design of High-Frequency Single-Input Multiple-Output Wireless Power Transfer System with Parasitic Capacitance of Coupled Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a design for a high-frequency single-input multiple-output (SIMO) wireless power transfer (WPT) system that incorporates the parasitic capacitance of coupled coils. Additionally, the effect of the mutual inductance among the receiving coils is considered in the design. To evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposal, a SIMO WPT system using a class-E inverter as the transmitter and two resistive loads as receivers is designed and tested. The switch-voltage waveforms in both the numerical calculations and experiment meet the class-E Zero-Voltage-Switching / Zero- Derivative-Switching (ZVS/ZDS) conditions, enabling a high power-transmission efficiency at a high frequency. Furthermore, the calculated results are consistent with the experimental ones, validating the proposal. The results also highlight the significance of accounting for coil-coupled parasitic capacitance in the design of high-frequency SIMO WPT systems.

articleTitle: Renewable Microgrid Technology for Electrified Transportation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The development of green electrified transportation with penetration of renewable energies is an important trend, which poses both opportunities and challenges. This paper provides a review about the emerging role of renewable microgrid technology in supporting and advancing electrified transportation system. As important solutions, the renewable micro grid and energy router technology for electrified transportation are reviewed in this work. Also, our previous studies are comprehensively discussed in this paper. The integration of renewable microgrids with electrified transportation infrastructure offers enhanced reliability, improved renewable energy utilization, and optimized energy management. Energy routers further enable flexible energy distribution and facilitate vehicle-to-grid (V2G) applications. This work concludes that the integration of renewable microgrids and electrified transportation poses important opportunities for sustainable and efficient urban energy systems. In addition, several future research trends are discussed, including energy management technology, stability and resilience and tech-economic assessment.

articleTitle: In-Orbit Performance Evaluation of the MDASat-1 CubeSat Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In recent years, South Africa has increasingly leveraged space-based technologies to enhance national resource management and strengthen its security capabilities. As the nation transitions to a digital economy, space science and technology (SST) has become a vital component, particularly in remote sensing applications, including weather monitoring, renewable energy (solar and wind), communications, resource management, and the exploration of inaccessible areas. This evolving landscape drives ongoing research at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology (CPUT), with a particular focus on nanosatellite development for remote sensing. This paper presents case studies from the MDASat-1 mission, demonstrating the practical implementation and testing of nanosatellite systems at CPUT. Using whole orbit data recorded on 1 September 2024, this analysis highlights the mission's contribution to advancing space technologies for societal benefits, with the power system performing nominally during the mission.

articleTitle: Voltage Control in Distribution Systems with Solid-State Transformers Using Online Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Solid-state transformers (SSTs) can be utilized to regulate node voltages in distribution systems. In this paper, we employ a variant of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to calculate the reactive power outputs of SSTs, aiming to mitigate voltage deviation issues caused by the increasing integration of photovoltaic (PV) generation in a distribution system while improving the power factor at the substation.

articleTitle: Fault-Ride-Through Operation of Solid-state-Transformer Equipped with Ultra Small Capacitors in H-Bridge Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault-ride-through control method for solid-state transformers (SSTs) equipped with ultra-small capacitors, utilizing active power calculation. The control method continuously calculates load power and determines the source power reference based on the calculated load power. The proposed approach ensures stable capacitor voltage during load-side faults. Simulation results of the fault-ride-through operation confirm that the control method enhances the continuous operation performance of the SST.

articleTitle: Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge Converter with High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The phase-shifted full-bridge (PSFB) converter with a center-tapped rectifier (CTR) structure, commonly used in low-voltage, high-current applications, faces the issue of high voltage stress on the rectifier diodes. To address this, the center-tap clamping (CTC) circuit has been studied previously. However, applying the CTC structure increases the number of secondary windings on the transformer. In this paper, we propose a new winding technique to solve this issue. The proposed technique adds a center tap to the one-turn winding of the secondary side, instead of adding it to the two-turn winding as in the conventional CTC structure. This reduces the winding resistance, thereby decreasing conduction losses. The proposed converter was experimentally validated using a prototype designed for an output of 12V/70A and 840W.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Sustainable Energy Trading Optimizing Prosumer Incentives and Carbon Footprint
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing energy management for prosumers in smart grid environments, balancing financial incentives with carbon emission reduction. We propose a multi-objective optimization model that considers the complex interplay between solar energy generation, battery storage utilization, and energy trading among prosumers. The model is lmplemented using MATLAB, employing a Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) algorithm to solve the nonlinear optimization problem. Our approach uniquely integrates both economic and environmental factors by maximizing incentives for solar and battery usage while minimizing carbon emissions associated with energy consumption and storage. The optimization considers various constraints, including energy balance, battery capacity, and solar generation limits. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness using a case study with 10 prosumers, showcasing how the optimal allocation of energy resources can lead to significant reductions in carbon footprint while maximizing financial benefits. This research contributes to the growing field of sustainable energy management in smart grids, offering a practical tool for prosumers to make informed decisions about their energy usage and trading strategies. The results highlight the potential for such optimization models to play a crucial role in promoting more sustainable and economically viable energy systems in the context of increasing decentralization and renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Machine Learning Approach to Offshore Wind Farm Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wind energy holds a significant position among renewable energy sources. Wind turbines generate electricity by harnessing wind power, and wind farms, typically consisting of several turbines, are commonly employed. The location of wind farms can greatly influence the efficiency of the energy produced. Offshore wind farms, in particular, offer various advantages over onshore installations. In a well-optimized energy production process, the in-tegrity of the grid structure enhances the operational efficiency of wind energy. Therefore, accurately pre-dicting the energy output of wind farms is critical. While classical machine learning (ML) approaches, such as regression and deep learning, are widely used for wind power forecasting, these methods often require large datasets and substantial computational power. Although parallel computing methods can help improve performance, they are typically limited in scope. In contrast, quantum computing represents a new computational paradigm, offering advantages in natural parallelization and efficient data processing. This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical model for power forecasting of offshore wind farms. In the proposed model, a quantum neural network is employed as a feature extractor, while support vector regression performs the forecasting task. This study marks one of the initial steps in exploring the opportunities offered by quantum computing beyond classical methods in wind power forecast. The results demonstrate the applicability of quantum-classical hybrid models to computationally intensive problems such as energy production.

articleTitle: Procedures of Analysis and Design for Microgrid Supplied Power by An Inverter with Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A micro grid is defined as a part of power system it operates connected to a large power system normally, it is required to operate independently during a long blackout of the large power system. The independent operation will give higher resilience in the power system and it is important in our life. The design of the micro grid is not easy because it must operate in connection with the large power system and operate independently also. A guide line for study for a micro grid is announced by public sectors, however, the procedures for conducting analysis and simulations to satisfy guideline items are not clear. This paper presents necessary procedures to make study, kinds of standard evaluation criteria or guideline for designing micro grid.

articleTitle: Multilevel PFC Converter Based on Flying-Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a multilevel PFC converter based on a flying capacitor design, which reduces voltage stress on MOSFETs and achieves three voltage levels using sinusoidal pulse width shift sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM). This control method is simple, with the inductor current exhibiting a double-frequency ripple, contributing to improve the input current performance. A 500W prototype was developed, operating with a 110V AC input and delivering a 200V DC output with a power factor of 0.998. The lowest total harmonic distortion (THD) of the input current is 3.84%. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed converter, making it suitable for off-line power supplies where stable DC output, and low THD are critical for optimal system performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Supercapacitor Assisted Multilevel Inverter Topology for Off-Grid Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Supercapacitor assisted (SCA) techniques are a new family of power electronic building blocks for renewable energy systems based on the theory published as SCA-loss management (SCALoM) concept. SCA inverter is a unique application of SCALoM theory, capable of meeting any capacity of off-grid inverter requirement, based on a combination of an even number of smaller inverters with suitably sized supercapacitor banks. SCA-inverter technique reduces input loop losses and transistor voltage stresses while providing DC-UPS capability without using batteries. This paper discusses the technical background of the SCA-inverter arrangement of operating seamlessly without common load balancing issues observed in other multi-inverter systems and techniques. The experiment results of two/four-SCA-inverter arrangement show stable operation of the inverter systems, both in switching transients of the supercapacitor banks and steady state operation. Four-SCA-inverter arrangement shows up to 2.5% efficiency improvement by equally partitioning the load into four inverters with no load balancing issues. As the four supercapacitor modules are switched at millihertz order frequency, it eliminaties the need for any EMC filters and dynamic losses in the frontend SCA arrangement are negligible.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Frequency Control by Grid Side Converter of PMSG-Based Wind Turbine Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The development of offshore wind farms are being advanced in Japan and Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators (PMSGs) are widely used there. Penetration of inverter-based power resources (IBRs) into power system reduces inertia of the system. As IBRs increase, concerns on deviations in system frequency are emerging. In wind turbine generation, PMSG is connected to the external system through a back-to-back (BTB) converter. BTB converter consist of Machine Side Converter (MSC), Grid Side Converter (GSC) and DC capacitor. Active power output of PMSG is controlled by GSC. The voltage of the DC capacitor has to be kept constant and it is generally controlled by GSC. In this study, we focus on the issue on system frequency and aims to improve the frequency deviation by controlling the active power output of PMSG by the GSC and controlling the capacitor voltage by MSC. The usefulness of the proposed control scheme is investigated through numerical simulations using XTAP, an electromagnetic transient analysis program. The results showed that the proposed control scheme is capable of suppressing frequency deviation successfully.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Hydrogen-Detecting Characteristics of Diode-Based Gas-Sensing Devices at Elevated Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Diode-based gas-sensing devices using titanium dioxide (anodized titania, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) films and platinum (Pt)-based electrodes coated with or without gold (Au(fi)/BE/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or BE/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, respectively, ft: film thickness of gold (Au) deposited by radio-frequency magnetron sputtering (9 [nm]), BE (base electrode): Pt or (100-x)Pt-xPd (x: 14–50 [wt%])) were fabricated and their hydrogen (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)-detecting characteristics were evaluated in this work. The response of the 64Pt-36Pd/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> diode to 980 ppb H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in dry nitrogen was larger than that of the Pt/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> diode, probably because the addition of Pd to Pt increased the amounts of dissociative hydrogen adsorbates on the Pt-electrode surface and dissolved hydrogen species into the Pt-electrode. In addition, the coating of Au significantly enhanced the response in dry nitrogen (typical responses to 980 ppb H2 under a forward bias of 100 mV: ca. 1.8 mA for the Au(20)/Pt/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> diode, ca. 8.6 mA for the Au(20)/64Pt-36Pd/TO2 diode). The coating of Au probably decreased the number of oxygen adsorbates on the BE electrode surface to consume H2, thereby increasing the effective hydrogen concentration over the surface. The Au(20)/64Pt-36Pd/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> diode exhibited the largest response especially to less than 5 ppm H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> among all sensors tested, and the sensor sensitively detected even a quite low concentration of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(98 ppb).

articleTitle: Accurate ESR Monitoring of a DC-Link Capacitor with Switching Ripple Voltage by a Leafony
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Condition monitoring helps improve the reliability of power electronic converters including their DC-link capacitors because it can predict converter failure and degradation. In practice, however, condition monitoring usually utilizes sensors to obtain health condition, which are constraint with regard to cost and size. This paper proposes condition monitoring method of DC- link capacitor in a three-phase PWM inverter with a front-end six- pulse diode rectifier by a Leafony that is a tiny microcontroller. The proposed method measures equivalent-series resistance (ESR) of the capacitor, where the Leafony is utilized to sense the switching ripple voltage of the DC-link capacitor and to perform a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis of the switching ripple voltage of the DC-link capacitor. Experimental results obtained from a 200-V laboratory system have confirmed that measuring the switching ripple voltage improves the accuracy of the ESR.

articleTitle: Investigation of Innovative Battery Storage Systems for Shipboard Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The evolution of waterborne transport is toward more sustainable systems. Electric ships with batteries as energy supplies sources are viable solutions for specific applications. In the paper a modular hybrid energy system (HESS) based on batteries of different parameters is analyzed and a control algorithm able to equalize the state of charge (SOC) is verified by simulation in both standard operation and in presence of faults.

articleTitle: Consideration of Hydrogen Utilization By Using Railway Assets
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The JR-West Group is working toward achieving virtually zero CO2 emissions by 2050 as stated in “JR-West Group Zero Carbon 2050” announced in April 2021, and is considering the use of hydrogen as one of its main tool of success. The Hydrogen Society Promotion Act, which was enacted in May 2024, regards hydrogen as a key energy and a raw material for promoting GX (Green Transformation), and aims to contribute to the realization of a hydrogen society, as well as the decarbonization in the region by using the railway asset network.

articleTitle: DC Microgrid Reliability Enhancement with Adaptive Converter Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Due to the different device selections, aging levels, and thermal dissipation performance, some converters may take additional thermal stress on switching devices than others in paralleled converter systems, which will reduce system reliability. To address this problem, this paper proposes a power-sharing strategy with adaptive thermal management. First, the temperature-based power loss model and electrical-thermal model are established. Based on that, a high-accuracy IGBT junction temperature estimate considering the power loss-temperature coupling can be achieved. Further, the thermal-sharing for all the switching devices in paralleled converters can be achieved with the proposed adaptive thermal management strategy. The proposed strategy can change the power-sharing ratio adaptively according to the system operation conditions, which will contribute to the system reliability enhancement. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified through PLECS thermal simulation and joint real-time simulation with Dspace and RT-box.

articleTitle: Electric Power Control of a Heat Generation System using a Rotating Heater
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In recent years, power generation based on renewable energy has increased, and there is duration when surplus power is generated due to seasonal and weather conditions. To solve this problem, it has been proposed to convert this surplus power into heat for grid stability and use it for chemical plants and other needs. Additionally, a system using a rotating heater (RH) with a structure like a squirrel-cage induction motor instead of a conventional Joule heater for more efficient heat conversion has been proposed. In this study, the RH is driven by an inverter and generates heat from the mechanical input of the induction motor connected to the grid. Therefore, by controlling the mechanical torque of the induction motor (IM), the power from the grid is controlled and converted into heat. In addition, a method to control the input power to the RH and the power from the grid through the IM independently by a single inverter is investigated, and experiments are conducted using a 1kW-class small-scale experimental system to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An 18-kW Wide-Output-Range Bidirectional DC Power Supply with 80V, 600A Using Totem-Pole Bridgeless PFC
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces an 18-kW wide-output-range bidirectional DC power supply with 80V, 600A using single-phase totem-pole bridgeless Power Factor Correction (PFC) circuit. The developed DC power supply is capable of 2.67 times output-current range (from 225A to 600A) at the rated power of 18 kW under AC 200V input. The DC power supply consists of three single-phase 6-kW AC-DC converters (AC-DC CONVs). And the AC-DC CONV is composed of three-stage converter, which includes single-phase Totem-Pole Bridgeless PFC (TP-BL PFC) circuit, the bidirectional LLC converter with fixed-frequency operation, and four-phase interleaved non-isolated bidirectional DC-DC converter. To achieve high efficiency, the single-phase TP-BL PFC circuit is adopted in three-phase input system. Isolated DC-DC converter is adopted to a bidirectional full-bridge LLC converter with fixed-frequency operation because the output voltage for the LLC converter is not needed to be regulated. In addition, minimizing a voltage rating of power devices for non-isolated bidirectional DC-DC converter can be used because the secondary bus-line voltage is kept stable. To confirm the feasibility of the developed DC power supply, a prototype is manufactured and tested. The measured overall efficiency at the rated power is around 91% at the rated current condition and over 93 % at the rated-voltage condition, respectively. In this paper, the results of the test equipment are shown, which is using the developed bidirectional DC power supply for realizing high energy saving in factories. This means that the low power losses of the developed bidirectional DC power supply can enhance environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Research on Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on an ICEEMDAN-FuIILinear-TSMixer-CNN Combined Model
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In response to the challenges of high randomness, significant fluctuations, and low prediction accuracy in wind power, we propose an improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) method to decompose wind power data. The decomposed components are then sorted and regrouped using a multi-scale permutation entropy algorithm. Subsequently, these regrouped components are analyzed and predicted using a combination of fully connected linear (FullLinear), time-series mixer (TSMixer), and convolutional neural network (CNN). The final prediction values are obtained by combining the results of these predictions. Validation using SCADA data from a Turkish wind turbine indicates that this method significantly improves prediction performance compared to single models, with an overall improvement of approximately 40% to 50%. This approach enables accurate short-term wind power prediction, providing a solid foundation for the stable operation and optimal scheduling of the power grid.

articleTitle: Design of Modularized High Step-Up Converter with Improved Light-Load Efficiency for Power Semiconductor Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a modularized power module (PM) designed to enhance efficiency during light-load conditions, which is critical for power semiconductor testing. The proposed system features a cascaded architecture that enables a wide output voltage range of 0 to 1200V while maintaining high efficiency across various operating conditions. The modular design enables the series connection of multiple PMs, offering flexibility and scalability in high-voltage applications. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the design, demonstrating its ability to operate efficiently under light-load conditions. This paper addresses the challenges associated with high-voltage generation and contributes to modular design strategies that reduce system complexity, ultimately improving the performance of power semiconductor testing platforms.

articleTitle: Modeling and Gain Design for Multi-Cycle Controlled LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Energy harvesting is emerging as a key power source for IoT devices, but the minimal power it provides necessitates efficient utilization. LLC resonant converters, known for their high efficiency due to soft switching, need higher switching frequencies to meet the miniaturization demands of IoT devices. Controlling such high-frequency SMPSs (Switched-Mode Power Supplies) with digital controllers poses challenges. Multi-cycle control, which updates control outputs every few switching cycles, has been proposed to address this issue. This study investigates the loop transfer function model of an LLC resonant converter with multi-cycle control. In addition, using this model, we designed the controller gain and validated the model's accuracy and the effectiveness of the designed gain through experimental results.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking of Series-Parallel Connected Bifacial PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Bifacial photovoltaic (BiPV) modules capture solar energy from their front and rear surfaces, posing unique challenges due to their exposure to non-uniform irradiance and temperature variations. In the pursuit of optimizing the energy output of BiPV systems, this paper focuses on investigating the effectiveness of the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods of series-parallel (SP) connected BiPV modules using advanced metaheuristic algorithms like the genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and gray wolf optimizer (GWO). The efficiency of the selected techniques is compared to each other in tracking the maximum power point (MPP) of a (2 × 2) BiPV array feeding a DC/DC converter under three different cases. Through detailed simulations, the results demonstrate that these algorithms can significantly enhance the energy yield of BiPV arrays of SP configurations. The findings indicate that selecting an optimization strategy is essential to increasing the overall effectiveness of BiPV systems. Each methodology provides unique benefits depending on the operating circumstances.

articleTitle: SOC-Based Mode Switching in Hybrid Battery Systems for Electric Motorcycles
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid battery management system for motorcycles that switches operational modes based on the State of Charge (SOC) of a secondary battery. Traditional systems often face the problem of the secondary battery depleting during driving. To address this issue, the proposed system dynamically adjusts between power boost and energy-saving modes, aiming to optimize energy efficiency and extend battery life. Experimental results confirm that the sub-battery successfully provides power boost, and when its SOC falls below 20% or rises above 80%, the proposed system seamlessly switches to main battery-only operation.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling of Electric Vehicle Charging Sessions: an Empirical Validation of an Italy - France Route
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The transition to Electric Vehicles (EVs) represents a significant change in the mobility sector, promising greater environmental sustainability, safety and efficiency. Despite these benefits, EVs adoption is hampered by range anxiety. This study presents a predictive model designed to estimate the number of charging sessions needed for an EV under various usage scenarios. The model simulates the behaviour of the electric vehicle through a network of Charging Stations (CSs) and evaluates its performance by comparing the simulated results with real data. To validate the model, an experimental test is conducted on the Bergamo-Paris route. The vehicle required three charging sessions, consistent with the model's predictions. This model is critical for optimizing energy management strategies, potentially alleviating range anxiety and driving EVs adoption.

articleTitle: Loss of Grid Behavior for a Grid Forming ESS Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into the power grid poses both opportunities and challenges, especially to grid stability and reliability. The grid forming inverter ensures that load experiences no interruption in power supply in event of absence of utility. This paper investigates the performance of a grid-forming energy storage system inverter rated at 700kW during loss of grid. The study is driven by the need to understand how these systems can contribute to a stable grid in the face of increasing reliance on distributed energy resources. Various test cases are considered focusing on different load parameters to investigate inverter's response under diverse operating conditions. Using a Controller Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation environment, inverter is tested for loss of grid for different loads and different voltage/reactive power droop settings.

articleTitle: Edge-Side Data Squashing and Metric Learning for Energy Prosumer Clustering: Toward Parameter Optimization of Residential Photovoltaic Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As power systems change due to widespread use of distributed energy resources (DERs), power distribution system operators (DSOs) face the challenge of determining the appropriate operational DER parameters to improve power flow conditions. In particular, a scheme that allows cooperatively adjusting their personalized DER parameters by considering the power flow data measured at their endpoints represents a promising approach for effectively achieving power flow control. It is essential to determine tailor-made parameters that accurately reflect the differences in power flow conditions at individual prosumers based on the measured data. Meanwhile, the centralized data accumulation and management increase operational costs and burdens owing to the rise in excessive communication and storage capacity. In this study, we propose an approach to squash the high-dimensional data measured from the thousands of DERs into low-dimensional data and cluster prosumers with similar power flow conditions. We focus on prosumers who installed residential photovoltaic power (PV) with individual smart inverters; DSOs require personalized optimization for inverter parameters to avoid PV generation loss. The proposed scheme was applied to high-dimensional power flow data measured from thousands of prosumers. The results show that the proposed method effectively encapsulates the power flow conditions while reducing the dimensionality of prosumer data into low-dimensional features.

articleTitle: Magnet Temperature Detection of PMSM with Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Temperature information of the magnet on permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) is crucial to prevent failures caused by the thermal demagnetization of magnets. This paper proposes a detection method for the magnet temperature of PMSMs using a wireless power transfer (WPT) system with a thermistor. The magnet temperature is measured by the NTC thermistor, which is connected to the secondary side of a WPT system. The temperature change of the magnet is detected through the change in the input power on the primary side. The prototype of the WPT system is designed and demonstrated based on the characteristics of the thermistor.

articleTitle: Durability Testing of Battery-Electrolysers for Hydrogen Cooking and Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper investigates the development and testing of a lead-acid battery-electrolyser over a minimum 6-month period from autumn 2023. A lead-acid battery-electrolyser is a single device with dual functions that serves both as a battery for energy storage and as an electrolyser for hydrogen production. The study involved the fabrication of three battery-electrolyser cells, that were subjected to long-term durability tests under various cycling modes, including battery-only, electrolyser-only, and battery-electrolyser operations. The tests aimed to accelerate degradation and simulate real-world conditions typical of remote off-grid communities. Results showed a 27% capacity decrease in the cell operating as a battery after 398 discharge cycles. The cell operating as a battery-electrolyser exhibited a 21% capacity loss after 198 deep discharge cycles. In contrast, the third cell, operating as an electrolyser only, showed negligible capacity change, indicating minimal degradation. These findings demonstrate the ability to use a lead-acid battery as a means of hydrogen production but underscore the challenges in achieving a target of 2000 cycles for commercial viability. The paper concludes by suggesting that further improvements in cell design are required to achieve improved cell performance. This study contributes valuable insights into the durability and potential of lead-acid battery-electrolysers for sustainable energy applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Switching Speed of Electrochromic Energy Storage Devices: Application in Smart Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The cost of energy storage devices (ESDs) is reduced via the exploitation of the electrochromic (EC) properties. Due to its low-cost and outstanding cycling capability, nickel oxide (NiO) is considered an excellent candidate for the electrode material of electrochromic and energy storage devices (EC-ESDs). Nevertheless, NiO offers a slow switching speed, which limits the application of the EC-ESDs. To overcome this limitation, the surface of the fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) is modified. The achieved values of switching speeds for the coloration and bleach are found to be 0.86 and 0.29 s. Moreover, the obtained optical modulation (OM) is -77% @ 550 nm along with a coloration efficiency of -42 cm2/C. It offered an areal capacitance of -130 mF/cm2 @ 5 mV/s.

articleTitle: Fast and Stable Current Control Using Deadbeat PI Control with Smith Compensator
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast and stable current control method that can achieve deadbeat characteristics even in the presence of delays that occur in experimental systems. Deadbeat control is a promising method for high-speed current control. However, it is generally difficult to implement advanced deadbeat control in terms of calculation. Therefore, we focused on deadbeat PI control, which can be easily implemented by only designing PI gains. In implementing deadbeat control to achieve such a fast response in an experimental system, processing delays need to be considered. This is because the response to be realized is so fast that the system tends to degrade and be unstable due to the processing delay. Therefore, this paper aims to realize a fast and stable deadbeat PI current control by combining Smith compensation which is often used as a delay compensation method. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by analysis, simulation, and experiment.

articleTitle: Expansion of Switched Reluctance Motor Driving Range by Flux-weakening Control under Current Vector Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel flux-weakening control for switched reluctance motors (SRMs) driven by current vector control. The proposed method enhances the advantage of SRMs being capable of high-speed rotation. This paper shows the calculation method of the dq0-axis currents of the proposed method. Furthermore, the expansion effect of the driving range of the proposed method compared to the conventional method is shown. The rotational speed range has been expanded by up to 770 min<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Experimental verification shows that the proposed method can achieve current vector control under high-speed rotation conditions, which would be over-modulated by conventional methods. Furthermore, the experimental results of the efficiency map showed that the proposed method expanded the range of high efficiency and linear controllable area.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection and Factor Estimation Using Graph Neural Network with Storage Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is a technique to conserve maintenance before failure by finding their indications in advance and it is the key effective maintenance operations and reduced downtime. Methods for predictive maintenance based on anomaly detection of sensors using deep learning have been actively studied, but the identification of anomalous sensors remains a challenging task. As sensors corresponding to the cause of anomaly do not necessarily indicate large anomaly scores. In this work, we use a graph neural network for anomaly detection and factor estimation. The vertices of the graph that appears in the network correspond to the sensors, so we can interpret the relevant weights as the relationship between the sensors. We specifically used sparse graph to improve interpretability of graph, and we confirmed the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network-based Grid Impedance Identification Method of Grid-connected Converter with Grid-following and Grid-forming Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This article presents an artificial neural network (ANN)-based grid impedance identification method for grid-connected converter (GCC) system with grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) control. A general model of GCC in both GFL and GFM is first established. The necessary components of output voltage, including fundamental component and harmonic component(s), are then extracted for ANN training. Finally, the experimental results verify the effectiveness of proposed method. The proposed ANN-based identification method can precisely predict both grid inductance (GI) and grid resistance (GR) with simpler modelling process, more accuracy and much less data, which optimizes and perfects the grid impedance identification method in both GFL and GFM.

articleTitle: High Boost-Ratio Multi-Source Inverter Based on Sinusoidally-Modulated Floating-Output Series-Interleaved GaN Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents an original solution for harvesting power from multiple sources of different characteristics and delivering it onto a single or three-phase sinusoidal output, without the need for individual DC-DC converters and high voltage capacitive DC-Link interconnection. Specifically, it looks at a high boost-ratio implementation of such approach, which uses gallium nitride high electron-mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) based high switching frequency floating-output series-interleaved boost DC-DC converter cells. The results show the possibility to generate a Japanese-standard mains compatible outlet (100 Vrms/50 Hz) directly from supply voltages as low as 30 V.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Among Multisampling Methods for Three-Phase Grid-Connected Cascaded H - Bridge Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative analysis among three multisampling methods is performed. The considered multisampling techniques have been already proposed in literature, however, in this work, they are applied to a suppressed carrier arrangement-driven grid-connected cascaded h-bridge inverter. The comparative analysis is carried out by analyzing the system dynamic and harmonic behavior. First, the considered multisampling techniques are explicated through the modulation patterns. Subsequently, the comparative analysis is performed through Hardware-In-the-Loop real-time tests and both the system dynamic and harmonic content are investigated. Results show that the higher sampling frequency technique guarantees the best dynamic and harmonic performances.

articleTitle: Trends in the Electric Vehicle Charging Stations and Spatial Distribution by Charger Type in Fukuoka
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study examines the trends in electric vehicle charging stations and chargers in Fukuoka from 2021 to 2024, categorized into rapid and general chargers. The number of electric vehicle charging stations increased from 147 to 191. Rapid chargers grew from 63 to 91, while general chargers rose from 172 to 231, though rapid chargers remain below 30% of the total. Kernel Density shows the highest density around Tenjin in Chuo Ward, with general chargers being denser than rapid chargers. CHAdeMO Rapid, 200V, and Charger with Cable are characterized by having high-density areas in Nishi, Higashi and Sawara Ward, respectively, outside of Chuo Ward.

articleTitle: Development of Pole-Changing Generator for Small Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This report describes the development of a generator for small wind power generation. This generator has a wide power band. Therefore, it can be effectively used as a small wind power generator. The output voltage, output current, and torque of the generator can be changed by switching the internal coil connections. To confirm these characteristics, tests were conducted using an induction machine and a wind turbine. As a result, it was confirmed that the developed generator can keep up with the maximum power of a small wind turbine. Small wind power generation using the proposed generator was proposed as one method to promote the use of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Digital Predictive-based Interleaving Control Scheme for Critical Conduction Mode Boost PFC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel digital predictive-based interleaving control scheme for the boost PFC converter operating in critical conduction mode. In the proposed method, the switching on-time and off-time for achieving CRM operation are determined by analytical equations of the PFC converter, eliminating the need for zero-crossing point detection circuits. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits more stable CRM interleaving against the parameters mismatching compared with the previous methods. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control.

articleTitle: M3C-based Bipolar DC Transmission Scheme for Offshore Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Bipolar transmission schemes for offshore wind power can improve transmission reliability and have received wide attention in recent years. It usually uses two modular multilevel converters (MMCs) to form a bipolar transmission structure, which increases the construction and maintenance costs. In this paper, a bipolar transmission scheme for offshore wind power based on modular multilevel matrix converters (M3C) is proposed. Based on the principle of bridge arm multiplexing, the number of valves is reduced to 3/4 than the traditional scheme. However, due to the reduction in the number of bridge arms, the control freedom of M3C is also reduced. In this regard, this paper proposes a switching matrix casting strategy, which controls the switching tubes in the sub modules of each bridge arm by casting matrices, and realizes the autonomous balancing of submodule capacitance voltages by using the matrix theory. In the end, the feasibility and effectiveness of this strategy are verified by a simulation model of the M3C applying the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: De-loading Control and Grid Frequency Support of the Dynamic Low Frequency Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the penetration rate of wind power in the power grid, grid frequency support is more and more important. To date, the frequency support of variable speed constant frequency wind farms sent out by flexible DC transmission has been solved, including using grid frequency detection signals to construct additional power commands for grid-following wind turbines, grid-forming wind turbine with autonomous inertia response capability, and some studies have solved the problem of providing grid frequency information to wind farms in flexible DC transmission without relying on communication. However, flexible DC wind farms rely on expensive high-voltage and high-capacity offshore converter stations, and the dispersed offshore wind turbine inverters face reliability risks. This article focuses on the frequency support research of a novel dynamic low-frequency wind power system, which does not require wind turbine inverters and large offshore converter stations, and adopts variable voltage and variable frequency low-frequency AC transmission. In response to the problem of low control freedom, a sophisticated control design has been implemented to achieve power de-loading operation prioritizing speed acceleration and then pitch action, thereby meeting the requirements of power grid dispatch operation or power reserve for frequency support. Then a comprehensive frequency support strategy that can achieve fast inertia response and primary frequency regulation of the entire wind farm has been proposed. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed control strategy were verified through electromagnetic transient simulation.

articleTitle: Current Situation and Issues of Hydrogen Generation System Fueled by Sodium Borohydride
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The global energy demand is increasing, and there is a need for safe energy supply and environmentally friendly energy generation. In Japan, the low energy self-sufficiency rate is also an issue, and hydrogen energy, which can provide a stable energy supply, is attracting attention. Hydrogen energy source is a next-generation energy source that can help reduce dependence on fossil fuels; however, its widespread use has been slow due to persistent challenges in its transportation and storage methods. In response, the authors have been conducting research and development on a hydrogen generation system using sodium borohydride as a fuel. This paper provides an overview of the hydrogen generation system that has been developed and the current efforts.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization Strategies for Totem Pole PFC Under Light Load DCM Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel synchronous rectification (SR) switching strategy for Continuous Conduction Mode (CCM) Totem-pole Power Factor Correction (PFC). The study primarily addresses efficiency issues of PFC under light load conditions. By introducing an additional Zero Current Detection (ZCD) circuit, the system operates in Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM) during light loads, thereby enhancing efficiency. This study uses small-signal analysis to address the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) issue of PFC in DCM and improves current distortion through DCM Duty-Ratio Feedforward (DFF). PLECS simulations confirm the effectiveness of ZCD and DFF. The research enhances PFC efficiency under light load conditions and resolves the DCM THD problem, with findings validated on a 1 kW PFC converter.

articleTitle: Roles of Photovoltaic Generation Systems in Microgrid Forming with Large Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Microgrids, as a cornerstone of smart grids, can bolster grid resilience by integrating various renewable energy resources, including Photovoltaic Generation Systems (PVGSs), Energy Storage Systems (ESSs), etc., and by supplying power independently during extreme events. Despite their many advantages, microgrid forming faces challenges due to the diverse equipment in industrial parks. Specifically, large motors require about 5–7 times their rated current for startup, which can create significant difficulties during microgrid forming. Therefore, establishing a startup sequence for large motors is crucial. Large motors typically demand substantial reactive power during startup. Integrating controllable reactive power sources, such as PVGSs, with ESSs can mitigate the impact on the ESSs during startup and enhance the success rate of microgrid forming. This paper explores the role of PVGSs in microgrid forming with large induction motors. This study simulates a microgrid consisting of an ESS with a rated capacity of 8.8 MWh and a PVGS with a rated power of 900 kW in an industrial park. It examines simultaneous and sequential motor startup sequences during microgrid forming without and with PVGS under different power factors. Simulation results demonstrate that the reactive power control of PVGSs can effectively improve microgrid forming with large induction motors.

articleTitle: A Common-Signal Driven Split Output Gate Driver for Si/SiC Hybrid Switches to Realize Zero-Voltage Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A split output gate driver (sp-GD) is proposed for silicon/silicon carbide (Si/SiC) hybrid switches (HyS) to realize zero-voltage switching (ZVS). The HyS comprises a silicon (Si) insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) and a silicon carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) connected in parallel, functioning as a single switch. The sp-GD integrates AND/OR logic gates with a resistor-capacitor delay circuit. It operates with a single gate signal but is engineered to control the timing of this signal, ensuring that the SiC MOSFET turns on before the Si IGBT and turns off after the Si IGBT. This design compensates for the slower switching response of the Si IGBT, especially during its turn-off phase. The efficacy of the sp-GD has been validated experimentally, demonstrating an up to a 40% reduction in total switching losses of the HyS compared to a conventional single output gate driver (conv-GD). Furthermore, simulations of a photovoltaic inverter using the HyS indicate that the sp-GD enhances inverter efficiency by up to 4.2 % relative to the conv-GD.

articleTitle: Efficient Integration of Industrial Sector Coupling Systems in DC Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The European Green Deal, launched in December 2019, emphasises green hydrogen as a key element for achieving climate neutrality within the EU by 2050. Green hydrogen, primarily produced through electrolysis and powered by renewable energy sources such as photovoltaic systems, plays a vital role in industrial sector coupling. Integration of industrial sector coupling systems, encompassing electrolysers, fuel cells, and heat pumps, is critical for increasing energy efficiency and decarbonisation efforts. Such systems inherently operate in direct current (DC) or utilise DC at the converter level. This paper examines the efficiency advantages of DC distribution grids over conventional alternating current (AC) infrastructures for sector coupling applications. The WAVE-H2 research platform in Freudenstadt, Germany, serves as the basis for experimental testing of these systems under both AC and DC conditions. The study outlines the platform's electrical infrastructure, evaluates the power supply configuration for state-of-the-art sector coupling systems, and proposes steps for transitioning to a DC supply input. Simulations comparing AC and DC scenarios reveal notable efficiency gains due to reduced conversion and transmission losses. The simulation analysis shows that integrating industrial-scale systems into DC distribution grids could achieve energy savings of up to 4.2%, highlighting the preference for DC technology.

articleTitle: Current-Limiting Vector Control for Pulse-Load Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Parallel boost circuits are commonly employed to deliver reliable power supply for loads that demand high voltages and currents over short durations. However, the prevailing control method, based on traditional PI control, introduces several limitations. These include significant voltage dips and extended adjustment times, which can adversely impact load performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel control strategy termed Current Limiting Control (CLC). Initially, a mathematical model of the circuit is constructed to facilitate an analysis of the switching states, complemented by equations and three-dimensional visualizations of various states. Subsequently, a three-stage control strategy is introduced to mitigate voltage drops and minimize adjustment time while maintaining current balance across the inductors of the two BOOST circuits. Finally, simulations and experimental results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the dynamic performance under heavy load conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Micro-Reactor for Hydrogen Production from Solid $\text{NaBH}_{4}$ Hydrolysis
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: At the Ariel Fluid Dynamics Lab, we developed a pump-based hydrogen generator utilizing a catalytic reaction between NaBH4 powder and water. The pump circulates the water solution through the powder chamber in a closed-loop reaction, exhibiting clear advantages in safety and energy density over alternative hydrogen sources. Novel concepts are presented for extension of operating time including freshwater feeding from external source (such as in marine vehicles, near pipelines), or water recovered from the FC. Introducing freshwater feeding and product emission in such scenarios offers possibilities for significantly enhancing fuel energy density and extending effective operation time.
