The study includes extensive examples of prototypes and a validated numerical model that allows for performance optimization and system scalability. The numerical model validation against experimental measurements showed a relative cumulative error of less than 9%. The achieved fuel energy density is 3868 Wh/kg for the first hour, with a 93 % H2 extraction yield from the powder. For long-term operation, the fuel energy density reduces to 2900 Wh/kg with a 99% H2 extraction yield. This methodology holds promise for long-term mobile applications or off-grid systems and may contribute to further optimization of power packs for versatile applications.

articleTitle: Common Mode Noise Reduction with Balance Technique Considering Soft Saturation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Balance techniques have been widely utilized to reduce common-mode (CM) noise. Powder cores, however, introduced soft saturation characteristics which disrupt balance conditions. This is because the leakage flux increases at heavy loads, resulting in decrease of coupling coefficient. In this study, the effect of the soft saturation characteristics of powder cores on the balance condition is investigated. Additionally, a winding structure minimizing the leakage flux by using foil winding is proposed. The proposed structure achieves a high coupling coefficient regardless of load conditions, confirmed by static magnetic field simulations. The CM noises of the conventional and proposed winding structures are compared in various load conditions from 0.5 kW to 4 kW and verified the effectiveness of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Feasible Sub-Network Enumeration and Combination Approach for Loss Minimization in Locally PV-Dense Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In this study, we discuss a system configuration approach to minimize distribution losses by optimizing the switching states of sectionalizing switches. Specifically, the approach aims to determine the loss-minimum configuration in distribution networks with dense, localized photovoltaic (PV) system integration by enumerating and effectively combining feasible sub-network configurations. This approach overcomes the limitations of previous studies, which struggled to derive accurate loss-minimizing configurations under static load conditions, especially without accounting for such concentrated PV installations. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations on a representative distribution system model.

articleTitle: A Soft-Switching Modular Three-Phase Dynamic Voltage Restorer with Fictitious DC-Link
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a soft-switching modular three-phase dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) with a fictitious DC- link. The proposed structure can maintain load voltage stability under undervoltage, overvoltage, voltage sag, and voltage swell. The proposed scheme combines three single-phase modules, each incorporating a single-phase rectifier with a soft-switching inverter in a fictitious DC-link. The single-phase rectifier uses line-frequency switching and is synchronous to the source voltage to reduce switching loss. By using simple resonant circuits, all the inverter's main switches operate in zero-voltage switching (ZVS) mode during the on period, while the auxiliary switches operate in zero-current switching (ZCS) mode during the off period. This structure can minimize switching loss, mitigate voltage stress, and decrease EMI. The use of small AC capacitors in the DC link extends the life of the DVR while reducing its size. The soft- switching three-phase DVR simulation waveforms are provided to demonstrate the performance.

articleTitle: Method for Estimating Power Losses in Low-Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In the proposed work, the study of a section of the shop network of an industrial enterprise with the determination of the equivalent circuit resistance. The calculation method presents the errors in the failure to take into account each of the considered parameters of the network. Causes and main damages of switching devices for voltage 0.4 kV are given. The main factor that influences in determining the equivalent resistance of the investigated circuit is the resistance of low-voltage switching devices. Determination of the type of empirical dependence of the resistance of devices depends on the current flowing through the contact connections. The error at non-calculation of this parameter for the mixed section of the power supply scheme reaches 77.15 %. Neglecting the heating temperature of conductors when calculating the equivalent resistance also has a significant impact and leads to an error of 5.6 %. Also neglecting the line loading factor and ambient temperature in determining the circuit resistance leads to an error of 3.17 % and 2.4 %, respectively. The results of the study can be used to assess the level of power and energy losses in low-voltage shop networks, which will significantly increase the reliability of the data obtained.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Instability in a Power Grid with Multiple Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: IBRs (Inverter-Based Resources) have been widely connected to the conventional power grid, where grid-forming (GFM) control attracts attention for enhancing the grid's stability. This paper uses a test grid model with 4 GFM inverters connected to the infinite bus and reports its time-domain simulation using a nonlinear state-space model. We show that instability phenomena occur in the grid model and are affected by the parameters of GFM control and the grid's codition.

articleTitle: Development of a Power Supply for Optogenetic Devices Used in Continuous Mouse Experiments with Renal Sympathetic Nerve Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a growing global health issue with no fundamental cure, prompting the need for innovative treatment approaches. In this context, our research, in collaboration with medical doctors and co-researchers, focuses on the protective effects of sympathetic nerve stimulation in the kidneys, aiming to develop new therapeutic strategies. Traditional methods, such as pharmacological or electrical nerve stimulation, lack precision, affecting a broad range of nerves. In contrast, our proposed solar-powered optogenetics device, fixed on a mouse's back, offers a high level of precision in localized neural stimulation via blue light. This device is powered by solar cells under high-brightness LED lighting installed in the mouse cage. Unlike battery-operated devices that require frequent replacement, this system provides continuous stimulation, supporting long-term experiments with free-moving mice. In this presentation, our system represents the first application of optogenetics for kidney sympathetic nerve control, offering a novel approach to CKD treatment.

articleTitle: A Study of Rectifier Circuit Failure with Special Winding Type Twenty-four-phase Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper examines the effects of a missing diode in the rectifier circuit of a special winding twenty-four-phase transformer. Until recently, we studied AC-DC transformers developed for grid power in dc distribution networks. We developed a special winding structure transformer that reduces the number of windings more effectively than traditional designs. We found that when the positive-side diode of Rl was missing, the DC ripple increased by 8.35%. but when other locations were lacking, no change in DC voltage was observed. For line voltage, when the positive diode of phase Rl is missing, the base phase shifts from phase Rl to phase T8 and S6. When diodes in other phases are missing, the line voltage lacks one phase.

articleTitle: Improvement of Power Efficiency of Stirling Engine Power Supply Vehicle Based on Temperature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a temperature control aimed at achieving increased power output and improved efficiency of a Free-Piston Stirling Engine Generator (FPSEG) that generates electricity from a heat source by the combustion of woody biomass fuel, operating in a combined system with a PV charger and Li-ion batteries on a Stirling Engine Power Supply Vehicle. Based on the combustion furnace model and generator output characteristics, the power generation efficiency of the FPSEG system is effectively regulated. Additionally, a PD control with a feed-forward element is proposed to pre-adjust the input fuel amount based on the model-predicted temperature drop, thereby improving the impact of inverse response on the final temperature. The effectiveness of this control method is experimentally validated, confirming its potential to improve vehicle performance and stability.

articleTitle: Recent Energy-Saving Technologies for Railway Traction Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Electric railways offer an energy-efficient mode of transportation powered by electricity. However, recent environmental concerns have heightened the focus on energy savings within this sector. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of technologies and research aimed at enhancing energy efficiency in electric railways from multiple perspectives.

articleTitle: Developing an Ideal Model for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Locations
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study developed a model for selecting optimal locations for electric vehicle charger to establish an ideal charging infrastructure. Conducted in Fukuoka City, Japan, the study identified underserved areas in the outskirts of the city based on the current locations of charging stations and extracted service areas. To ensure service coverage in underserved regions, the study considered traffic volume by day of the week and time of day to determine optimal locations for charger accessible within 5 and 10 minutes. The results indicated that to establish a 5-minute accessible charging infrastructure, 65 to 74 additional stations are needed, while 11 to 13 additional stations are required for a 10-minute accessible infrastructure. The study demonstrates effectiveness in addressing infrastructure deficiencies in smaller cities compared to metropolitan areas and allowing flexible location selection based on peak and off-peak traffic volumes.

articleTitle: Model-based development of energy management systems for renewable energy
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: We are using Model Based Development (MBD) techniques to design and implement energy management systems such as solar-to-hydrogen conversion (STH) systems. We have applied model-based development to a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) system with a unique power supply configuration of our own design, and achieved a daily STH efficiency of 18.78%. This was the highest efficiency for a sub-kilowatt-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) system in outdoor operation at that time. The concentrating photovoltaic (CPV) module, electrolyzer, and DC-DC converter were precisely modeled based on actual measured component characteristics, simulation verification of control methods, and control software implemented using automatic code generation techniques. The control software was implemented using automatic code generation technology. In addition, the feasibility of applying the software to a mega solar system was verified to confirm its effectiveness in system design.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Wind Energy Assessment for Transmission Network Integration Considering the Location of Electrical Substations and Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wind energy is an abundant renewable resource that can support decarbonization of energy supply. It is, therefore, essential to conduct a comprehensive assessment of wind energy potential for effective transmission network planning and integration. This work introduces a spatial-temporal assessment method-ology for wind energy name plate-rated power capacity that considers the locations of electrical substations and transmission lines. This methodology applies Geographic Information System (GIS) land cover data to define siting exclusions for wind turbine installations. The correlation between generated wind power and estimates of power system load, as well as capacity factor, on a sub- regional basis for specific latest generation low and very low wind speed turbines, is estimated. A case study for the proposed methodology is conducted for the Commonwealth of Kentucky, USA with state-of-the-art wind turbines, land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD), and publicly available spatiotemporal wind data from the NASA EarthData Pathfinder dataset. The results indicate the availability of suitable land for wind turbine deployment, which can contribute to fulfilling the regional annual energy requirement, even with the example restricted sitting exclusion scenario in which turbines must be within 10km distance of a substation.

articleTitle: Investigation of Cable Line Heat Mode Parameters in Power Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The paper develops regression models of dependences of the estimated service life of cable line insulation on the load factor in various operating conditions. The study of thermal modes using approximation functions of the obtained results is carried out. The temperature parameters of the cable line with different types of insulation have been obtained. The results can be used to clarify the temperature modes of cable lines when selecting their cross-sections at the stage of design of electrical engineering systems.

articleTitle: Impactful Driving Performances for e-Bus Service Operations: Assessment Through Virtual Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The strong technical development of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is capturing mobility interests to delve with the energy transition. Despite the technical improvements are increasing the overall performances of EV subsystems, when deploying a public transport service the effect of driving style can play a critical component for the daily energy consumption and charging schedule. This paper presents an assessment of driving performances regarding the operational public service of electric buses by means of a virtual environment. The analysis is founded on a wide set of travelling data acquired remotely, then processed through a virtual e-Bus model developed in Matlab-Simulink. This approach allows to decouple sideways contributions impacting the overall energy consumption, thus isolating the human-related factors. Results show that the variability of energy consumption based on driving styles can be considerable among different drivers during the same daily shift considering the same bus line, reaching maximum values of +36%. For Transport Operators deploying e-Buses for public service, this leads to range reduction for each vehicle. A valuable countermeasure can be acting on training drivers thus to put into practice informed decisions for drivers, thus to reduce extra-consumption and extending the range of e-Buses.

articleTitle: Impacts of the Sampling Interval of Economic Load Dispatching Control on the Performance of Automatic Generation Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The paper examines the impacts of the sampling interval of economic load dispatching control (EDC) on the performance of automatic generation control (AGC) of a power system. As the penetration of solar and wind power generation increases, the frequency control of a power system faces more challenges because the increase causes more fluctuations as well as forecasting errors in their output. The improvement of AGC systems is thus indispensable in a power system with high penetration of solar and wind power generation. The importance of EDC - a part of AGC systems in charge of the fluctuation period longer than about 20 minutes - is increasing because the output fluctuations of solar and wind power generation contain considerable fluctuations with the period. The paper examines the impacts of the sampling interval of EDC on the performance of AGC through the simulation with, the standard AGC model of IEE, Japan - i.e., AGC30 [1]. We change the sampling interval of EDC from 1 minute to 10 minutes (its default value: 5 minutes) in the simulation study. In the study, we assume forecast error in the outputs of intermittent renewables because, EDC being a predictive control with the forecast values, the forecast error strongly affects its performance. The results implicate the importance of proper parameter setting in EDC to improve the performance of AGC.

articleTitle: A Wind Speed Interval Prediction Framework Based on Machine Learning Models and Kernel Density Estimation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Predicting wind speed is crucial in the wind energy sector, especially for controlling and balancing production and consumption in smart grids. However, wind speed is characterized by high uncertainty and variability. These fluctuations in wind speed are obvious in short term timescales. Deterministic wind speed forecasts, also named point predictions, do not consider the inherent uncertainties in wind speed predictions. Estimating these uncertainties is essential for providing reliable information to energy operators, enabling them to develop effective operational strategies. In this work, we introduce a probabilistic prediction intervals approach for short-term wind speed forecasting. The proposed framework consists of a hybrid model that integrates machine learning models and an automatic feature selection technique to estimate both point predictions and prediction intervals for wind speed. The simulation works demonstrate the effectiveness of our designed framework and demonstrate its ability to generate satisfactory prediction intervals in the most adopted evaluation criteria.

articleTitle: Assessment of Reliability Indicators of In-Plant Power Supply Systems with Two-Transformer Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The proposed article is devoted to the evaluation of reliability indicators of in-plant power supply systems with dual-transformer substations 10/0.4 kV. The paper considers the reliability of the system for the following variants of power supply schemes: without redundancy; with redundancy when installing a sectional circuit breaker; with double redundancy: when installing a sectional circuit breaker and a redundant jumper at 0.4 kV.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Load Scheduling Optimization of Cost, Renewable Energy Utilization, and Load Balance Using a Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of a Genetic Algorithm (GA) for optimizing load scheduling in residential energy systems. The primary objectives were minimizing operational costs, maximizing renewable energy utilization, and load balancing across various household appliances. The GA-based approach effectively addressed these objectives by dynamically scheduling appliance loads, taking into account factors such as electricity prices, solar generation, and battery storage constraints. The results demonstrate a significant reduction in total energy costs by approximately 36.9% compared to manual scheduling methods, alongside an increase in the utilization of photovoltaic (PV) energy by 5.1 % and battery storage system (BSS) energy by 65.9%. These findings highlight the potential of optimization algorithms to enhance the efficiency and sustainability of home energy management systems. The study also underscores the critical role of parameter tuning in achieving the desired optimization outcomes, providing valuable insights for future research and practical implementations in residential energy management.

articleTitle: A Single-Switch DC-DC Converter with a High Voltage Gain Capability and Reduced Voltage Stress of the Switch for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The growing trend toward high-efficiency, high-gain converters that minimize component count, has spurred the development of many new step-up topologies. In this context introduces a new single-switch, non-isolated DC-DC step-up converter topology specifically designed for renewable energy applications. Key advantages of this topology include a high boost factor, continuous input current, reduced voltage stress on the switch, and a suitable number of elements relative to the achieved boost factor. These features address many of the critical design objectives. The steady-state analysis of the proposed converter is presented and discussed. Simulation and experimental results are presented to verify the theory and performance of the converter.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Impact of Uncertainty on Reactive Power Reduction Through Fixed Power Factor Adjustment of PV Systems in Medium-Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Concerns have been raised about the impact of excessive inflows of lagging reactive power on voltage stability, leading to evaluations focusing on reducing reactive power output from photovoltaic (PV) inverters connected to distribution networks. This study assessed the impact of uncertain factors on reducing lagging reactive power. The results indicate that reactive power reduction increases with higher levels of PV capacity. Furthermore, it was confirmed that the value of power factor adjustment has a more significant impact on reactive power reduction than the PV grid-connected section.

articleTitle: High Frequency Half-Bridge Resonant Converter with Synchronous Rectification for High Input Voltage Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: With the rapid development of gallium nitride (GaN) power devices, they have been widely utilized for high-frequency applications to enhance the system efficiency and power density. However, the voltage blocking capability of GaN power devices is limited, constraining the applications of GaN power devices for high input voltage applications. An input series/output parallel (ISOP) half-bridge (HB) resonant converter is adopted in this research. The voltage stress on primary-side power switches is reduced and the conduction losses caused by the secondary-side rectifiers are also reduced due to parallel operation. Furthermore, HB resonant converter has the characteristic of soft switching in decreasing the switching losses in power components. GaN power devices are employed. Also, ANSYS is used for design of the planar transformers in high-frequency applications. Then, the control driving signals for secondary-side synchronous rectifiers (SRs) are generated by sensing resonant current to increase the efficiency of the converter. Finally, an ISOP HB resonant converter is built with input voltage of 740-840 V, output voltage of 200 V, series-resonant frequency of 1 MHz, and output power of 2.7 kW. The experimental results show that the highest efficiency of the ISOP HB resonant converter is 98.2% at output power of 1.35 kW, while the efficiency of full load at 2.7 kW is 95.9%.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of Distributed Thermostatically Controlled Load for Frequency Regulation and Impact on Voltage Profile of a Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) offer significant potential for frequency regulation in power systems, particularly as the integration of renewable energy sources introduces greater variability. This paper presents a novel approach to TCL control, treating them as distributed units rather than aggregated units, to avoid coordination challenges that could lead to grid instability. A robust control algorithm was developed and tested using a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation environment to evaluate its effectiveness in frequency regulation and its impact on voltage profiles. The results demonstrate that coordinated TCLs significantly enhance frequency stability and that using TCLs for frequency regulation can impact node voltages. It is important to explore the full potential of TCLs to utilize them not only for frequency regulation but also for voltage management.

articleTitle: A Sliding Mode Controller for the Detection of Voltage Problems in Dynamic Voltage Restorers
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Voltage sags are important voltage problem in electrical power systems. Dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) is the method to regulate for these voltage problems. DVR is a device connected in series to system, and it plays an important role to detect the voltage sags. In the literature, there are different methods to detect voltage sags for DVR structures in electrical grids. In this study, the sliding mode control (SMC) structure is developed, and the response of the DVR is measured using the different voltage scenario. A controller design was created using the voltage amplitude and phase information obtained with the improved sliding mode control. This controller compensates for balanced/unbalanced voltage drops occurring in the electrical system via DVR. Simulation results of the developed SMC-based controller are presented using the MATLAB/Simulink program. The proposed detection method provides fast and successful results for solving voltage problems.

articleTitle: Solid-State Transformers Connected to 6.6-kV Distribution System in Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents research on Solid-State Transformers (SSTs) conducted under a MEXT project in Japan. The proposed SST interfaces 6.6 kV medium-voltage grids with 200 V low-voltage networks, using SiC and GaN devices in a modular multilevel converter topology. The paper introduces the development of a high-efficiency low-voltage inverter utilizing GaN devices. Additionally, this paper presents a methodology for determining optimal battery capacity based on demand fluctuations and renewable energy output analysis. This research contributes to advancing SST design and implementation in smart grid applications, providing insights for next-generation power distribution systems.

articleTitle: Isolated Quasi-Switched Boost Integrated T-Type DC-DC Converter for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Over the last few years, there has been a high demand for new or improved isolated DC-DC to fulfill requirements of applications related with RES. In this context, this paper introduces a new isolated DC-DC converter, for use in renewable energy applications. The topology proposed contains an Active quasi-switched Boost Three-Level T-type DC-DC converter with continuous input current at the converter input side, connected to a high-frequency step-up isolation transformer, and a voltage doubler rectifier (VDR) on the output side. The steady-state analysis of the proposed converter is presented and discussed. Simulation results are presented to verify the theory and performance of the converter.

articleTitle: Continuous Operation of GFM Inverter with Carrier Frequency Reduction and One-Pulse Modulation Under Overcurrent Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) inverters, which provide inertia to the grid, are attracting attention as a solution to the problem of insufficient inertia caused by mass deployment of renewable energy using inverters. However, GFM inverters are prone to output overcurrent when power disturbances occur in the grid, and the solid-state switching devices cannot withstand the heat generated by the overcurrent. As a result, the GFM inverter either stops operation or limits the output current, which does not provide sufficient inertia. The objective of this study is to continue operation even under overcurrent conditions by suppressing heat generation due to solid-state switching device losses, and to supply sufficient inertia to the power grid. Two loss reduction methods are proposed to enable GFM inverters to continue operation under overcurrent for short periods duration: the first is carrier frequency reduction, which reduces the carrier frequency of PWM during overcurrent, and the other is one-pulse modulation, which outputs only one pulse per half cycle of the fundamental wave. The effectiveness of the proposed method was demonstrated through experiments.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Derivative-Feedback Control of Grid-Connected Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a single-phase grid-connected inverter controlled by a pseudo-derivative-feedback (PDF) controller. The main circuit is based on a full-bridge inverter, focusing on the stability analysis and comparison of the transient responses of the PDF and proportional-resonant (PR) controllers. The control analysis examines the behavior of both controllers, discusses their performance, and validates their operation through simulations and experimental testing under two different conditions. Finally, the paper compares the controllers based on grid-connected simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: A Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Approach to Implement Renewable Energy System into Sport Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Given contemporary and impending challenges concerning resource depletion and climate change, the adoption of renewable energy systems is pivotal for mitigating ecological impacts. However, the decision-making process regarding their viable implementation remains subjective. This study suggests a multi-criteria decision-making framework utilizing the Multi- Attribute Utility Theory (MAUT), augmented by Monte Carlo simulation to provide a more objective weighting. This methodology is applied to assess seven distinct renewable energy systems as potential alternatives for integration into a wakeboard cable facility. The preferred outcomes are then utilized to conduct a feasibility assessment at a wakeboard cable facility in Germany, with sensitivity testing performed on the results. The findings reveal a preference for photovoltaic systems, emphasizing both ecological and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Forward Active Clamp High Step-Down Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This conference paper describes the development of an active clamp high-frequency, high step-down isolated DC-DC converter, which is mainly applied in data centers, microprocessors, and computer power systems. The proposed converter uses a planar transformer and two active clamp circuit to achieve high switching frequency. The high-voltage side of this circuit achieves high step-down ratio through a series connected clamp capacitor and transformer. Additionally, the parallel switches are connected to the clamp capacitor and transformer to achieve zero-voltage switching (ZVS) which allows the transformer to operate in the first and third quadrants. The low-voltage side adopts a current-doubler rectifier circuit to achieve low output current ripple. The converter can achieve soft switching, which reduces switching losses and more suitable for high frequency to reduce the volume of magnetic components and achieve higher power density. This paper is 54 W, with a switching frequency of 500 kHz, a DC input voltage 48 V, an output voltage 1.8 V and an output current of 30 A. The highest measured efficiency can reach 91.8%. The transient response time is around 200 µs when load transition from half load to full load.

articleTitle: MPC-based Optimal Operation of Smart City Considering Multi Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Cities are transitioning to smart cities to achieve a decarbonized society. Energy management that integrates renewable energy (RES) and combined cooling heat and power (CCHP) is being studied with the goal of improving energy use and eliminating carbon emissions. To deal with uncertainty in RES, model predictive control (MPC), which iteratively predicts and optimises to solve the problem, has attracted attention. In addition, cooling and heating tanks are also important components in reducing the required capacity of batteries and improving the flexibility of cooling and heating. This study proposes an optimal MPC-based operation in a smart city with cooling/heating storage and verifies its effectiveness by comparing costs and carbon emissions through simulation.

articleTitle: Assessment of Large-Scale Solar Photovoltaic Potential on Building Roofs and Facades Using Geo-Aware Graph Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Assessing building photovoltaic (PV) potential is crucial for urban energy planning and achieving net-zero energy building goals. However, it still faces numerous limitations and challenges at the urban scale. Traditional solar irradiation simulation methods are computationally inefficient and difficult to apply to large-scale, high-resolution urban building analysis. Machine learning methods for predicting solar irradiation often inadequately consider the interrelationships among buildings. Moreover, most studies have overlooked the significance of building facades in PV power generation potential, with only a few small-scale studies simultaneously considering both rooftop and facade PV potential. This study proposes a novel geo-aware graph attention network (GA-GAT) model to accurately and efficiently predict solar irradiation on large-scale urban buildings. The model thoroughly considers the complex interactions among neighboring buildings and assesses the potential for buildings to achieve net-zero energy and net-zero electricity based on the predictions. The study focuses on approximately 45000 buildings in Manhattan, New York City, analyzing solar irradiation on rooftops and facades with a spatial resolution of 1 meter. Through this city-wide, high-resolution solar irradiation model, the study further explores the potential for Manhattan to achieve net-zero energy (NZEB) and net-zero electricity buildings (NZEB-e). The results show that achieving NZEB remains challenging. However, if both roof and facade are considered, NEZB-e has the potential to be achieved in many buildings. This research provides a scientific basis and decision support for urban PV planning and NZEB policy formulation.

articleTitle: Leveraging Synthetic Data to Empower AI Models to Predict Photovoltaic Energy Production to Aid in the Decarbonization of Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This research explores the use of synthetic data to enhance the accuracy of machine learning models predicting the energy production of photovoltaic (PV) systems integrated into buildings. We address the challenge of data scarcity in real-world scenarios by generating a large and diverse dataset using BIMSolar, encompassing a wide range of building types, PV panel models, and installation locations. The synthetic data approach allows us to directly estimate energy production for new scenarios without requiring historical data, enabling a shift from forecasting to prediction. We evaluate the performance of various machine learning models, including Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost, using metrics such as MSE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, MAE, and MAPE. Notably, XGBoost and Decision Tree models emerge as top performers, demonstrating high accuracy and efficiency while consuming minimal energy during training. This research presents a promising approach to support building decarbonization efforts by providing reliable estimates of PV energy production, ultimately facilitating a transition towards a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Comparison of Rapid Charging Performance for Lithium-Ion Batteries with Various Positive Electrode Active Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) that use various positive electrode active materials developed with the aim of improving performance and reducing costs are now in practical use. Hence, in order to support the selection of optimal batteries for various applications such as in-vehicle and grid-connected batteries, it is necessary to academically compare the battery performance of various LIBs and use the knowledge gained to consider their suitability for each application. In addition, there has been an increase in the number of cases where rapid charging performance is required for LIBs, mainly in vehicle applications. However, although various basic characteristics that are important in practical applications have been analyzed and compared in previous studies, there have been no studies that have compared the effect on the ultra-rapid charging performance of the positive electrode. In this study, LIBs with only the positive electrode changed to LiCoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, LiNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and LiFePO4 (all with specific capacities of 2.2 mAh/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) were assembled, and the rapid charging characteristics up to the 10C level and electrochemical impedance characteristics of these cells were systematically compared. On the basis of these results, we analyzed the differences in the performance of the positive electrodes during rapid charging electrochemically.

articleTitle: Prediction from 3D Pictogram Drawing Using AR Technology for Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Digital Twin technology, which involves creating a virtual replica using data collected from the real world, including 3D CAD and CG modeling, is an essential tool for energy conservation. The 3D direct drawing system using AR technology can create many shape models for pictograms. However, the model-creating command is difficult for a user because it is multiple and complicated. In this paper, the pictogram drawing trajectory data are investigated and accumulated. After that, their shapes are predicted for automatically converted to the desired shape using the Neural Network method, k-nearest Neighbor method, and Support Vector Machine method of machine learning, and the accuracy rates of the two methods are compared.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Speed Control Systems for Variable Speed Wind Power Generation Systems Using SRG and Capacitor-Less AC-AC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper extends previous work on simulation models of switched reluctance generators (SRG) by demonstrating that selecting appropriate proportional-integral (PI) gain settings enables rapid adaptation to wind speed variations, thereby ensuring system stability. The study shows that employing continuously varying gains provides a detailed understanding of the system's dynamic performance, offering insights into the effects of different gain profiles on stability. The transient responses induced by changes in PI gain are effectively mitigated through the introduction of a compensatory signal derived from the system's maximum transient response. Alternatively, it has been demonstrated that a gain with a smooth transition profile, such as one based on a Bessel curve, achieves a comparable stabilizing effect by eliminating transient phenomena and improving response smoothness. These measures collectively enhance the system's stability and robustness, making the control framework more adaptable to dynamic conditions and offering practical insights for the design of wind power generation systems. The findings highlight the potential of these methods to optimize energy conversion and improve the operational reliability of SRG-based systems under varying wind speeds.

articleTitle: Time and Day-Based Peak Electricity Demand Forecasting: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Peak Cut and Decarbonization
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study aims to address peak power cuts and shifts in Japan by forecasting peak electricity demand using machine learning models. The focus is on a method that excludes meteorological data and utilizes only time-based features. This approach enables medium-term forecasts one month ahead, making it feasible for operational planning without reliance on weather forecasts. It also reduces computational requirements, avoiding the need for high-spec central processing units or graphical processing units. We evaluate and compare several models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, K-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Tree, and LightGBM, to determine their accuracy in providing reliable forecasts. The LightGBM model, in particular, demonstrated remarkable results, achieving forecasting accuracies of 60 in June 2024 and 74 in July 2024. This indicates that it is a highly accurate and computationally efficient model, significantly enhancing peak demand forecasting precision. This approach facilitates peak cut and peak shift strategies, which help avoid electricity shortages and achieve stable demand and supply. Furthermore, it contributes to decarbonization by eliminating unnecessary waste.

articleTitle: Minimal Short Circuit Ratio for Inverter-Based Resources Considering Transmission Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The paper examines the power transmission characteristics including transmission loss for a single-inverter infinite bus system focusing on minimal short-circuit-ratio (SCR). Deriving the equations among power, voltage, and transmission loss, it analyzes the power-voltage characteristics - i.e., p-v and s-v curves - as well as power-loss characteristics of the system. The SCRs corresponding to the noses of the power-voltage characteristics are evaluated as a minimal SCR from the viewpoints of voltage stability. SCRs that achieve several loss factors levels are then examined from the viewpoints of transmission efficiency. The results show that, while the minimal SCR for voltage stability can be evaluated as 1 to 2, which corresponds to the noses, plus margin, larger SCR is required to keep the transmission loss to 5% to 10% for a distribution line.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Optimization of Vapor Injection Refrigeration Cycle
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Refrigerant vapor-injection technique has been proved to improve the performance of refrigeration systems, which can mitigate the problem of exhaust overheating and supplement refrigerant flow for compressor at low evaporation temperature. To analyze the refrigeration performance, the evaporation and condensation temperature, heat exchange temperature difference, injecting pressure and evaporator superheat are comprehensively analyzed. The applicability for different refrigerants is extensively evaluated. Compared with the conventional system, the vapor-injection cycle demonstrates better performance especially under severe conditions.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Scheme Based on the Stockwell Transform for a Multilevel Converter of a Switched Reluctance Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault diagnosis scheme employing the Stockwell transform (ST) for a multilevel converter in a switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive. The goal of this research is to enhance the reliability and performance of SRM drives by accurately detecting and diagnosing faults within the multilevel converter. The Stockwell transform is utilized to decompose the current signals of the SRM into time-frequency representations, providing comprehensive insights into the signal characteristics under both normal and faulty conditions. By analyzing these representations, specific fault signatures are identified, facilitating precise fault detection and localization. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated through several simulations tests conducted under various fault scenarios (focusing on the most likely or most critical faults), including open-circuit and short-circuit faults. The results indicate that the ST-based approach achieves high accuracy and robustness in fault diagnosis, thereby significantly improving the fault-tolerant capability of SRM drives. Moreover, this method can be a valuable tool for predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring in industrial applications, contributing to the improvement of reliable and efficient SRM drive systems.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Approaches for Short-Term Solar Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Forecasting renewable energy generation is essential for effectively managing the electricity grid and energy supply using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models. An important aspect of enhancing the performance of forecasting models is feature selection, which involves identifying and choosing the most relevant features from the dataset. Numerous techniques for feature selection have been applied in solar photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. This research investigates the efficacy of various feature selection approaches, including the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), Euclidean distance (ED), principal component analysis (PCA), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), in improving the accuracy of short-term solar PV forecasting. This short-term forecasting allows for rapid energy generation and consumption adjustments, ensuring a more stable and efficient electricity grid. The long short-term memory (LSTM) model utilizes the selected features from each method to forecast solar PV power output 30 minutes in advance. This specific 30-minute timeframe was selected based on its critical relevance to grid operations and real-time energy market decision-making. Among all feature selection methods, PCC has been proven to be the most effective. The PCC-LSTM model demonstrated superior performance, achieving the lowest root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0745 and 0.0309, respectively, along with the highest coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R^{2})$</tex> of 0.8889.

articleTitle: New Power Sharing Algorithm for Bi-directional Converter in AC/DC Hybrid Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Due to the increase in the DC energy produced by inverter-based sources and the increase in DC loads, the idea of a DC-grid is on the rise. As the existing loads are primarily AC loads, and the grid-codes for a DC distribution grid are not formed, it is practical to explore the concept of a AC/DC hybrid microgrid, with a bi-directional converter connecting the AC and DC grids. In this research we explore a new control strategy for the interlinking bi-directional converter is explored. The bi-directional converter through its control algorithm will carry out power sharing between the AC and DC grids seamlessly. An external disturbance such as a change of load on either the AC or the DC side will lead to an automatic power sharing between the power grids based on pre-defined control parameters.

articleTitle: LVDC Sourced Ultra-Low-Profile LED Drivers Using GaN Power Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In general residential and non-residential spaces, such as houses, offices and shops, lighting equipment is powered from AC power. This requires an isolated AC-DC power converter in each lighting set, which not only limits the shape and design of the equipment, but also causes non-negligible power loss. In this study, the authors investigated the distribution of 24 V low-voltage DC power to residential and non-residential spaces, which has been gaining popularity in recent years due to its compatibility with renewable energy. The authors proposed and developed an ultra-thin card-shaped driver circuit for LED lighting. Experimental results verified that the developed 2 mm thin LED driver achieves high power conversion efficiency even in very high frequency soft switching operation up to 2.0 MHz in a practical load range.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Fuzzy Logic and PI Control for Harmonic Suppression in Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Harmonics pose a significant issue in electric power systems due to their adverse effects, making their elimination highly desirable. The use of nonlinear loads and conventional rectifier circuits generates harmonics, which in turn reduces the power factor and overall system efficiency. This paper presents the modeling of a three-phase, three-wire Shunt Active Power Filter and its control mechanisms. A fuzzy logic-based control system has been developed to minimize harmonic levels. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, the results were compared with those of conventional PI control. Simulations were conducted using Matlab/Simulink, and the results demonstrate that the proposed control technique outperforms the conventional method in harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: JR East's Renewable Energy Development Projects in Tohoku area
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As a railway company, East Japan Railway Company (JR East) has been working to develop renewable energy plants not only to achieve net zero emission of C02 by fiscal 2050 [1] but also to increase the value of areas along its railway lines and promote regional development. As part of these efforts, some mega solar power plants and wind power plants have been introduced in Tohoku area. These plants have been planned in conjunction with plans to utilize unused land along railway lines and remodeling projects of stations. In this paper, the authors report on some of these efforts.

articleTitle: Prevention Oscillatory False Triggering of Two Paralleled GaN-HEMTs by Optimization Parasitic Capacitance and Common-Source Inductance
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Recently, GaN-HEMTs are expected to be used in high-power applications due to their characteristics. To deal with high-power in GaN-HEMTs, it is necessary to connect in parallel to reduce the current stress. However, the paralleled GaN-HEMTs often suffer from oscillatory false triggering, which is a key issue for preventing the practical application of GaN-HEMTs in high-power applications. The purpose of this study is to develop a new method to avoid the oscillatory false triggering of parallel connection by optimally designing the parasitic capacitance and common-source inductance. To achieve this purpose, this paper derives and analyzes an equivalent circuit after the turn-off transition of the circuit which have half-bridge structure with two-paralleled GaN - HEMTs. As a result, we derived the guideline to prevent the oscillatory false triggering caused between two paralleled GaN - HEMTs. The validity of this guideline was confirmed by experiments.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Totem-Pole Converter with Four Quadrants Active and Reactive Power Control by Using the Direct-Quadrature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A single-phase totem pole converter with four quadrants of active and reactive power flow control is designed and implemented in this paper. This converter consists of a DC side and an AC side. When energy is supplied from the DC side to the AC side, it operates in a DC-AC grid-tied mode. When energy is supplied from the AC side to the DC side, it functions as a Power Factor Corrector (PFC). In addition, the converter can provide reactive power to the grid to realize the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) function during grid fault scenarios. This converter utilizes Clarke and Park transformations to convert the AC components into DC components. Besides, the proportional-integral (PI) controller is adopted to regulate the active and reactive power as well as to achieve the four quadrants power flow control. The circuit specifications are with 400V dc on the DC side and 110Vac/220Vac on the AC side. The rated apparent power is 500VA. Finally, the developed circuit and control strategies are first verified via the PLECS simulation software. The digital signal processor (DSP) TMS320F28379D made by Texas Instruments is utilized to achieve the hardware circuit validation.

articleTitle: Energy Management of Aquaculture Considering Load Unit Commitment Under Different Contract Power
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) include promoting land-based aqua-cultures to reduce negative impact on marine resources. This paper proposes operating a grid-connected land-based aquaculture facility using photovoltaic and wind generator microgrids to reduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions. Based on load profiles to avoid short switching times, and simulations are conducted to optimize facility capacity and min-imize annual costs. Simulations also explore different grid contract power scenarios, revealing a tradeoff between economic cost and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CO}_{2}$</tex> emissions based on the Pareto front. While smaller BESS capacity and contracted power reduce costs, they increase vulnerability to power outages, highlighting the need for further analysis.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Cost Analysis of Solar Production by Fixed and Tracking Systems: A Prospective Study for AI Using
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study compares fixed and solar tracking photovoltaic (PV) systems in four European countries, using the Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) as key performance measure. This analysis examines the cost-effectiveness and energy efficiency of vertical single axis, inclined single axis, and dual axis tracking systems compared to fixed PV systems. Results demonstrate that vertical or inclined single axis tracking systems achieve an optimal trade-off between enhanced energy production and cost-effectiveness, making them a favorable choice for maximizing returns on solar energy investments. While dual axis trackers offer higher energy yields, their significantly greater capital and operational expenses lead to increased LCOE, thus reducing overall cost-efficiency. The study also highlights the critical need for advanced optimization approaches to further improve energy yields and minimize operational costs in future PV systems. Our next research studies will explore the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven methodologies, particularly Neural Networks, to develop real-time forecasting models. These AI-based models will enhance the performance of the system to foster more adaptive and intelligent solar tracking solutions in response to changing environmental and operational conditions.

articleTitle: A 2LLC2L Filter Design and Optimization for Grid-Connected Solar PV Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents the optimal design parameters for a proposed 2LLC2L filter intended for solar PV inverters. Additionally, it introduces an optimal design for the inductor cores to minimize harmonic currents injected into the grid, reduce the filter's size, and lower its overall cost. Each inductor on both the inverter and grid side is split into two identical inductors, wound on a common core, to achieve these objectives. The paper also provides a comparison between the experimental results of the 2LLC2L filter and a conventional LCL filter. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimal filter design approach.

articleTitle: Diode-Clamped Linear Amplifier using Only n-channel MOSFETs Applied Separated Gate Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a diode-clamped linear amplifier (DCLA) using only n-channel MOSFETs applied by separated gate drive circuits. Conventional DCLA uses the source follower function of MOSFETs and therefore require an n-channel MOSFETs and a complementary p-channel MOSFETs. In addition, high voltage reference signals are required due to unity voltage gain. The proposed DCLA can be composed of only n-channel MOSFETs and directly controls the gate-source voltage of the MOSFETs resulting in low voltage drive signals. In this paper, the proposed circuit was experimentally verified using voltage feedback control, and it was confirmed that the efficiency was improved compared to conventional circuits and that the THD of the output voltage was approximately 2%.

articleTitle: Control Algorithm for IoT-Enabled Dual-Axis Solar Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Solar energy, valued for being abundant, affordable, and clean, is becoming a major focus of research aimed at improving the methods used to harness it. One effective approach is using solar tracking systems, which adjust the orientation of solar panels to maintain optimal alignment with the sun, thereby increasing energy capture. Specifically, dual-axis solar tracking systems can boost energy yield by 30-40% compared to stationary panels because they can continuously adjust to the sun's position. Although traditional solar tracking methods have significantly improved energy yield compared to static panel installations, recent Internet of Things (IoT) technology has ushered in a new era of intelligent solar tracking systems, offering enhanced functionality and efficiency beyond conventional sun-sensing mechanisms. Previous work by the team discussed an IoT-based dual-axis solar tracking system and demonstrated its efficacy, showing that it performs comparably to traditional sensor-based systems. The system employs cost-effective, compact computers like the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W to access real-time internet data for precise Sun tracking. An electric linear actuator system controls the solar panels, ensuring efficient alignment. The IoT -based solar tracking system features a sophisticated control algorithm that optimizes solar power generation. Our previous work discussed the comparison with sensor-based system. This paper delves deeper into the development of the control algorithm used for the IoT-based tracking system.

articleTitle: State-of-Charge Balancing Control Utilizing the Circulating Current for Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) may consist of many lithium-ion batteries (LIB) connected in series and parallel. In this configuration, each state of charge (SOC) of the LIB may be unbalanced during operation, which reduces the effective capacity of the BESS. To prevent the unbalance of SOC in the system, the balancing method should be introduced. In the passive balancing method, the extra energy of batteries is consumed as heat by resistors which are parallel-connected to them. Therefore, the energy loss due to the balancing would be an issue as the scale of the BESS becomes larger. To date, previous studies have not fully investigated energy loss due to the passive balancing in such large-scale BESS. Therefore, we quantitatively evaluated the energy loss using a system which consists of batteries connected in series and parallel and passive balancing circuits. Furthermore, we proposed a novel balancing algorithm to suppress energy loss. The energy loss due to the balancing using the conventional algorithm and the proposed algorithm are compared, and it is found that the energy loss can be reduced by 37.1 % at least with the proposed balancing method compared to the existing method.

articleTitle: A Low-Carbon Charging Operation Planning Approach for Electric Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: We propose a charging operation planning method to reduce carbon emissions from electric bus charging. The proposed method prioritizes charging during periods of low carbon intensity, considering life-cycle carbon dioxide emissions. This is determined by the amount of local photovoltaic (PV) surplus power and the proportion of renewable energy in the entire grid generation. Simulations based on real-city data evaluated the proposed charging method's effectiveness in reducing emissions by prioritizing grid power charging during low-emission periods while utilizing PV surplus power. The proposed method significantly leverages local PV generation and prioritizes charging during low carbon intensity periods, reducing the emission by up to 81% against overnight charging. Especially in adverse weather conditions, the method effectively decarbonized the operation compared with the surplus-use-oriented method lessening about 244.7 kg- CO2 on a representative day.

articleTitle: Position Sensorless Control of Switched Reluctance Generator Using State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study focuses on the position sensorless control method for Switched Reluctance Generators (SRG) using a state observer. SRG is being considered as a cost-effective alternative to permanent magnet synchronous generators, particularly in renewable energy applications such as hydroelectric power generation. Accurate rotor position control is required for SRG, and traditionally, position sensors have been used to achieve this. However, the use of sensors increases costs and reduces durability in outdoor environments. This study proposes a sensorless control method that estimates the rotor position based on electrical signals using a state observer, eliminating the need for physical sensors. A linear state observer model for SRG was constructed, and its performance was verified through simulations under both low-speed and high-speed operating conditions. The simulation results demonstrated that the proposed method could accurately estimate the rotor position with minimal error. This study contributes to cost reduction and improved reliability of SRG in the field of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Mitigation of 180Hz Midpoint Voltage Ripple in Vienna Rectifiers for Water Electrolysis Using a Parallel Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method to mitigate the 180Hz voltage ripple at the DC-Link midpoint of Vienna rectifiers. Conventional solutions involve altering switching states or adding compensating circuits, which increase complexity and cost. In this study, a parallel configuration is introduced, where one module is connected to the a, b, c phases, and the other to the -c, -a, -b phases, effectively canceling the 180Hz ripple. This approach reduces the ripple without additional control strategies or circuits, providing a simpler and more economical solution, as validated through simulation.

articleTitle: A Personalized Federated Learning Scheme for Operational Parameter Determination of PV Smart Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: With the increasing integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems into distribution networks, voltage regulation has become a significant challenge. Smart inverters (SIs) that allow remote switching of reactive/active power control parameters via communication commands provide a flexible solution for voltage regulation in PV-dominated systems. However, this requires the distribution system operator (DSO) to determine appropriate operational parameters for individual inverters to ensure fair and effective operation, avoiding potential loss of PV generation opportunities. This study proposes a personalized federated learning framework to optimize the SI control parameters. The DSO utilizes statistical data on voltage and potential PV generation at each point and shares control sensitivities among the connection points with similar power flow conditions. This approach efficiently derives the tailor-made control parameter for each inverter, improving voltage control, minimizing PV generation opportunity losses, and ensuring fairness among PV owners. Numerical simulations on a high-PV penetration distribution model demonstrate the framework's potential to enhance voltage regulation and PV utilization.

articleTitle: Efficient Green Hydrogen Production from Wind Power: A System Design Perspective Regarding Optimal Operating Pressure for Alkaline Electrolyzers
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The operating pressure in alkaline water electrolyzers plays a critical role for the efficiency and safety of hydrogen production from wind energy. Higher operating pressures offer the advantage of reduced compression costs, but also increase gas-crossover, leading to potentially explosive mixtures of hydrogen and oxygen and thus impacting system safety. This research investigates the optimal selection of operating pressure to maximize the utilization of fluctuating wind power inputs while also maintaining safety constraints. Based on a comprehensive model of an alkaline water electrolysis plant, lower operating limits are determined as a function of system pressure. Based on the established lower limits, a case study using wind power data over one year is conducted to investigate the impact of selecting the right operating pressure on the economic performance. The study demonstrates that for large electrolysis systems powered by wind energy, the optimal operating pressure is lower than the values typically used in comparable studies from the literature. The results show that operating at intermediate pressures can be beneficial for increasing production. The optimal Levelized Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH) for independent electrolyzer groups is achieved when both are operating at 8 bar. For this plant configuration, the LCOH is calculated to be 9.50 €kg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategies for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This review presents an in-depth examination of energy management strategies (EMS) utilized in hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs). The primary goal of EMS in HEVs is to improve fuel efficiency, reduce emissions, and extend battery life by optimizing power distribution between the internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric motor. The review classifies EMS into three categories: rule-based, optimization-based, and data-driven methods. Rule-based methods are relatively simple and computationally efficient but may not always yield optimal performance. On the other hand, optimization-based strategies, which include dynamic programming and genetic algorithms, offer more effective solutions but introduce greater complexity. Data-driven techniques, such as reinforcement learning and neural networks, show promise for adaptive real-time decision-making, thereby improving performance across various driving conditions. This paper highlights the advantages and challenges associated with each method and emphasizes the role of emerging technologies in improving HEV efficiency. By comparing different strategies, this review outlines future research directions for the development of more sophisticated EMS, fostering advancements in HEV technology.

articleTitle: Intelectual Methods for Analysis of Renewables in the Energy Balance for Low Emission Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The growing global focus on mitigating climate change has emphasized the need for efficient strategies that integrate renewable energy sources (RES) while minimizing emissions. This paper explores the application of various intellectual methods-Energy System Models (e.g., TIMES, LEAP), Multi-Objective Optimization, Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) Models, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and Machine Learning (ML)-for analysing energy balances and developing low-emission strategies. These methods offer distinct capabilities in balancing technological, economic, and environmental aspects of energy systems. The paper examines how these approaches facilitate the integration of RES, address operational challenges, and handle uncertainties in energy demand and supply. Case studies demonstrate how AI and ML techniques optimize energy dispatch and demand forecasting, while system models provide long-term planning solutions. A comprehensive comparison of these methods is presented, highlighting their strengths and limitations in transitioning towards sustainable and low-emission energy systems.

articleTitle: Total Harmonic Distortion Reduction in Three-Phase PV Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper aims at examining the total harmonic distortion in PV systems with especial reference to three-phase inverters and the MPPT algorithms adopted. PV inverters generally produce harmonics into grid systems by their internal switching and non-linear changes. To assess the effect of harmonic distortion on the quality and stability of the power and the performance of the utilized system, 1MWp PV system is modeled and implemented through MATLAB/SIMULINK to analyze harmonic reduction. This research work offers solutions that surround the methods of minimizing total harmonic distortion, the incorporation of filtering approaches, proposed MPPT methods, using D-STATCOM and efficient control of inverters systems.

articleTitle: Resilience and Frequency Control in Low-Inertia Power Systems: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: There are growing concerns about the resilience levels of future power systems. The rapid transition to renewable energy sources (RES), is transforming power systems by replacing conventional synchronous generators with inverter-based resources. This shift has led to a significant reduction in system inertia, which traditionally helped stabilize frequency fluctuations following power imbalances. As a result, low-inertia power grids face critical challenges, including faster rates of change of frequency (RoCoF), larger frequency deviations, and a heightened risk of system instability. Another significant concern is climate change as the frequency of the extreme weather events has increased dramatically in the last decade. These events caused significant disruptions to power system and these events are expected to lead to even greater disruptions in the future. This paper addresses the critical challenges associated with optimizing frequency control in low-inertia power grids and addressing climate change challenges. A detailed review of current practices is presented to highlight potential solutions. Additionally, the paper explores the importance of developing standardized resilience metrics and performance optimization strategies to ensure robust and efficient grid operations. Future research directions include the need for improved resilience metrics, dynamic grid stability models, and regulatory frameworks that support a holistic transition to low-inertia power systems with high renewable penetration.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Data Driven Special Protection Scheme Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The insufficient installation of transmission lines due to community approval issues has exacerbated stability problems in the power system. Additionally, faults or outages in transmission lines that transfer power from generation areas to load areas can lead to power mismatches and angle stability issues. To protect against angle stability problems, the Korean power system employs Special Protection Schemes (SPSs) that trip generators in the event of extremely high voltage in transmission lines. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning-based online adaptive SPS by analyzing the Transient Stability Index (TSI). The advantage of this method is its ability to assess appropriate SPS generators depending on intermittent power system conditions, which often renders conventional SPS systems inadequate. The proposed algorithm is applied in a case study involving the Korean electric power system, including high voltage AC transmission lines with High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) systems, and is verified under varying system conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling of a H2 Generation System Pilot Through Wastewater Electrolysis and PV Solar Energy for Water Resource Valorization in O&G Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling of a Hydrogen (H2) Production System that utilizes wastewater from oil fields and photovoltaic solar energy, addressing global decarbonization challenges through non-conventional energy solutions. The study focuses on two main aspects: the reutilization of industrial wastewater from oil and gas fields and the exploration of hydrogen as a viable energy vector. A MATLAB-based model simulates the water electrolysis process using wastewater from high water cut oil reservoirs, typically disposed of or recirculated without further use. This approach incorporates a technical and economic prefeasibility analysis to serve as a sizing tool for similar projects, utilizing residual and industrial waters as valuable resources. Future work will focus on the photovoltaic systems, storage, and H2 transport logistics. The study demonstrates the economic viability of producing H2 from previously untapped resources, highlighting its potential applicability across multiple industries.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Technical Resource for Tidal Stream Energy in South-West Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: To reach the objective of net-zero carbon by 2050, Japan is promoting the development of renewable energies. Among these, tidal current energy provides high predictability and stability, which can help mitigate the negative impact of the high variability of other sources (solar, wind) on the grid management. As an initial step for the design of a tidal current energy national development plan, this paper presents a resource analysis for South - West Japan. Results for current velocity from an ocean numerical model were used to identify tidal energy sites and estimate the theoretical resource for each of them. Applying the same ocean model results to the specifications of nine turbines, energy output was estimated for each site. Results showed an estimated installable capacity of 4,422.5 MW and an annual energy yield of 8,956.06 GWh.
