More than 78% of this resource is allocated in only six areas or sites: the straits between Goto Islands, the entrances to Ariake Sea, Hayasui Strait, Kurushima Strait, Bisan Strait, and Naruto Strait. Though this work provides valuable insights for the theoretical and technical resource in South - West Japan, further research is needed to evaluate the economical viability of tidal energy exploitation in each site.

articleTitle: Mitigating Grid Peaks in E-Mobility Charging A Comparative Evaluation of §14a EnWG and Priority-Driven Load Reduction Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The rapid expansion of zero-emission electric vehicles (EVs) and their charging infrastructure presents significant challenges for low-voltage (LV) networks. To address the risks of grid congestion, § 14a of the German Energy Industry Act (En WG) was developed. This study aims to highlight differences in grid peak mitigation between various approaches and assess their overall impact on LV networks. The paper compares the non-discriminatory EnWG approach with a priority-based approach that considers charging demand and duration for each EV. Using Pandapower and Python, this paper demonstrates the relative limitations of the En Wgapproach compared to the more responsive priority-based method.

articleTitle: A Brief Overview of Future Mobility and Energy Management Strategies with Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Concept on Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a notable increase in interest in electric vehicles (EVs) due to several factors, including the depletion of fossil fuels, environmental concerns such as carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions, and the fact that the vehicle industry is the main driver of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. In line with this growing interest, there are both opportunities and challenges in the integration of EV charging systems into the electricity grid. Grid operators may begin to regard electric vehicles (EVs) as a novel distributed resource, given that the stored energy in their batteries can be employed for a multitude of applications. The concept of vehicle-to-everything (V2X), enables the batteries of electric vehicles (EVs) to participate in energy management as a distributed resource. EVs can support the grid through topologies such as vehicle-to-grid (V2G), vehicle-to-home (V2H), vehicle-to-load (V2L), vehicle-to-building (V2B), and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V). This paper provides a summary of the benefits and challenges associated with the implementation of each V2X approach, as well as proposing potential solutions to address these challenges.

articleTitle: Open Interface System Protocols for Space Based Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Renewable energy systems have been recognized to play an important role in future environmentally friendly energy systems. An important source of renewable energy is solar power derived when solar panels intercept with incident solar radiation. The degradation effect of cloud obstruction has led to the consideration of space-based solar power systems. In space-based solar power systems, satellites with large solar panel payload transmit solar energy to earth-based rectennas. The deployment of multiple space based solar power satellites is necessary to ensure that more energy is derived from space based solar power. However, the realization of such a system requires the design of communication protocols between in-orbiting space-based power satellites. The use of such a system enables multiple receiving antenna ground stations to concurrently receive power from solar power satellites. The presented research aims to present the design of system protocols that enable the realization of this goal, considering heterogeneous solar power satellites and operational conditions. This is carried out while considering communications between in-orbiting space-based solar power satellites, along with satellite rectennas. Furthermore, performance analysis and investigations show that the use of the proposed solution enhances power accessibility and reduces deficit by an average of 18%.

articleTitle: Tensor Network-Based Lightweight Energy Forecasting for Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) operations demand lightweight energy forecasting models due to increasing computational requirements. This paper applies tensor-train (TT) decomposition to a mixture density network (MDN) model, training it from scratch to enhance forecasting accuracy while reducing computational overhead. Our computer experiments demonstrate that the proposed TT-based approach, trained from scratch, outperforms well-known model compression methods such as pruning and singular value decomposition in both parameter reduction and forecasting accuracy. We also explore potential reasons for TT's effectiveness by examining matrix rank properties. This research contributes to the development of efficient and accurate forecasting models crucial for VPP management and renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Configuration Optimization of Dual Active Bridge Converter Systems for Interfacing Large-Scale Water Electrolyzer with Stand-Alone Renewables
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper explores Dual Active Bridge Converter System (DABCS) configurations for interfacing a water electrolyzer in the MW range with a medium voltage direct current bus powered by stand-alone renewable power sources. The number of submodules in the DABCS varies based on the voltage and current ratings of the Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) employed. The results show that configurations with a high submodule count, enabled by low-voltage IGBT modules, exhibit superior semiconductor efficiency. However, this advantage is offset by a decrease in Medium Frequency Transformer (MFT) efficiency with an increasing number of submodules. A Pareto optimization analysis of DABCS efficiency versus power density is employed to reveal the most suitable trade-off.

articleTitle: An Optimal Resilience Dispatch Method Integrating Hybrid Energy Resources for a Steel Factory Campus
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: When a power outage occurs, it may cause significant economic losses for industries. However, previous studies on power system resilience have seldom focused on user-side microgrids. This study proposes composite resilience indices for user-side microgrids to quantify their ability to withstand extreme events. The proposed resilience indices consider load value, minimum power supply, energy shortages, and the degradation characteristics of islanded microgrids. Additionally, this study introduces a two-stage resilience optimization and reconfiguration strategy, including energy-level scheduling and grid-level feeder reconfiguration. A genetic algorithm based multi-objective optimization approach is used for energy scheduling, followed by feeder reconfiguration using particle swarm algorithm integrated with DlgSILENT system modeling to meet the grid codes and maximize demand supply. The proposed methods are validated using a realistic steel corporation as a test system, showing the flexibility and practical feasibility of the system. User-side microgrid resilience can be effectively enhanced by the proposed method considering load priority.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Method for LLC Resonant Convertor of EV Battery Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This research provides a thorough analysis of the LLC resonant converter's mathematical modeling, design, and control using MATLAB Simulink (R2024a). Distinct control strategies, Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Controller (LADRC), Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID), PI and PI-PD controller, have been implemented and rigorously analyzed under varying operational conditions. The investigation encompassed dynamic response, stability, and disturbance rejection capabilities of each controller. The results consistently demonstrated the superiority of the LADRC in comparison to PID family controllers, highlighting enhanced transient response, reduced overshoot, and improved robustness across diverse scenarios. The conclusion drawn from this study supports the efficacy of LADRC in LLC resonant converters, providing valuable insights into the selection of control strategies for optimal performance in practical applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Determination for Voltage Regulators Parameters by Monitoring Power Flow and Three-Phase Unbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposed a framework for dynamically determining the appropriate line drop compensator (LDC) parameters and the monitoring phase for voltage regulators using a machine learning technique and real-time power flow information to improve the hosting capacity of photovoltaic (PV) and electric vehicles (EV) in distribution systems. Although PV and EV installations are eco-friendly, these installations cause the challenges to voltage control due to power flow complications and the deterioration of three-phase unbalanced voltage. In the LDC control, the voltage is controlled by the tap operation of voltage regulators and the performance depends on the LDC parameters and the monitoring phase. To control the voltage within a permissive range, appropriate determination of these operation parameters is indispensable. Particularly, under the complicated power flow due to PV and EV installation, the dynamic determination of these parameters is one of the effective methods. However, the appropriate judgement of power flow conditions for determining the parameters and the prevention of hunting of tap operation are challenges. Therefore, we propose a dynamic determination framework consisted of an appropriate monitoring phase selection method, considering prevention of hunching and LDC parameter determination method based on a mixture of experts using real-time power flow data to these challenges. The effectiveness of the framework was evaluated from the viewpoint of improvement of the hosting capacity using the actual distribution system model in the Hokuriku area in Japan.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Sea Environment on Capacitive Power Transfer Systems: Equivalent Circuit Parameters and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: It is suggested that capacitive power transfer (CPT) technologies can be used to recharge electric maritime vehicles' batteries. This work presents a configuration of the Underwater Unmanned Vehicle (UUV)-CPT system. The modelling of the systems' equivalent electrical circuit is discussed and the theoretical analysis of the External Watery Medium (EWM) on the Equivalent Circuit Parameters (ECPs) is conducted. To observe the effects of the EWM over the system, 3-D Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is performed on both cases with and without EWM. Using the Particle Optimization Algorithm (PSO), the calculations for the new ECPs of circular electric couplers are specified and the implications of EWM are carried out. The accuracy of the proposed parameter specification approach is examined and verified through experimental setup. The system-level impacts of EWM on the performance of the capacitive power transfer system are analyzed.

articleTitle: Secure Identities for Renewable Energy Sources Through Self-Sovereign Identity and Attribute-Based Access Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Traditional electricity networks operate with centralized power generation and unidirectional energy flow. The emergence of private renewable energy sources (RES) and the shift towards decentralized grids necessitate effective smart grid management, which has been extensively studied in the literature. This framework employs an authentication and authorization framework for RES utilized in peer-to-peer energy trading, focusing on cybersecurity. By addressing the CIA triad, the platform is developed with a security-by-design approach using self-sovereign identity (SSI) authentication and attribute-based access control (ABAC) authorization of RES, and evaluated against denial-of-service, false data injection, and man-in-the-middle attacks. Preliminary tests assess the framework's resilience in high-load scenarios, demonstrating its capacity to uphold confidentiality, availability, and integrity.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Water-Energy Nexus on DC Island Microgrid with RESs
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Fresh water and energy are scarce resources on islands, making it crucial to ensure an adequate supply of both for residents. The complex interplay between water and energy demands necessitates innovative and efficient solutions for the water-energy nexus. This paper introduces a novel direct current (DC) island microgrid system incorporating renewable energy sources (RESs), a battery storage system (BS), and a desalination system (DS) to meet the intricate water and energy needs of island inhabitants. Compared to traditional alternating current (AC) microgrids, this DC microgrid offers reduced capital expenditure and higher energy efficiency, making it a more viable option for island applications. The significance of capital expenditure in the decision-making process for building microgrid systems on islands cannot be overstated. Therefore, this study focuses on an optimal planning method designed to minimize capital expenditure while ensuring the water and energy nexus demands are met. This method includes a detailed analysis of the integration of RESs, BS, and DS within the microgrid system, evaluating their collective impact on both economic and operational performance. The results from this study indicate that an optimized island DC microgrid can achieve substantial economic efficiency alongside effective water and energy production. This research contributes to the growing field of microgrid systems, offering practical insights and methodologies for enhancing the sustainability and efficiency of island infrastructures.

articleTitle: Combined 3D FEA and Machine Learning Design of Inductive Polyphase Coils for Wireless EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technologies are currently researched and developed for charging the batteries of electric unmanned air and ground vehicles. This paper presents systems with special polyphase inductive coils, which generate rotating fields and achieve high power density and efficiency. The complex geometry is modeled and studied with 3D electromagnetic finite element analysis (FEA). In order to reduce the substantial computational effort, machine learning techniques are proposed for surrogate modeling. A deep learning algorithm is introduced to capture the physics-based relationships between geometry and electromagnetic properties in inductive coils for wireless charging. Parametric models are systematically gener-ated and analyzed by 3D FEA to create a data base with hundreds of designs, which are then used as training and testing data for the machine learning model. A multi-input univariate output for the mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver for an example two-phase WPT system is established. The outputs of the deep learning model are satisfactorily validated with 3.3 % NRMSE and a R2 value of 0.985.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Battery Energy Extraction from Lead-Acid and Lithium-Polymer Batteries by Pulse Discharging and Source Multiplexing in An Efficient Operating Point
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Batteries have been the focus of current research due to the proliferation of electric vehicles and renewable energy applications. However, the main problem for the widespread use of batteries is their poor energy density. In this study, the pulse discharge of batteries has been identified as a factor affecting maximum energy extraction from batteries. The effects of the duty ratio of pulse delivery and outcomes of the variation of the pulse period have been studied. The optimum pulse period and the most effective duty ratio for lithium-polymer and lead-acid battery chemistries have been validated through experimental results. The best operating point is obtained using data analysis. Generally, in an electrochemical cell or a half cell, the electrodes are covered with positively or negatively charged ion clouds, developing the potential up to standard values in the idle situation. For the continuous electron exchange, higher activation energy is required to overcome internal resistance which is dissipated mainly as heat. In this directed study, pulse discharging of batteries is enabled to extract a portion of energy dissipated as heat by providing a rest period for the battery to re-establish its equilibrium status at an optimum frequency. The most effective duty ratio was observed as 50% for both batteries. Finally, a battery multiplexing strategy is proposed for a continuous power supply.

articleTitle: Optimized Design Search of Tidal Turbine with Low Cut-in Speed for Energy Harvesting Smart Buoys
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Smart buoys have increasingly become important for marine monitoring. Their use in offshore marine monitoring is however limited by the availability of a long-term self-powering, environmentally friendly power source. In this study, the Savonius tidal turbine, which can exploit reliable and predictable tidal energy, is proposed as power source for the smart buoy. Despite its advantages of having a low cut-in speed, low cost and ease of operation, the Savonius turbine has low efficiency. Starting with a Savonius turbine with splitters as the baseline, a multi-objective optimization was performed using Artificial Neural Networks-assisted Genetic Algorithm and Computational Fluid Dynamics, to maximize the turbine's efficiency under a wide operating range, while minimizing the aspect ratio and torque fluctuation. A double stage turbine was further constructed from the optimized blade shape and experimentally tested in a circulating water tank. The results showed that, compared to the baseline shape, the optimized geometry improved the single stage turbine's efficiency by 6.41%, with a 12.9% reduction in the aspect ratio. The negative torque range and the amplitude of the torque fluctuations were reduced by 50% and 20.4%, respectively. On the other hand, the double stage turbine recorded a 10.45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> reduction in efficiency compared to the optimized single stage turbine. However, the negative torque range was eliminated in the double stage turbine, and the amplitude of the torque fluctuation reduced by 83.19%. The reduced torque fluctuations promote smooth turbine rotation, which significantly improves the turbine's startability at low cut-in speed and reduces the fatigue load on the shaft and bearings. The internal flow analysis revealed that the accelerated flow between the main and splitter blades has an opposing effect on the torque produced, thus simultaneous optimization of the main and splitter blades is necessary to improve the overall turbine efficiency.

articleTitle: Fast-Responding and Flexible Energy Storage Systems for Renewable Integration: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper examines the critical role of flexibility and fast response in Energy Storage Systems (ESS) for integrating renewable energy sources into modern power grids. As the global share of renewable energy grows, ESS technologies must evolve to meet the increasing demand for dynamic and reliable energy solutions. This review, titled Fast Responding and Flexible Energy Storage Systems for Renewable Integration: Challenges and Opportunities, highlights recent advancements in ESS control strategies, hybrid systems, and innovative business models that enhance the performance and market adaptability of energy storage. The paper also addresses key challenges related to technology, market structures, and regulatory frameworks, offering insights into potential future developments. The need for fast-responding ESS to ensure grid stability, frequency control, and efficient energy management in the face of fluctuating renewable energy generation is emphasized.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Phase Shift Application in Bidirectional Chopper with Single-Cell Auxiliary Full-Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes the application of phase shift to a bidirectional chopper with an auxiliary converter for the application of onboard battery energy storage system (BESS) in electric railways. The proposed chopper is composed of a bidirectional chopper as the main converter, an auxiliary converter made of single-phase full-bridge cells connected in cascade, and an inductor. The auxiliary converter operates as an active power filter, effectively reducing the inductor switching-ripple current (i.e., its inductance value) and volume, where increasing the number of cells would lead to bigger reductions. However, using multiple cells raises the converter loss and cost, whereas using a single cell limits the switching-ripple current reduction. Thus, phase shift is applied to the carriers of the chopper to produce lower switching-ripple current when a single cell is used. Theoretically, it is able to produce switching-ripple current at 1/4 of the conventional bidirectional chopper under the same frequency. Experimental results conducted with a 2 kW down-scaled model further validate the theoretical analysis results, and confirm the steady-state performance of the proposed chopper.

articleTitle: Fleet Characteristics Analysis for the Generation of a Generic Commercial Fleet Model
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: With the increasing number of electric vehicles (EVs) the charging demand grows accordingly. Especially fleets stress the power system due to fast electrification, high-power, and simultaneous charging. Charging management can help improve the system, but typically require currently not-available fleet data for setup and training. This paper analyzes the theoretical fleet behavior regarding arrival, departure, state of charge, and charging strategy, and explores and explains their statistical parameters. The analysis is based on a real-world dataset, which contains around 84,200 charging sessions. The resulting data and equations can be used to create a generic model for the realistic generation of commercial EV fleet profiles.

articleTitle: Design and Lag Compansated Control of a GaN Based Phase Shifted Full Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and modeling of a Phase Shifted Full Bridge (PSFB) converter utilizing Gallium Nitride (GaN) MOSFETs, with a focus on control strategy development to optimize converter performance. The converter is designed to operate within an input voltage range of 200-400V, with a switching frequency of 500kHz, delivering an output power of 500W at 28V. The high switching frequency enabled by GaN MOSFETs allows for significant reductions in size and weight of the converter, while maintaining high efficiency. This study delves into the detailed modeling of the PSFB topology, emphasizing the challenges and solutions in implementing an effective control strategy. Simulation results demonstrate the converter's ability to maintain stable and efficient operation across the specified input voltage range and varying load conditions, providing valuable insights into the design of high-frequency, high-power density converters.

articleTitle: A Hydrogen-Driven Technology Mapping for Future Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This research paper explores hydrogen-driven sustainable technologies for future energy hubs, addressing the urgent need for cleaner energy solutions amidst growing environmental concerns and the decline of fossil fuel resources. The primary objectives are to map technologies related to hydrogen energy, analyze their macro-environmental impacts, and examine the interactions within the hydrogen sector to identify gaps and develop viable business models. Utilizing a hybrid research design, the study employs qualitative analyses including PESTEL and SWOT, complemented by interrelationship and gap analyses. Methods such as comparative analysis and business modelling are also integral to understanding the economic viability and strategic integration of hydrogen technologies within global energy frameworks. The findings reveal that hydrogen stands as a flexible and sustainable energy source, capable of significantly influencing future energy paradigms. The research highlights the potential for collaborative innovation across various sectors, advocating for strategic stakeholder engagement to harness full capabilities of hydrogen. It concludes that substantial opportunities exist for enhancing energy security and environmental sustainability through hydrogen technology, with future research needed to further explore economic models and refine deployment strategies within energy hubs.

articleTitle: Strategic Green Marketing for Smart Grids: Boosting Consumer Adoption of Sustainable Energy Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of green marketing strategies in promoting smart grids, highlighting sustainable branding, consumer education, and strategic alliances. The aim is to evaluate how different marketing strategies may improve customer knowledge and trust, facilitating the transition to sustainable energy technologies. The qualitative study approach has identified critical findings demonstrating that authenticity, engagement, and transparency in green marketing campaigns substantially improve consumer acceptance of smart grids. Targeted green marketing methods efficiently mitigate technical, financial, and behavioral hurdles to adoption by emphasizing environmental and economic advantages and enhancing consumer engagement and trust. This study advances sustainable marketing by offering tangible strategies for marketers and energy sector professionals, highlighting the importance of strategic partnerships with influencers and sustainability organizations. It also suggests future research directions, including empirical assessments of green marketing's impact on smart grid adoption and exploring emerging technologies to improve these strategies. This research underscores the critical role of green marketing in facilitating a cultural shift towards environmental sustainability. Marketers, policymakers, and energy professionals are urged to utilize these insights to promote the implementation of smart grids and foster a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: An European-Based Erasmus Mundus Pathway for the Higher Education in the Hydrogen Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Hydrogen has the potential to play a significant role in reducing emissions in the coming decades, serving as a key component in the array of solutions to mitigate climate change. Specifically, green hydrogen emerges as a critical element for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors, such as specific transport and industrial segments, while facilitating the integration of large volumes of variable renewable energy sources and enhancing flexibility in the power sector. The European Union has been actively promoting a clean hydrogen economy by 2030 as part of its strategy to achieve the 2050 decarbonization targets. Developing appropriate training programs is essential for the sector's growth, ensuring that the necessary skills for the hydrogen industry are adequately addressed-a priority concern for companies operating in this field.

articleTitle: Renewable Power Generation Maximization for UAVs with Adaptive Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The demand for efficient and Fuel consumption alternative renewable energy sources in the aviation sector has led to the exploration of advanced technologies such as Ram Air Turbines (RATs). RATs are critical in applications requiring power generation in emergency scenarios that may happen to un-manned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, the primary challenge lies in optimizing the performance of the RATs, such as power output and operational stability, under varying and unpredictable wind conditions. Traditional control methods often fail to adapt to these dynamic environments. This paper underscores the necessity of utilizing a recurrent neural network (RNN) to detect uncertain wind turbine dynamics; a sliding mode control rule is created in the suggested controller to monitor the optimal turbine rotation speed. Next, an online update technique is developed to provide real-time weight updates for the RNN, enabling control over maximum power extraction. According to simulation results, the suggested controller outperforms a traditional control approach in tracking the optimal turbine rotation speed and extracting the most wind power from RATs by 13 times, even in severe nonlinearities and system uncertainties.

articleTitle: A Simplified Fuzzy Sliding Mode Controller for PV Emulation
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper proposes a Piecewise-linear Fuzzy Sliding Mode Control (PWL-FSMC) based Photovoltaic (PV) Emulator for accurately replicating the characteristics of an actual solar panel. The emulator utilizes a non-ideal, switching buck converter topology in voltage control mode. A closed-loop control system regulates the output current and voltage of the buck converter to match the actual PV output, ensuring emulation accuracy. The integration of sliding mode control (SMC) with fuzzy controller (FC) improves the robustness and adaptability of the system. Thereby, effectively mitigating uncertainties, disturbances, and nonlinearities inherent in PV systems. Furthermore, piecewise linear implementation offers simplicity, computational efficiency, and low-cost microcontroller compatibility. It enhances the tracking accuracy, transient response, and reduces the chattering phenomenon associated with SMC. The performance of the proposed PV emulator is validated through simulation in the MATLAB Simulink environment. Comparative analysis against PI, SMC and Conventional Fuzzy sliding mode control (CFSMC) demonstrates the accuracy, speed, and adaptability of the proposed approach, particularly under partial shading conditions (PSC). The proposed PWL-FSMC eliminates the need for extensive inference, fuzzification and defuzzification mechanisms associated with conventional FC. Consequently, not only an enhanced tracking performance in terms of speed and accuracy is achieved but it also simplifies the implementation, making it particularly suitable to be implemented using a low-cost microcontroller in lab environments where space and resources are limited.

articleTitle: Wind-to-Hydrogen and Battery-Based Microgrid Systems for Residential Building Applications: A Feasibility Study in Canada
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: As climate change issues escalate globally, there is a growing shift towards renewable energy solutions. This study explores the viability of a wind-to-hydrogen microgrid (MG) system and compares it with a battery-based system for supplying electricity to a grid-connected residential house in Canada. Utilizing the HOMER platform, simulation models were developed to assess two configurations: wind turbine (WT)-hydrogen system and WT-battery. These models were optimized for renewable energy fractions (RFs) ranging from 0% to 80% and included components such as WTs, fuel cells (FCs), electrolysers, hydrogen storage tanks, and batteries. The results indicate that both wind-to-hydrogen and wind-battery systems are feasible for grid-connected residential use. While increasing the RF led to higher net present costs (NPC), the cost of electricity (COE) often decreased due to the ability to sell surplus energy back to the grid. Specifically, the WT-hydrogen system achieved a COE of 0.09 CA$/kWh, and an RF of 81.4%, compared to the battery-based system with the same COE, and an RF of 80.3%. Both systems reduced carbon dioxide emissions, with net energy purchases being negative for most months, indicating more energy was sold than bought. The WT-hydrogen system was only about 6.5% more expensive than the battery system, but its costs are expected to decrease, potentially making it more advantageous due to its carbon-free emissions and higher energy density. Policy support may be needed to encourage widespread adoption.

articleTitle: Status and Challenges of Energy Efficiency & Conservation Using DC Power Technologies in Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Electrification is growing around the world because it is clean, safe, and efficient in terms of energy use and expected to play a key role in the energy systems and infrastructure of the future. For electrification, DC technology is an indispensable fundamental technology not only for conventional power systems (generation, transmission & distribution, and consumption), but also for transportation systems, which used to be based on fossil fuels, and for industrial, commercial, and residential heat applications. This paper introduces some Japanese initiatives, including NEDO's (an agency of the Japanese government) activities, about the status of DC utilization in ideal power systems and future efforts, based on Japan's historical background and its achievements.

articleTitle: Advancements in Time-Domain-Based Protection and Dynamic State Estimation for Power Systems with Inverter-Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper aims to construct a state-of-the-art review of the state estimation tool in the area of protection and control systems, examining the latest applications and discussing the pending challenges of this technique. Publications covering state estimation for power systems are categorized in terms of application, algorithm type, and component to monitor. This work demonstrates that most applications of state estimators in protection and control systems rely on unrealistic synthetic data and conventional estimation algorithms. The main barriers to implementing state estimation in the protection and control area are related to the lack of novel techniques, high computational complexity, and the unavailability of mathematical and physical models reflecting the real behavior of each system component. This paper extensively compiles various publications and, based on the identification of challenges and implementation opportunities, proposes a proof-of-concept case study that leads to the development of an experimental state estimator environment with real-time simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Analysis of Synchronous Reference Frame Based Enhanced Power Quality Management with Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Harmonic distortion is a significant challenge in power systems that degrades energy quality and shortens the lifespan of equipment. Therefore, effectively managing and minimizing these distortions is crucial for the reliability and efficiency of modern power grids. This paper has been presented a shunt active power filter (SAPF) designed for a three-phase power system to address issues such as harmonic distortion and reactive power caused by nonlinear loads. A design incorporating synchronous reference frame (SRF) theory and hysteresis control methods to provide effective compensation and to supply pure and balanced current to the grid have been proposed in this study. Furthermore, a metaheuristic-based PI control has been used to regulate the DC bus voltage, which contributes to reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) and improving energy efficiency. A comparison of different metaheuristic algorithms, such as particle swarm optimization and gray wolf algorithm, have been conducted to assess their efficacy in stabilization of DC bus voltage of SAPF. The results demonstrated that the proposed system effectively addresses the challenges posed by nonlinear loads, with particle swarm optimization exhibiting the most favourable performance for voltage regulation. This work contributes to the advancement of power quality, system stability, and the demonstration of the benefits of metaheuristic-based PI control in an active power filter.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Control Scheme for the Hybrid Cascaded Converter based STATCOM with Greatly Reduced Switching Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study presents the static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) utilizing a hybrid cascaded converter, which requires fewer power semiconductor devices compared with the conventional cascaded H-bridge converter. To enhance efficiency, a hybrid modulation scheme is implemented, effectively minimizing switching losses without compromising output performance. Additionally, a tailored capacitor voltage balancing control strategy is introduced. Laboratory experiments validate the practicality of the proposed STATCOM and demonstrate the effectiveness of the control scheme. Moreover, a comparative analysis with the traditional way highlights significant improvements in output quality and loss reduction. The experimental findings further reveal the robustness of the proposed STATCOM under dynamic operating conditions, including transitions between capacitive and inductive modes. The system maintains stable DC capacitor voltages and achieves excellent harmonic performance, with a total harmonic distortion (THD) below 3% across all test scenarios. These results underscore the potential of the proposed STATCOM to address challenges in grid-connected applications, particularly in systems requiring high efficiency and reliability. The proposed control scheme provides a promising foundation for future advancements in power electronics for grid stabilization and power quality improvement.

articleTitle: Digital Marketing Strategies for Smart Grids: Utilizing Online Platforms to Drive Awareness and Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study investigates the multifaceted role of digital marketing strategies in driving the awareness, acceptance, and adoption of Smart Grid (SG) technologies. The research uses a qualitative exploratory approach to analyze how various online platforms-including social media, multimedia content, email marketing, and paid advertising-can effectively engage diverse audience segments, such as consumers, businesses, utility companies, and policymakers. The findings underscore the importance of personalized, data-driven approaches in enhancing public understanding of SG technologies while emphasizing community engagement and trust-building among stakeholders. The study highlights how sophisticated digital marketing tactics-ranging from engaging videos, podcasts, and infographics to targeted paid advertising-simplify complex SG concepts and increase SG solutions' visibility and perceived value. Emerging trends, such as influencer marketing and advanced analytics, are critical drivers of future digital marketing efforts in the energy sector. This research provides practical insights for energy companies, policymakers, and marketers, underscoring the potential of digital marketing as a catalyst for accelerating SG adoption, contributing to improved energy efficiency, and fostering a more sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Automating Substation Modeling Using Labeled Images
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive workflow for automating substation modeling using labeled aerial images. Our approach streamlines the process into three key steps: generating the input dataset as labeled images, inferring an electrical substation model based on standard design principles and exemplarily importing the model into DIgSILENT PowerFactory as a simulation environment. We demonstrate that this new automated process significantly enhances speed, improves consistency, and facilitates easier updation of models, outperforming traditional manual methods.

articleTitle: Eco-Friendly Energy Storage Systems Based Demand Side Management for Rural Microgrid by Dandelion Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Energy storage systems play an essential role in ensuring a consistent power supply for microgrids in rural areas without access to the main grid. These systems also facilitate the efficient utilization of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind by storing excess energy for subsequent use. Selecting the most suitable type and capacity of batteries is of paramount importance for sustainable energy storage in rural microgrids. Lead-acid batteries are commonly utilized due to their relatively low cost and high discharge capacity. In contrast, lithium-ion batteries offer several advantages, including reduced environmental impact, lighter and more compact designs, and faster charge and discharge capabilities. This study employs the Dandelion Optimization Algorithm to compare the costs and environmental impacts of lead-acid and lithium-ion batteries, ultimately determining the optimal battery selection. The study also aims to identify the optimal battery capacity for balancing solar and wind power generation and demand power in microgrids. Energy storage systems facilitate efficient demand management functions and can promote the adoption of off-grid microgrids in rural areas. The results of this research can inform future studies in the field of metaheuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Long-Term Trends and Disruption in Medium Voltage Power Electronics: Identifying Future Power Electronics Technologies of High Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Medium voltage converters are a key component of renewable energy systems like photovoltaic and wind, of large-scale energy storage systems like batteries or hydrogen, and of applications like electric vehicle charging, datacenters, large medium voltage drives, hydrogen production and “green steel”. All these high-power applications went into exponential growth in the last decade and will keep growing during the next decades driven by the so-called “electrification”, the trend to replace fossil fuels by electricity based on renewable energy. The drivers of these trends and the role of power electronics are discussed, especially also the Solid-State Transformer (SST).

articleTitle: Transmission Expansion Planning with Photovoltaic Generation Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This document addresses the critical aspects of Transmission Expansion Planning (TEP) within electrical systems, emphasizing the need for reliable, efficient, and sustainable power supply. The study highlights the importance of optimizing transmission infrastructure to meet specific technical, economic and environmental parameters. The paper discusses various mathematical modeling approaches used in TEP, including linearized models such as DC charge flow and hybrid models. The inclusion of renewable energy sources in a linear hybrid model is examined as it introduces complexities that traditional models may not adequately address. The methodology used in this work focuses on the modification of a disjunctive linear model, adapting it to consider photovoltaic generation among its restrictions. Likewise, the input parameters of this renewable generation were obtained through an unsupervised K-means learning algorithm. The carried-out analysis, based on segmentation into irradiance and temperature clusters, highlights the importance of integrating specific climate data into planning models to adequately capture the differences between winter and summer scenarios.

articleTitle: Combined Machine Learning and Differential Evolution for Optimal Design of Electric Aircraft Propulsion Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Electric aircraft propulsion requires highly efficient and power-dense fault-tolerant electric motors optimized for specific flight profile operation. State-of-the-art design of electric motors involves substantial computational resources and combines electromagnetic finite element analysis (FEA) and optimization techniques. This paper proposes a new approach using a physics-based machine learning (ML) multi-input univariate meta-model trained on FEA and differential evolution (DE) optimization results to predict electromagnetic torque output. Hundreds of individual designs, generated through multiple generations of a DE algorithm, are analyzed by 3D FEA to create a database, which is then employed for the training and satisfactory validation of the ML model. The coreless axial flux permanent magnet (CAFPM) machine topology considered for an example study typically necessitates intensive 3D FEA simulation due to its specific geometry, although it does not experience the non-linear saturation associated with ferromagnetic core materials. The hybrid ML-DE model is satisfactorily validated with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> value of 0.97 and normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) of less than 0.05. The relative merits of the newly proposed combined ML-DE optimization are discussed, especially in terms of low error and the potential for overall computational time minimization.

articleTitle: RoCoF Threshold-Based Gain Scheduling for FFR Implementation in High Renewable Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The increasing integration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) in power systems reduces system inertia, leading to rapid Rates of Change of Frequency (RoCof) and posing challenges for frequency regulation. This study introduces a gain scheduling strategy for Fast Frequency Response (FFR) that leverages RoCoF thresholds to maintain frequency above predefined levels with minimal control gains. The method employs a RoCoF controller to regulate FFR, effectively reducing RoCoF in the power system. By adopting an analytical approach, this strategy calculates the frequency nadir directly from real-time measurements of frequency and RoCoF, eliminating the traditional need for power loss measurements and precise event timing. The critical control gain, determined based on triggering conditions, remains constant throughout the disturbance, ensuring a consistent response. Extensively validated across diverse system conditions, our methodology effectively estimates frequency dynamics and adjusts control gains accordingly, thus enhancing operational efficiency and ensuring robust frequency regulation in scenarios with varying system inertia and contingencies.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Charging Systems in Industrial DC Microgrids - Outlook and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Becoming climate neutral requires a series of measures to reduce carbon footprint, and the more efficient and cleaner energy consumption is a major one. A shift to renewable energy sources is needed, which requires increased flexibility between energy consumption and generation. For this purpose, direct current micro grids (DC MGs) can be particularly valuable, as they offer an energy-efficient integration of sustainable energy sources like photovoltaic systems, enabling improved energy flexibility. Additionally, DC MGs also offer a further boost to energy efficiency by improving grid performance and minimizing voltage converter losses. An additional enhancement in energy flexibility and efficiency could be achieved by employing bidirectional charging in electric vehicles (EV s) to serve as temporary energy storage systems in combination with microgrids. Due to the early stages in this field, further study of their interaction is critical. Thus, this work addresses how modeling bidirectional charging systems can impact the investigation of this topic and provides an overview of key technical definitions and technologies related to EV s that are fundamental for the modeling process and future work. This paper proposes two modeling approaches of a bidirectional electrical vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) to be connected to a DC MG model. Developing those models contributes to understanding the integration of DC MGs and EV s with bidirectional charging, designing appropriate control techniques, and analyzing potential stability issues resulting from their interaction.

articleTitle: Transformerless Ultra-High Gain Buck-Boost DC-DC Converter with Single-Switch of Reduced Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This paper introduces a new DC-DC power converter topology capable of both step-up and step-down voltage conversion, with an exceptionally high voltage gain ratio. Besides the high extension of the voltage gain range, the converter is also characterized by the use of a single switch. Moreover, the stress imposed on the switch's voltage is minimized, enabling the utilization of low-voltage, low RDS-ON MOSFETs. Consequently, this modification leads to reduced costs and losses associated with switch conduction and turn ON. Another aspect concerning the proposed converter is that the input current exhibits a continuous behavior, which can be significant for various applications. The paper provides insights into the operational performance, steady-state behavior, and mathematical underpinnings of the proposed dc-dc converter. Comparative evaluation of the static voltage gain of the proposed converter and other topologies with comparable characteristics will also be shown. Verification of the presented converter's key features are conducted through both simulation and experimental assessments using a 440-W laboratory prototype. Through these analyses, the efficacy and viability of the modified coupled-inductor SEPIC converter with enhanced voltage gain capability are confirmed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Floating Wind Turbine Reliability with Shared Damping Mooring
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The reliability of mooring systems has long been a challenge for expanding floating wind turbines into deeper waters. The performance of the mooring system directly determines the service life and survival capability of floating wind turbines. To address this issue, our team has developed a shared damping mooring system. This system reduces the fatigue impact from operating sea conditions and effectively minimizes dragging damage at the fairlead. In this study, two widely used dampers were selected to construct the shared damping mooring system, and their effectiveness in enhancing the reliability of semi-submersible wind turbines was explored. Compared to traditional mooring methods, it was found that this shared damping approach can effectively increase the service life of mooring lines, reduce the local stress and tension levels at the fairlead, and improve the stability of semi-submersible wind turbines. Simulation results indicate that the shared damping mooring system can effectively alleviate fatigue damage, and the shaped memory alloy damper provides significant damping force under low-frequency environmental loads. This characteristic significantly enhances the floating foundation's stability and extends the mooring system's lifetime.

articleTitle: Dynamic Voltage Operating Strategy of Offshore Wind Farm with Flexible Transmission Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: A variable voltage control strategy is proposed for wind farm sending by flexible transmission techniques, in which the voltage of the point of common coupling (PCC) of the wind farm varies dynamically with the overall wind speed of wind turbine clusters. This is achieved by dynamically adjusting the voltage of the AC port of the sending-end station of flexible DC transmission or the low-frequency side AC port of the flexible low-frequency transmission, and cooperating with the dynamic dc-bus voltage control of the back-to-back converter of the wind energy conversion system (WECS). The proposed control is beneficial to reduce the switching loss of the WECS converter and reduce the peak value of the fault transient current. Besides, by replacing the dc-bus capacitor of WECS with supercapacitor, the proposed control strategy can realize a wide range change of dc-bus voltage, so as to provide frequency support for power grid without a DC-DC converter. The electromagnetic transient simulation verifies the feasibility and superiority of the proposed control strategies.

articleTitle: Benchmarking of Existing and New Technologies in Hydrogen Value Chain and Related Business Models
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: The paper provides an analysis on the hydrogen landscape aiming to identify the gaps and what needs be done to reach the different hydrogen targets by 2030. After an overview of the EU targets, the discussion focuses on the validation of the existing and new technologies in the hydrogen value chain and business models that are adopted in large-size projects. This will be done considering one of the largest hydrogen facilities in Europe, Holland Hydrogen I and several other hydrogen initiatives in Europe. The objective of this analysis is to critically assess these initiatives, considering from small-size projects to large-size projects, with a view to identifying opportunities for enhancement and innovation, and to understand whether it is realistic or not to meet these targets with the current available technologies and regional policy and legislation.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Forecasting Using Ensemble Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Integrating renewable energy resources with new technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) is critical for balancing energy supply and demand. The predictability of variable energy sources, such as solar Energy, plays a vital role in maintaining the stability and efficiency of electrical grids. In this context, this study examines the use of various algorithms in AI applications within renewable energy systems. A comprehensive literature analysis reveals the advantages and challenges of popular AI techniques such as Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Machines, and Decision Trees in energy prediction and optimization. This study mainly focuses on the effectiveness of boosting algorithms such as XGBoost, CatBoost, AdaBoost, LightGBM algorithms and Ensemble learning in estimating alternating current (AC). The results have shown that the Ensemble model achieved the highest R2 value (0.942) and the lowest error metrics MAE (0.040) to demonstrate its superior ability to explain variance in data and make precise predictions. This paper critically evaluates existing methods and proposes an innovative approach to AC prediction in solar power systems using advanced machine-learning techniques.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Forced-Air Cooling System for a Compact Medium Voltage Solar Photovoltaic Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: This study describes designing and optimizing a forced-air cooling system for a compact, medium-voltage solar PV inverter. As solar energy adoption increases, enhancing inverter performance is crucial for maximizing the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. Power loss, ambient temperature, and inlet air velocity are considered while designing the inverter thermal profile. Airflow modeling optimizes inverter enclosure heat and temperature dispersion using CFD models. The research evaluates heat sink, fan, and cooling component materials to increase heat transfer. The compact medium-voltage inverter's forced air-cooling technology is carefully integrated to retain its form and footprint. This study also considers the broader impact of effective thermal management on the overall efficiency and longevity of renewable energy grids, highlighting the potential to improve these systems' performance significantly. Finally, our study creates lightweight, energy-efficient, resilient forced-air cooling systems for medium-voltage solar PV inverters. The findings could guide engineers and researchers in developing and optimizing thermal management solutions for a wide range of renewable energy power electronics systems, contributing to the ongoing advancement of sustainable energy technologies.

articleTitle: The Role and Benefits of Residential Photovoltaic Prosumers on Rooftops and Contribution Towards the Energy Transition: Galapagos Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 13th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: For this research work, the impact of the implementation of photovoltaic systems on the roofs of buildings is analyzed. The Elecgalapagos building is taken into consideration as a case study, the meteorological conditions and the performance that the photovoltaic system achieves when implemented are analyzed. These energy generation systems are ideal in the Galapagos Islands, knowing that it is difficult to expand to surrounding areas due to regulations that limit horizontal locations. However, by having areas that are free such as roofs, it is possible to take advantage of them to generate clean energy for the buildings themselves or in turn inject into the public electricity grid. These initiatives are a direct contribution to achieving the energy transition with a higher percentage of renewable energy and fewer fossil fuels. As a result, it has been identified that it is possible to generate at least 4kW for at least 4 hours in the worst conditions and on sunny days it has been identified that it is possible to generate 7.7 kW for at least 4 continuous hours. In terms of energy, in the most favorable case (sunny day) 52.5kWh per day are achieved and in the most unfavorable case (Tick fog day) 29.4kWh are recorded. In general terms, it is possible to guarantee an energy supply for around 30% of the building, there is a bidirectional intelligent metering system, with connection to the public electrical network.
